processes.title: Acquire to dispose
processes.description: The acquire to dispose process is a critical business process that involves managing the lifecycle of both owned and leased assets from acquisition to disposal. This process includes the acquisition, deployment, maintenance, and eventual disposal of assets such as equipment, vehicles, and property. Dynamics 365 can be used to support this process by providing a centralized platform for managing asset data, tracking asset usage and maintenance history, and streamlining the asset disposal process. We have defined the acquire to dispose process here to also include financial management or accounting processes of fixed assets and asset leases. This includes the planning, budgeting, and management process for owned and leased assets. By implementing Dynamics 365 to support the acquire to dispose process, organizations can improve asset visibility, increase operational efficiency, and reduce costs associated with asset management.

processes.title: Analyze the asset lease register in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: Multiple report can be used to track the financial operations for leased assets. The Asset movement report serves as a roll forward report for the right-of-use asset balances for each lease. This report lets you view the asset transactions of a lease during a specified period. The Differences report shows the differences between information loaded into the Lease import framework and the information that's currently in the system. This lets you compare what was adjusted, updated, or added through the Lease import framework. The values in the report will vary based on the selected lease. The report will only show those fields that differ from what is currently in the system and what is in the staging tables. The old value is what is either currently in the system or what was previously in the system, depending on whether the import process has run. The new value shows the value that's in the staging table that will replace the old value. The Lease modification report shows all leases that have been modified within a specified date range. The report also shows the user who adjusted the lease, and the total amount of liability adjusted. The Lease movement report serves as a roll forward report for the lease liability balances for each lease. This report allows the user to view the liability transactions of a lease during a specified period. The Lease transactions inquiry shows all the journal entries that have been generated by Asset leasing. Each journal entry is linked with the book ID it was originated from. This lets you easily associate the journal entry with corresponding lease. The Lease transactions inquiry functions in a manner that's similar to the Voucher transactions page in General ledger.

processes.title: Dispose of assets
processes.description: In the rapidly evolving business environment of today, for any organization, the process of retiring and disposing of assets holds a pivotal role in the lifecycle management of resources within that organization. The retire and dispose of assets business process involves retiring and disposing of fixed assets that are no longer needed. It also covers when assets must be replaced by assessing the lifecycle stage, usability, and alignment of assets with the organizational goals. As assets mature, outgrow their usefulness, or no longer fit the evolving demands of the business, or as technology evolves, the strategic choice to retire and dispose of assets is crucial. Making informed decisions about their retirement and disposal ensures that the organization maintains operational efficiency, optimizes resource allocation, and adheres to legal and environmental responsibilities. When a fixed asset is no longer needed, it can either be scrapped or sold. If the asset still has value, it's likely to be set to be sold. When a fixed asset is sold with profit, the profit is recognized in the year of the sale, and then it's posted to the profit and loss part of the chart of accounts.

processes.title: Perform asset maintenance
processes.description: In many organizations, the terms maintenance and repair are used interchangeably. However, they might refer to different areas in the asset management process. Maintenance includes activities that can be scheduled and/or performed at a specific time to help prevent assets from breaking down and increase their life. Repairs help restore the functionality of assets when they are damaged or inoperable from a process standpoint. There are three main types of maintenance tasks: Reactive: Reactive maintenance involves repairing an asset that has broken down or experienced a failure, typically one that isn't critical for business. If the maintenance strategy isn't effectively planned for the appropriate assets, reactive maintenance can lead to unexpected downtime and higher costs. Preventive: Preventive maintenance involves performing periodic planned tasks to review the state of an asset and apply corrective procedures to help prevent it from failing. These tasks can help extend the life of the asset and can also help the organization avoid unplanned repair and restoration costs. Predictive: Predictive maintenance involves using signals from machines and equipment on the production floor to sense deviations or irregularities in day-to-day operations. By using sensor intelligence mechanisms and/or smart technology, the organization can predict failures or outages before they occur. This proactive approach helps ensure that maintenance can be performed in a timely manner to mitigate potential delays. If parts are beyond repair, it might be better to replace the asset than repair it. In this way, the daily operations continue to run at maximum efficiency. Most tangible assets, such as vehicles, machines, and production equipment, go through a maintenance and repair journey. However, intangible assets, such as software, brands, intellectual property (IP), patents, and so on, might also require maintenance and repair. Investment in intangible assets is expensed instead of capitalized. The owner of an asset can lease it to another party for money or another factor. Maintenance and repair of leased assets might depend on the agreement between the lessor and the lessee, based on whether the lease is a capital lease or an operating lease.

processes.title: Manage active assets
processes.description: Organization may have certain assets that are large items in the balance sheet. Based on the location and area where the assets are installed or deployed, there may be extra tax component associated with the asset. These assets may have insurance associated with them as well. In some cases, assets may be leased out to a lessee. Hence, it becomes important for companies to optimally manage and report asset information. Fixed assets are reported on the balance sheet. Activities related to investments are captured in a company's cash flow statement. The acquisition or disposal of an asset is also recorded in the cash flow statement. When you use a general ledger together with fixed assets, you can view the current value of all fixed assets. The way in which fixed assets are handled must correspond to both international accounting standards and the accounting legislation in each country/region. Companies start off by evaluating the need for assets and budget/plan it up in advance. The process then involves either acquiring an asset or leasing an asset depending on multiple parameters. In case the asset is acquired, it goes through a high-level process that could be a mix of more asset related information adjustment, depreciation, disposal. Companies can define rules to record acquisition method, depreciation and disposal, write-ups and write-downs. The management of assets and its finance is an ongoing operational process for an organization. It becomes more important when audits are executed to review financial information. In Dynamics 365, you find multiple reports to assess fixed asset information. One such example is the Fixed assets roll forward report (Finance).

processes.title: Extend an asset lease in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: For organizations that adhere to ASC 842 or IFRS 16, a lease is remeasured to reflect a change in the present value of the future minimum lease payments (PVFMLP). If the PVFMLP increases, the journal entry that is created will be a debit to the right-of-use (ROU) asset account and a credit to the lease liability account for the difference between the new PVFMLP and the previous PVFMLP. If the PVFMLP decreases, the journal entry will be a debit to the lease liability account and a credit to the ROU asset account for the difference. If the adjustment decreases the ROU asset past 0 (zero), the remainder is credited to the gain on lease modification posting account that is specified on the Lease posting accounts page. The system accounts for these transactions and other adjustment entries, such as classification changes, initial direct costs, lease incentives, prepayments, and dismantling costs that arise from lease modifications.

processes.title: Modify asset lease terms in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: Asset leasing allows leases to be adjusted if the lease terms are modified, the lease is extended, or if there are additional circumstances under which a lease requires an adjustment. When a lease is linked to fixed asset, the right-of-use adjustment is posted using the ID that's assigned in Fixed assets.

processes.title: Classify assets

This helps organizations manage, track, and report on their assets more effectively. Common asset classifications include: Tangible vs. Intangible (e.g., machinery vs. patents) Current vs. Non-current (e.g., inventory vs. buildings) IT assets, Facilities, Vehicles, etc. Depreciation categories for accounting purposes How Dynamics 365 Supports Asset Classification Microsoft Dynamics 365, particularly in modules like Dynamics 365 Finance and Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, provides robust tools for asset classification: Asset Types and Categories: You can define asset types (e.g., equipment, vehicles) and assign them to categories. Categories can include depreciation profiles, useful life, and accounting rules. Fixed Asset Management: Allows classification by asset group, location, department, and responsible employee. Supports tagging assets with custom attributes for more granular classification. Hierarchical Structures: Assets can be grouped into parent-child relationships (e.g., a vehicle fleet with individual cars). Lifecycle Tracking: Tracks assets from acquisition to disposal, with classification updates at each stage. Reporting and Analytics: Enables filtering and reporting based on asset classifications for audits, budgeting, and compliance.

processes.title: Case to resolution
processes.description: The case to resolution process is a critical business process that enables organizations to effectively manage customer or employee inquiries, complaints, and issues. The process involves various steps, such as engaging with customers, logging the case, assigning it to the appropriate team or individual, investigating and resolving the issue, and closing the case. However, managing this process can be challenging, particularly as organizations grow in size and complexity, which is where technology solutions like Dynamics 365 come in. Microsoft Business Applications including Dynamics 365, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft 365 are a powerful platform that can support the case to resolution process by automating and streamlining many of its key steps. For example, Dynamics 365 Customer Service can enable organizations to engage in conversations with customers through various channels, including email, phone, chat and social media, identify and authenticate customers, answer customer questions, run transactions on behalf of customers, log cases and automatically assign cases to the appropriate team or individual based on predefined rules. It can also provide real-time visibility into case status and progress, enabling managers and teams to track performance, identify bottlenecks, and optimize the process for greater efficiency and effectiveness. Dynamics 365 Human Resources has functionality to help employees and managers communicate effectively through cases to manage common requests and issues. Likewise, Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management includes cases management tools to help with the process of managing issues with customers and vendors for example, including complex issues like a product recall. Dynamics 365 Finance and Supply Chain Management also include tools to help with the effective management of returns, exchanges, credits, price matching, and more. However, it's important to note that Dynamics 365 is just one component of a broader case to resolution process. The process involves multiple stakeholders, such as customers, employees, managers, and support teams, who may have different roles, responsibilities, and workflows. Moreover, the process may differ depending on the type of case, the industry, or the organization's specific requirements. Steps to Analyze Case Patterns in D365 Customer Service Analyzing case patterns in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service helps identify recurring issues, optimize resource allocation, and improve service efficiency. This guide outlines how to use Customer Service Historical Analytics to uncover case trends and patterns. 1. Accessing Case Analytics in D365 Step 1: Open Customer Service Historical Analytics Navigate to Customer Service Workspace or Customer Service Hub . Click Customer Service Historical Analytics from the left-hand navigation panel. Open the Case Insights Dashboard . 2. Identifying Case Trends & Recurring Issues Step 2: Review Case Volume Trends Metrics to Analyze: Total Cases Created Over Time – Identify seasonal or recurring spikes. Case Volume by Type – Determine which types of issues occur most often. Case Volume by Channel – Compare issues reported via email, chat, phone, or self-service portal . Top Customers by Case Count – Identify customers submitting frequent cases. Best Practice: Apply date range filters (weekly, monthly, quarterly) to spot long-term trends. Step 3: Analyze Case Resolution & Escalations Key Metrics: Average Resolution Time – Identify case types taking longer to resolve. Escalation Rate by Case Type – Find case categories that frequently require higher-level intervention. Case Reopen Rate – Detect cases that were closed but needed follow-up. Best Practice: If certain case types have high escalation or reopen rates , they may require process improvements or updated Knowledge Articles . 3. Analyzing Agent & Team Case Handling Patterns Step 4: Evaluate Agent & Team Performance In Customer Service Historical Analytics , open the Agent Insights dashboard. Filter by Agent Name or Team . Analyze the following KPIs: Average Case Handling Time Per Agent – Identify efficiency gaps. Number of Cases Assigned vs. Resolved – Compare workload vs. output. Escalation Rate Per Agent – Find agents frequently escalating cases. Best Practice: Compare case resolution trends across different teams or shifts to optimize staffing. 4. Detecting SLA Violations & Resolution Delays Step 5: Identify SLA Compliance Trends Key Metrics: Total SLA Breaches – Cases exceeding response or resolution deadlines. Cases Nearing SLA Deadline – Identify cases at risk of violating SLAs. Case Resolution Time vs. SLA Goal – Compare actual vs. expected resolution performance. Best Practice: Use Power Automate to notify managers when cases are approaching SLA limits. 5. Leveraging Customer Feedback for Pattern Analysis Step 6: Review Customer Satisfaction (CSAT) Scores Navigate to the CSAT (Customer Satisfaction) Dashboard . Analyze feedback on resolved cases. Identify recurring themes in low-rated cases (e.g., long wait times, incomplete resolutions). Best Practice: If certain case types consistently get low ratings, investigate process bottlenecks or training needs . 6. Best Practices for Case Pattern Analysis Monitor trends weekly/monthly to detect emerging issues early. Use AI-powered insights (Copilot) to recommend case resolutions. processes.title: Review call center performance
processes.description: As a Call Center Manager, I want to analyze case type trends, individual agent performance, and SLA violations, So that I can optimize service efficiency and reduce escalations. Steps to Review Call Center Performance by Case Type, Analyze Individual Performance, and Analyze SLA Violations in D365 Customer Service Tracking call center performance, individual agent performance, and SLA (Service Level Agreement) compliance ensures efficient customer service operations. This guide outlines how to review and analyze these metrics using Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service Historical Analytics . 1. Reviewing Call Center Performance by Case Type Step 1: Access Customer Service Historical Analytics Navigate to Customer Service Workspace or Customer Service Hub . Click on Customer Service Historical Analytics from the left-hand navigation panel. Open the Case Insights Dashboard . Step 2: Filter Cases by Type Locate the Case Type field in the analytics dashboard. Use filters to categorize cases by type (e.g., Technical Issue, Billing, Warranty, Product Inquiry ). Apply date filters to analyze performance over a specific period. Step 3: Analyze Case Trends Key Metrics to Review: Total number of cases per type (Identify the most common issues). Average resolution time by case type (Compare how quickly different case types are resolved). First Contact Resolution (FCR) rate (How often cases are resolved in the first interaction). Escalation rates by case type (Which types require managerial intervention). 2. Analyzing Individual Agent Performance Step 1: Open Agent Performance Dashboard In Customer Service Historical Analytics , go to Agent Insights . Select the Agent Performance dashboard. Step 2: Review Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Total Cases Handled: Number of cases an agent has worked on. Average Handling Time (AHT): The time taken to resolve cases. Resolution Rate: Percentage of cases resolved by the agent. Customer Satisfaction Score (CSAT): Based on customer feedback and surveys. Escalation Rate: Percentage of cases escalated to supervisors. Step 3: Compare Agent Performance Filter by agent name to compare performance. Identify top-performing agents vs. those needing training. Check if agents handle certain case types more efficiently . Best Practice: Use Power Automate to send automated alerts if an agent’s performance drops below a set threshold. 3. Analyzing SLA Violations Step 1: Access SLA Compliance Dashboard In Customer Service Historical Analytics , click on SLA Insights . Open the SLA Compliance dashboard. Step 2: Identify SLA Breaches Key Metrics to Analyze: Total SLA violations (Number of missed SLAs). Cases with SLA breaches (Filter cases that exceeded response/resolution time). Agents with the highest SLA violations (Identify recurring issues). SLA compliance percentage (Measure overall adherence). Step 3: Drill Down into SLA Violations Filter by Case Type to see which case types frequently exceed SLA limits. Filter by Agent/Team to identify who is missing SLAs. Review SLA breach reasons (e.g., long wait times, agent workload). Best Practice: Automate SLA alerts in Power Automate to notify managers when an SLA is about to breach. 4. Best Practices for Call Center Performance Management Use AI-powered insights (Copilot for Customer Service) for real-time analytics. Enable SLA breach notifications in Power Automate. Regularly review performance dashboards to address gaps proactively. Use Power BI for deeper analytics beyond built-in reports.

processes.title: Review case loads and rebalance case loads
processes.description: As a Customer Service Manager, I want to analyze and redistribute case loads across my team, So that no agent is overwhelmed and cases are resolved efficiently. Steps to Review and Rebalance Case Loads in D365 Customer Service Effectively reviewing and rebalancing case loads ensures that agents are not overwhelmed and that cases are resolved efficiently. This guide outlines how to analyze case distribution and redistribute cases using Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service Historical Analytics . 1. Reviewing Case Loads in D365 Customer Service Step 1: Access Customer Service Historical Analytics Navigate to Customer Service Workspace or Customer Service Hub . Click on Customer Service Historical Analytics from the left-hand navigation panel. Open the Agent Insights Dashboard or Case Insights Dashboard . Step 2: Review Current Case Load Distribution Key Metrics to Analyze: Total Cases Assigned Per Agent : Identify overloaded agents. Active vs. Resolved Cases : Determine backlog levels. Case Aging Report : Find cases that have been open too long. Escalation Rate Per Agent : Identify performance gaps. SLA Status by Agent : Check if any agents are at risk of breaching SLAs. Step 3: Identify Imbalances in Case Loads Compare case volumes across different agents and teams. Look for agents with a significantly higher number of open cases . Identify unassigned or overdue cases that require reassignment. 2. Rebalancing Case Loads in D365 Customer Service Step 1: Reassign Cases Manually Navigate to Customer Service Workspace and open Cases . Use filters to identify: Overloaded agents. Cases that need reassignment based on priority. Unassigned cases that need a responsible owner. Select cases that need reassignment. Click Assign , then select the appropriate agent or team. Click Save to confirm the reassignment. Best Practice: Leave an internal Case Note explaining why the case was reassigned. Step 2: Automate Case Balancing with Queues & Routing Rules Go to Service Management > Queues . Review the existing queues and ensure cases are evenly distributed. Navigate to Service Management > Routing Rules . Set up Auto-Assignment Rules based on: Agent workload. Case priority. Case type and required expertise. Best Practice: Use Omnichannel for Customer Service with Workstreams for automatic case distribution. Step 3: Set Up Real-Time Alerts for Case Load Monitoring Use Power Automate to notify managers when: An agent has more than a predefined number of active cases. A case has been unassigned for too long. An agent is consistently missing SLAs. 3. Best Practices for Case Load Balancing Regularly review workload distribution to avoid agent burnout. Use AI-based routing in Omnichannel for Customer Service for smarter case assignments. Enable workload-based case reassignment in Power Automate. Monitor SLA trends to prevent bottlenecks in case resolution.

processes.title: Assign a case
processes.description: As a Customer Support Manager , I want to assign cases to the appropriate team, individual, or queue so that cases are handled by the right people and resolved efficiently. Process for Assigning a Case to a Team, Individual, or Queue in D365 Customer Service Assigning cases correctly in D365 Customer Service ensures that the right team, individual, or queue handles the case efficiently, improving response times and resolution rates. 1. Steps to Assign a Case to a Team, Individual, or Queue Step 1: Open the Case Record Navigate to Customer Service Workspace . In the left navigation, go to Cases . Open the case that needs to be assigned. Step 2: Choose Assignment Method A. Assign to an Individual Click on the Assign button in the top action bar. In the Assign To window, select User . Search for and select the User to assign the case to. Click Assign . The case is now owned by the selected individual. B. Assign to a Team Click Assign . In the Assign To window, select Team . Search for and select the Team . Click Assign . The case is now owned by the selected team, and any team member can work on it. C. Assign to a Queue (For Automatic or Shared Work Handling) Open the Case Record . Locate the Queue field. Click Change Queue and select the appropriate queue. Click Save & Close . ✅ The case is now assigned to a queue, and available agents can pick it up. Step 3: Automate Assignment Using Routing Rules (Optional) If cases should be assigned automatically , configure Routing Rules : Navigate to Customer Service Admin Center . Go to Work Distribution & Routing → Routing Rule Sets . Define rules based on case priority, type, or customer . Assign cases directly to a queue, team, or user . Cases are now automatically routed based on predefined rules.

processes.title: Create a case from a channel
processes.description: As a Customer Support Manager , I want to ensure that cases are automatically created from various customer channels so that issues are tracked efficiently and resolved promptly. Steps to Create a Case from Different Channels in D365 Customer Service Cases can be created manually by agents or automatically when customer interactions come from various channels like chat, phone calls, portal requests, emails, and product returns . Steps to Create a Case from Different Channels A. Create a Case from a Chat (Omnichannel for Customer Service) Enable Omnichannel for Customer Service in Customer Service Admin Center . Customer starts a chat session via Live Chat, SMS, or WhatsApp . Agent receives the chat in the Omnichannel Agent Dashboard . Click Create Case directly from the chat window. The system auto-fills: Customer Name (if authenticated). Case Origin = Chat. Conversation Details from the chat. Agent enters additional details and clicks Save & Close . The case is now linked to the chat conversation. B. Create a Case from a Live Phone Call in Omnichannel Open Omnichannel for Customer Service . Navigate to the Omnichannel Agent Dashboard . When a phone call request arrives, click Accept . The call session will open in the conversation panel . Click More Actions (⋮) → Create Case . A new Case Form will open with the following auto-filled details: Customer Name Case Origin = Phone Call Call Transcript or Notes (if enabled) Enter additional details: Case Title (brief issue summary). Case Type (Inquiry, Complaint, Service Request, etc.). Priority (Low, Normal, High, Critical). Detailed Description of the issue. Assign the case to a specific agent, team, or queue (or let Routing Rules assign it automatically). Click Save & Close to link the case to the phone call session. The phone call is logged, and the case is linked for further resolution. C. Create a Case from a Portal Request Customer submits a request via the Customer Self-Service Portal . The system automatically creates a case when the request is submitted. The Case Record is auto-populated with: Customer Name & Contact Info . Case Title & Description (from the form submission). Case Origin = Portal. Case routing rules assign the case to a team or queue . Customer receives an automated email confirmation . The case is now in the system and ready for an agent to process. D. Create a Case from an Email Enable Email-to-Case Automation in Customer Service Admin Center . Customer sends an email to a designated support email address . The system automatically: Creates a Case Record . Links the email conversation to the case. Sets Case Origin = Email. The case is placed in the Email Queue , ready for assignment. Agents can now respond directly from the case record.

Steps to Manually Create a Case Step 1: Open Customer Service Workspace Navigate to Customer Service Workspace in Dynamics 365. Click on Cases from the left navigation panel. Click Save & Close or Save & Continue . The customer complaint case is logged and ready for resolution. B. Example based on Product Return Case Case Type: Product Return Order Number: Link the case to the corresponding order. Reason for Return: Select from predefined options (Defective, Wrong Item, Not Needed). Return Process: Attach return documents (receipts, images of the product). Supporting Evidence: Attach relevant documents (invoice copy, payment receipt, customer email). Resolution Process: Specify the next steps (review invoice, credit/refund processing). Assign case to Billing/Accounts Team . Click Save & Close . The disputed invoice case is logged and ready for financial review. processes.title: Send notification to customer
processes.description: As a Customer Service Representative (CSR), I want to automatically notify customers when a new case is created, updated, or resolved, So that I can ensure timely communication, reduce manual effort, and improve customer satisfaction. Process for Sending Customer Notifications in D365 CE for Case Management This document outlines the process and detailed steps for automatically sending notifications to customers in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Engagement (D365 CE) when a new case is created, updated, or resolved. 1. Process Overview Notification Scenarios New Case Acknowledgment : When a new case is created, the customer should receive a confirmation email with case details. Case Update Notification : When a case is updated (status change, assigned agent change, or important notes added), the customer should be informed. Case Resolution Notification : When a case is resolved or closed, the customer should receive a resolution summary. Technology Used Power Automate : Automates email notifications triggered by case events. D365 Email Templates : Predefined templates ensure consistent messaging. Dataverse Triggers : Listens for case events in the system. SMS Gateway (Optional) : For SMS notifications if required. 2. Process Workflow Step 1: Trigger Setup (Define Event) Define the trigger event for each type of notification: New Case Acknowledgment → Triggered when a new case is created. Case Update Notification → Triggered when a case status, owner, or priority is updated. Case Resolution Notification → Triggered when a case is marked as "Resolved" or "Closed." Step 2: Fetch Customer Details Retrieve the customer's email or preferred notification channel from the Case record. Get related Account or Contact information . Step 3: Select Notification Template Use Email Templates in D365 CE for consistent messaging. Personalize the template with: Case Number Case Title Current Status Assigned Agent Resolution Summary (for closed cases) Case Portal Link (if applicable) Step 4: Send Notification via Power Automate New Case Acknowledgment : Trigger: When a new case is created. Action: Send an email to the customer with the case number and SLA details. Case Update Notification : Trigger: When an important field changes (status, priority, owner, or a significant note is added). Action: Send an update email or SMS with the latest case details. Case Resolution Notification : Trigger: When a case status is changed to "Resolved" or "Closed." Action: Send a resolution summary to the customer with next steps or feedback request. Step 5: Log Notification in Case Timeline Create a Case Timeline entry in D365 CE for audit purposes. Store notification details, including: Timestamp Email content Customer response (if applicable) 3. Detailed Steps in Power Automate Below are the detailed steps for implementing this using Power Automate . A. Flow for New Case Acknowledgment Trigger : When a new Case is created in D365 CE (Dataverse trigger). Action : Retrieve related Contact/Account details. PROCESS OVERVIEW NOTIFICATION SCENARIOS * New Case Acknowledgment: When a new case is created, the customer should receive a confirmation email with case details. * Case Update Notification: When a case is updated (status change, assigned agent change, or important notes added), the customer should be informed. * Case Resolution Notification: When a case is resolved or closed, the customer should receive a resolution summary. TECHNOLOGY USED * Power Automate: Automates email notifications triggered by case events. * Dynamics 365 Email Templates: Predefined templates ensure consistent messaging. * Dataverse Triggers: Listens for case events in the system. * SMS Gateway (Optional): For SMS notifications if required. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 2. PROCESS WORKFLOW STEP 1: TRIGGER SETUP (DEFINE EVENT) Define the trigger event for each type of notification: * New Case Acknowledgment → Triggered when a new case is created. * Case Update Notification → Triggered when a case status, owner, or priority is updated. * Case Resolution Notification → Triggered when a case is marked as "Resolved" or "Closed." STEP 2: FETCH CUSTOMER DETAILS * Retrieve the customer's email or preferred notification channel from the Case record. * Get related Account or Contact information. STEP 3: SELECT NOTIFICATION TEMPLATE * Use Email Templates in Dynamics 365 CE for consistent messaging. * Personalize the template with: * Case Number * Case Title * Current Status * Assigned Agent * Resolution Summary (for closed cases) * Case Portal Link (if applicable) STEP 4: SEND NOTIFICATION VIA POWER AUTOMATE 1. New Case Acknowledgment: * Trigger: When a new case is created. * Action: Send an email to the customer with the case number and SLA details. 2. Case Update Notification: * Trigger: When an important field changes (status, priority, owner, or a significant note is added). * Action: Send an update email or SMS with the latest case details. 3. Case Resolution Notification: * Trigger: When a case status is changed to "Resolved" or "Closed." * Action: Send a resolution summary to the customer with next steps or feedback request. processes.title: Define agent skill sets
processes.description: As a user / HR Manager, I need to understand the process of defining an agent skill set, including required skills, gaps, training plans, so that support analysts/agents are assigned to the proper skills to support the areas they are best suited. Defining Agent Skill Set in D365 Case Management is part of Omnichannel for Customer Service and Unified Routing . It plays a crucial role in intelligent case routing but is not a mandatory prerequisite for basic case creation. However, if you're implementing automated case routing and queue management , agent skill definitions should be configured. Where to Define Agent Skill Sets? Agent skills are primarily set up in the Customer Service Admin Center or Omnichannel for Customer Service under the Work Distribution and Routing settings. Steps to Define Agent Skill Set for Case Routing Enable Unified Routing (If Not Already Enabled) Go to Customer Service Admin Center > Work Distribution > Unified Routing . Enable Unified Routing to allow intelligent case assignments. Define Skills Navigate to Customer Service Admin Center > Agent Experiences > Skills . Click New Skill and define: Skill Name (e.g., "Warranty Claims Processing"). Skill Category (Optional for grouping). Skill Proficiency Levels (Optional: Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced). Assign Skills to Agents Go to Customer Service Admin Center > Agent Experiences > Agent Profiles . Select an Agent Profile or create a new one. Assign skills based on expertise. Configure Skill-Based Routing Rules Navigate to Work Distribution & Routing > Routing Rulesets . Define a new Routing Rule for cases based on attributes like: Case Type Case Subject Customer Priority Entitlement Assign the rule to a queue with agents who have the required skills. Assign Agents to Queues Go to Workstreams > Create a Workstream (or modify an existing one). Add Skill Matching Criteria to route cases based on agent skills. Assign Agents to queues based on their defined skills. Enable Auto-Assignment of Cases to Agents Ensure auto-assignment is enabled within Routing & Work Distribution . Cases will now be assigned to the best-matched agent based on skill proficiency. How It Works in Case Management? When a case is created, unified routing checks agent availability, assigned skills, and proficiency. The system intelligently routes the case to the best-qualified agent . If no skilled agent is available, fallback rules (such as routing to a general queue) apply. Where Does This Fit in the Case Creation Process? Agent skill set definition fits under Step 4 (Queues & Routing) in case management setup. While not mandatory for case creation, it is essential for intelligent case assignment . processes.title: Define queues and teams
processes.description: Title: As a Customer Service Manager, I want to understand how to define Teams and Queues within D365 Customer Service so that cases are routed efficiently to the correct team and queue. Defining Queues and Teams in D365 Customer Service Queues and Teams are essential components in D365 Customer Service for managing and routing cases efficiently. Queues help organize and distribute work items, while Teams group users together based on roles, expertise, or business functions. 1. Defining Queues in D365 Customer Service A Queue is a collection of work items (Cases, Activities, Emails, etc.) that can be assigned to users or teams for resolution. Steps to Create a Queue Go to the Power Platform Admin Center → Select your D365 Customer Service App . Navigate to Customer Service Hub → Service Management → Queues . Click New to create a new queue. Fill in the details: Name : E.g., "Warranty Claims Queue" Type : Public : Any user can work on queue items. Private : Only assigned users can access the queue. Incoming Email (if using email-to-case routing). Associated Team (Optional) : Links the queue to a team for better work distribution. Save and Close . Types of Queues Default Queue : Assigned automatically to each user and team. Custom Queues : Specific to business processes (e.g., "High Priority Cases"). Routing Queues : Used in Omnichannel for automated case routing. 2. Defining Teams in D365 Customer Service A Team is a group of users who share ownership of records and work collaboratively. Steps to Create a Team Go to Power Platform Admin Center → Advanced Settings . Navigate to Settings → Security → Teams . Click New and enter: Team Name : E.g., "Warranty Support Team" Business Unit : Assign to the correct unit. Team Type : Owner Team (Default) – Can own records. Access Team – Can only collaborate but not own records. Queue Association : (Optional) Assign a default queue for the team. Add Users to the Team. Save and Close .

processes.title: Determine business process flow
processes.description: As a Customer Service Manager , I want to implement a Business Process Flow (BPF) for case management so that agents follow a structured, step-by-step approach to resolving customer issues efficiently and consistently Steps to Define a Business Process Flow (BPF) in D365 Customer Service A Business Process Flow (BPF) in Dynamics 365 Customer Service guides users through a structured sequence of stages to ensure consistent case resolution. 1. Access the Business Process Flow Designer Navigate to Power Apps ( https://make.powerapps.com ). Select the Environment where you want to create the BPF. Go to Solutions (or create a new solution to store the BPF). Click New → Select Process . In the Create Process dialog: Process Name : e.g., "Case Resolution Process" Category : Business Process Flow Entity : Case Click Create . 2. Define Stages & Steps in the Business Process Flow A BPF consists of Stages (phases) and Steps (fields to be filled in each stage). Example Stages for Case Management: Identify Issue Step 1 : Enter Case Title (Required). Step 2 : Select Case Type (Problem, Request, Inquiry). Investigate Step 1 : Assign to an Agent or Queue . Step 2 : Capture Customer Notes or Attachments . Step 3 : Set Case Priority . Resolve Step 1 : Enter Resolution Details . Step 2 : Confirm Customer Satisfaction . Close Case Step 1 : Mark Case as Resolved or Escalated . Step 2 : Generate Closure Summary Report . 3. Configure Conditional Branching (If Needed) If Case Type = "High Priority" , route it to a Supervisor Review stage. If Case Resolution Time > 24 hours , escalate the case automatically. To configure branching: Click the Stage where you want a decision point. Click Add Condition . Define logic (e.g., "If Case Priority = High, move to Escalation Stage"). Apply conditions and save. 4. Set Required Fields & Permissions Mark important fields as Required to ensure data entry before moving to the next stage. Assign security roles to control who can modify the BPF. 5. Activate and Publish the BPF Click Validate to check for errors. Click Save and then Activate . Publish the BPF so users can see it in Case Records . Bonus: Tracking & Reporting on BPF Progress Use Dashboards to track how long cases stay in each stage. Create Power BI reports to analyze case resolution efficiency.

processes.description: Defining Case Types and Policies in D365 Customer Service Defining Case Types and Policies ensures that customer issues are categorized correctly and handled according to standardized processes. Case Types classify cases (e.g., inquiries, complaints, service requests), while Policies dictate resolution procedures, escalations, and SLA adherence. 1. Steps to Define Case Types in D365 Step 1: Navigate to Power Apps for Case Type Configuration Go to Power Apps ( https://make.powerapps.com ). Select the Environment where you want to configure case types. Click on Tables in the left navigation. Search for and select the Case (incident) table. Step 2: Create a Case Type Choice (Option Set Field) In the Case table , go to the Columns tab. Find the Case Type column (or create a new Choice column if not available). Click Edit Choice and define case type values: Inquiry Service Request Complaint Technical Issue Click Save & Publish . 2. Steps to Define Case Subjects in D365 Step 1: Navigate to Customer Service Admin Center Go to Customer Service Admin Center ( https://admin.powerplatform.microsoft.com ). Select your Environment and open Customer Support . Navigate to Case Settings → Case Subjects . Step 2: Define Case Subjects (Hierarchical Categories) Click New Subject and enter: Name : (e.g., "Product Issues", "Billing", "Software Bug"). Parent Subject (Optional for nested categories). Click Save & Close . 3. Steps to Define Case Policies In Case Settings , configure the following options: Case Handling Times Define response and resolution time expectations. Configure SLAs to track service commitments. Advanced Similarity Rules Enable AI-based duplicate case detection to suggest related cases. Improve efficiency by preventing duplicate case creation. Automatic Record Creation & Update Rules Automate case creation from emails, chats, and other channels . Define rules to update existing cases based on new customer interactions. Surveys & Customer Feedback Set up customer satisfaction surveys for post-resolution feedback. Integrate with Microsoft Forms or Customer Voice . Other Settings Define default case resolution behaviors . Set up auto-close rules for resolved cases. Configure notifications for escalations and SLA breaches .

processes.title: Establish a knowledge base
processes.description: The case to resolution process is a critical business process that enables organizations to effectively manage customer or employee inquiries, complaints, and issues. The process involves various steps, such as engaging with customers, logging the case, assigning it to the appropriate team or individual, investigating and resolving the issue, and closing the case. However, managing this process can be challenging, particularly as organizations grow in size and complexity, which is where technology solutions like Dynamics 365 come in. Microsoft Business Applications including Dynamics 365, Microsoft Teams, and Microsoft 365 are a powerful platform that can support the case to resolution process by automating and streamlining many of its key steps. For example, Dynamics 365 Customer Service can enable organizations to engage in conversations with customers through various channels, including email, phone, chat and social media, identify and authenticate customers, answer customer questions, run transactions on behalf of customers, log cases and automatically assign cases to the appropriate team or individual based on predefined rules. It can also provide real-time visibility into case status and progress, enabling managers and teams to track performance, identify bottlenecks, and optimize the process for greater efficiency and effectiveness. Dynamics 365 Human Resources has functionality to help employees and managers communicate effectively through cases to manage common requests and issues. Likewise, Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management includes cases management tools to help with the process of managing issues with customers and vendors for example, including complex issues like a product recall. Dynamics 365 Finance and Supply Chain Management also include tools to help with the effective management of returns, exchanges, credits, price matching, and more. However, it's important to note that Dynamics 365 is just one component of a broader case to resolution process. The process involves multiple stakeholders, such as customers, employees, managers, and support teams, who may have different roles, responsibilities, and workflows. Moreover, the process may differ depending on the type of case, the industry, or the organization's specific requirements. Therefore, it's important to have a well-defined and flexible process that can adapt to different scenarios and needs, and to ensure that Dynamics 365 is integrated with other systems and processes for maximum effectiveness. Every organization has variations to the case to resolution process. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology solution to support the case to resolution.

processes.title: Create knowledge base articles
processes.description: As a consultant, I need to understand the process/details to create, revise, and publish knowledge base articles so that internally or externally knowledge can be searched and used to resolve issues before or after a case is opened. The AI system/copilot will walk me through the steps required to create my first knowledge base article. Ask the configuration prerequisites (Lookups, values, or other supporting entities) The expectation is to provide an order of prerequisites (1-x) Provide the user with the ability to fill in the details from each pre-requisite area (Knowledge Articles, queues, skills and SLAs by order) Once complete, I can move on to the next area Once all pre-requisites are entered, I should now be able to create a new knowledge base article (From user perspective) Security Roles for Creating Knowledge Base Articles in D365 Customer Service In Dynamics 365 Customer Service, users need specific security roles to create and manage knowledge base (KB) articles. The key roles involved in KB management include: Knowledge Manager – Full control over knowledge articles, including publishing and managing content. Knowledge Author – Can create, edit, and submit knowledge articles but does not have publishing permissions. Customer Service Manager – Can manage customer service operations, including knowledge articles. Customer Service Representative – Typically has read-only access to published knowledge articles but may have permissions to create drafts. System Administrator – Has full access, including the ability to configure knowledge management settings. Steps to Create a Knowledge Base Article in D365 Customer Service Follow these steps to create a KB article in Dynamics 365 Customer Service : Step 1: Navigate to Knowledge Management Sign in to Dynamics 365 Customer Service . In the Customer Service Workspace , select Knowledge Articles from the left navigation pane. Step 2: Create a New Knowledge Article Click + New to create a new article. Fill in the required fields: Title – Enter a meaningful title. Content – Add the main content of the article in the rich text editor. Keywords – Add keywords to improve searchability. Description – Provide a summary of the article. Expiration Date – Set if applicable. Subject – Categorize the article under relevant subjects. Step 3: Add Attachments (Optional) If needed, attach images, documents, or other reference materials. Step 4: Review and Submit for Approval Click Save to draft the article. Click Submit to send the article for review. If approval is required, a Knowledge Manager will review and approve/reject it. Step 5: Publish the Article Once approved, click Publish to make the article available to users. Choose the publishing options: Internal – Visible only to employees. External – Available to customers via the self-service portal. Restricted – Limited access based on permissions.

processes.title: Maintain knowledge base articles
processes.description: As a Knowledge Manager, I need to know how to review existing articles, identify updates, and provide the updates in knowledge base articles so that they can be reviewed/approved so the updated content is available to support analysts. 1. Reviewing Knowledge Base Articles A structured review process ensures that KB articles remain useful and up-to-date. This includes: A. Identifying Articles for Review Use expiration dates and review schedules to trigger a review. Monitor article feedback (user ratings, comments, and usage stats). Use search analytics to determine if articles are effectively addressing customer needs. Assign review responsibility to a Knowledge Manager or a designated team. B. Evaluating Articles Relevance: Is the article still applicable to current products, services, or processes? Accuracy: Does the content contain outdated information or incorrect details? Clarity: Is the article well-structured, concise, and easy to understand? Format & Compliance: Does it adhere to KB style guidelines and regulatory requirements? 2. Updating Knowledge Base Articles Once an article is identified for update, follow these steps: A. Initiate the Update Process The assigned editor or SME (Subject Matter Expert) creates a new draft version of the article. Changes should align with corporate guidelines, product updates, or new best practices . B. Editing and Revising Make necessary content updates (text, images, embedded videos, or links). Ensure formatting meets KB standards (structured sections like Overview, Steps, FAQs). Tag the article with relevant categories and keywords for better discoverability. C. Internal Review by Peers A peer or Knowledge Author verifies the technical accuracy of the changes. The article is checked for grammar, clarity, and formatting consistency . 3. Submitting for Approval Before publishing, the article must go through an approval process: A. Reviewer Assignment A designated reviewer or approver (Knowledge Manager, QA, or Team Lead) is assigned. The reviewer gets notified via D365 workflows or Power Automate . B. Review Process The reviewer validates content accuracy, completeness, and policy compliance . They provide comments or request changes if needed. If changes are needed, the article is sent back for revision. C. Approval and Publishing Once approved, the article moves to a published state . It becomes available in the Customer Service portal, internal support interface, or chatbot integration . 4. Ongoing Maintenance and Governance Regular Reviews : Schedule a periodic review cycle (e.g., every 6 months). Feedback Incorporation : Address customer feedback and internal team suggestions . Archival of Old Articles : Remove or retire articles that are no longer relevant . Workflow in Dynamics 365 Customer Service Identify articles needing updates (scheduled review, feedback, analytics). Edit & Draft the article with necessary updates. Submit for Review to an assigned reviewer. Approve & Publish once the reviewer confirms accuracy. Monitor & Maintain articles using review schedules and feedback.

Updated Steps to Retire a Knowledge Base (KB) Article in D365 Customer Service Retiring a Knowledge Base (KB) article in D365 Customer Service Workspace ensures that outdated or incorrect content is no longer accessible while preserving it for historical reference. 1. Steps to Retire a KB Article in Customer Service Workspace Step 1: Navigate to the Knowledge Articles Section Open Customer Service Workspace . In the left navigation pane , select Knowledge Articles . Step 2: Locate the Article to Retire Use the Search bar or apply Filters to find the article. Click on the Knowledge Article you want to retire. Step 3: Change the Article Status to "Retired" In the article record, locate the Status field . Click on the Status dropdown and select Retired . Click Save . Step 4: Validate the Article is No Longer Active Once an article is retired: It will no longer appear in search results for agents and customers. It cannot be linked to cases or suggested in case resolution. It remains stored in the system for historical reference . Step 5: Archive or Delete (Optional) Archive: Retired articles remain available for internal tracking and compliance. Delete: Administrators can permanently remove articles if they are no longer needed.

processes.title: Engage in conversations with customers
processes.description: As a Customer Service Representative (CSR), I want to communicate with customers via chat, email, phone, or in-person, So that I can provide timely support and ensure cases are handled efficiently. his document outlines the standard process and steps for handling customer cases in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service , including engaging with customers via chat, email, phone, or in-person interactions . 1. Process Overview The case management process ensures efficient tracking, resolution, and communication with customers across multiple channels. The key steps include: Case Creation – Capture customer issues from different channels. Case Triage & Assignment – Prioritize and assign the case to the right agent. Customer Engagement & Communication – Interact with the customer through their preferred channel (chat, email, phone, or in-person). Case Investigation & Resolution – Diagnose and work towards resolving the issue. Case Closure & Follow-up – Provide resolution confirmation and gather customer feedback. 2. Detailed Steps in the Case Management Process Step 1: Case Creation Cases can be created manually by a CSR, automatically from customer interactions, or via a self-service portal . Supported case creation methods: Email : An email received creates a case (via Email-to-Case automation). Chat : Live chat sessions initiate a case. Phone Call : A CSR logs a case from an inbound or outbound call. In-Person : A CSR manually logs the issue after an in-person conversation. Self-Service Portal : Customers submit cases via a support portal. Action Items: Ensure customer details (contact, account, and issue description) are correctly captured. Assign a priority and category for the case. Step 2: Case Triage & Assignment Automatic Assignment : Based on skill set, availability, or workload via Omnichannel for Customer Service or Workstreams . Manual Assignment : A supervisor or dispatcher assigns the case. Prioritization Rules : Cases are categorized as Low, Normal, High, or Urgent based on impact. Action Items: Ensure the correct agent is assigned. Add internal notes if required for additional context. Step 3: Customer Engagement & Communication The agent initiates or continues communication with the customer based on their preferred channel: 1. Live Chat (Omnichannel for Customer Service) Customer starts a conversation via chat. The CSR greets the customer and reviews previous interactions (if available). CSR works on resolving the issue in real-time. If further action is needed, the chat is converted into a case for follow-up. 2. Email (Customer Timeline in D365) CSR responds to customer emails directly within the Case record. Email templates can be used for standard responses. Attachments (screenshots, guides, etc.) can be included. If necessary, an escalation email is sent to internal teams. 3. Phone Call (Integrated Softphone or Manual Entry) CSR calls the customer and logs the conversation in the Case Timeline. Key details such as call duration, discussion points, and next steps are recorded. If needed, the call is transferred to a different team or escalated. 4. In-Person Meeting (Field Visit or Walk-in) If the customer visits the support center or an agent is dispatched onsite, notes are logged. Customer signs off on discussions or agreements, if applicable. Any necessary follow-up actions are scheduled. Action Items: Keep conversation history logged in the Case Timeline for visibility. Ensure follow-up tasks (if needed) are scheduled. Step 4: Case Investigation & Resolution The CSR diagnoses the issue using knowledge articles, past cases, or internal resources. If needed, the case is escalated to technical support or a manager . If a product return, refund, or service visit is required, the proper process is initiated. A resolution is determined and communicated to the customer. Action Items: Use Knowledge Base articles to assist in troubleshooting. Escalate the case if additional expertise is required. Document resolution steps in the case record. Step 5: Case Closure & Follow-up The agent confirms with the customer that the issue is resolved. The case is marked as “Resolved” in D365 Customer Service. A feedback survey is sent to the customer (optional). If unresolved, the case is reopened for further action. Action Items: Update the case with final resolution notes. Notify the customer and confirm resolution before closing the case. (Optional) Send a post-resolution survey for customer feedback.

processes.title: Create and track tasks for a case
processes.description: As a Customer Service Representative (CSR), I want to create and track tasks related to a case, So that I can ensure all necessary actions are completed for resolution. Steps to Create and Track Tasks for a Case in D365 Customer Service In Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service , tasks help agents track actions related to resolving customer cases. This document outlines the steps to create, assign, and track tasks associated with a case. 1. Process Overview When working on a case, tasks can be created to: Assign follow-up actions to an agent or team. Track pending actions such as investigations, customer callbacks, or approvals. Ensure that all case-related activities are completed before closing the case. Tasks can be managed through the Activities pane in the Case record. 2. Steps to Create a Task for a Case Step 1: Navigate to the Case Record Open Dynamics 365 Customer Service . Go to Service > Cases . Select an existing case or create a new one. Step 2: Add a New Task Within the Case record, locate the Timeline or Activities section. Click + Add Activity and select Task . Enter task details: Subject : A brief task name (e.g., "Follow up with customer"). Description : Additional details on what needs to be done. Owner : Assign the task to a specific agent or team. Due Date : Set a deadline for task completion. Priority : Choose Low, Normal, or High . Regarding : Ensure the case record is linked to the task. Click Save & Close to create the task. 3. Steps to Track and Update Tasks Step 1: View Tasks Related to a Case Open the Case record in D365. In the Timeline section, locate all open tasks. Use filters to view Active Tasks only. Step 2: Update Task Progress Click on an existing task to open it. Modify details such as status, notes, or due date . Change the Status Reason : Not Started (default) In Progress Waiting for Input (if waiting for a customer or internal team) Completed (when done) Click Save & Close to update the task. 4. Steps to Complete a Task and Close It Open the task from the Case Timeline . Change Status to Completed . Add final notes in the Description field if needed. Click Save & Close . 5. Automating Task Creation (Optional) Use Power Automate to automatically create tasks when: A case is assigned to a specific queue. A case reaches a certain status (e.g., "Waiting for Customer Response"). A high-priority case is created.

processes.title: Follow up on a case
processes.description: As a Customer Service Representative (CSR), I want to follow up on a case internally, with a customer, or with a vendor, So that I can ensure timely updates, track progress, and resolve the issue efficiently. Steps to Follow Up on a Case in D365 Customer Service Effective case follow-ups ensure timely resolution and maintain strong communication between internal teams, customers, and vendors. This guide outlines the steps for: Internal Case Follow-up (within the organization) Customer Case Follow-up (keeping customers informed) Vendor Case Follow-up (escalating cases to third-party vendors) 1. Internal Case Follow-up (Within the Organization) Step 1: Identify Follow-up Needs Open the Case Record in D365 Customer Service. Check the Status, Assigned Agent, and Notes to determine if internal follow-up is required. Step 2: Assign or Escalate the Case If additional expertise is needed, assign the case to another team or escalate. Use the Case Owner field to change ownership. Add an Internal Note with instructions or context. Step 3: Schedule a Task for Internal Follow-up Click + Add Activity > Task within the Case Timeline. Assign the task to an internal team member with a due date. Mark the task as In Progress or Waiting for Input . Step 4: Follow-up via Teams or Email Send an internal email by clicking Email in the Activities section. If immediate attention is required, initiate a Microsoft Teams chat with the assigned agent or team. Step 5: Monitor Status & Close Internal Task Review the case status and activity updates. Once internal feedback is received, close the task and proceed with external follow-up. 2. Customer Case Follow-up Step 1: Check Case Progress Open the Case Record and review the Case Timeline . Identify pending actions or updates. Step 2: Choose Follow-up Method Email : Use email templates for consistency. Phone Call : Log the details in Case Activities . Live Chat : Update the customer in real-time (if using Omnichannel). Step 3: Send an Update Click + Add Activity > Email within the Case. Select an Email Template or write a custom response. Include: Case Number Current Status Next Steps & Expected Resolution Time Customer Portal Link (if applicable) Click Send & Track Response . Step 4: Log Customer Response If the customer responds, update the case notes in the Timeline . If additional action is required, create a Task or reassign the case. Step 5: Set a Reminder for Next Follow-up If no immediate resolution is available, create a follow-up task . Mark the next follow-up date and notify the assigned agent. 3. Vendor Case Follow-up (Suitable for cases involving third-party vendors, suppliers, or service providers.) Step 1: Gather Vendor Contact Information Open the Case Record and check for linked vendor details. If the vendor is not listed, locate the contact under Accounts or Contacts . Step 2: Send a Vendor Inquiry Click + Add Activity > Email and address it to the vendor contact. Include: Case Reference Number Issue Summary Required Action from the Vendor Deadline for Response Step 3: Follow-up with a Phone Call (if needed) If no response is received within the SLA, call the vendor. Log the phone call under Activities > Phone Call . Step 4: Update the Case Record Document the vendor’s response and next steps in the Case Timeline . If additional vendor actions are required, set a Follow-up Task . Step 5: Notify the Customer (if applicable) If the vendor provides a resolution, update the customer. If delays occur, inform the customer with an expected timeline. As a Customer Service Representative (CSR), I want to follow up on a case internally, with a customer, or with a vendor, So that I can ensure timely updates, track progress, and resolve the issue efficiently.

processes.title: Merge cases
processes.description: As a Customer Service Representative (CSR), I want to merge duplicate cases into a single case, So that I can avoid redundancy and improve case tracking. Steps to Merge Cases in D365 Customer Service In Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service , merging duplicate or related cases ensures a streamlined case management process by consolidating information into a single case record. 1. When to Merge Cases Merging is useful when: A customer submits multiple cases for the same issue. Two agents create separate cases for the same customer request. A case is mistakenly duplicated. 2. Steps to Merge Cases in D365 Customer Service Step 1: Open the Case List View Navigate to Service > Cases in D365. Identify the cases you want to merge. Step 2: Select Cases to Merge Select the primary case (the case that will remain). Select the secondary case(s) (the ones to be merged into the primary case). Click on the "Merge Cases" option in the command bar. Step 3: Confirm the Merge Details A confirmation dialog will appear. Choose how to handle activities: Keep activities and merge them into the primary case. Close activities in the secondary case(s). Confirm that the selected primary case is correct. Click Merge . Step 4: Verify the Merged Case Open the primary case. Ensure that: Notes, emails, and activities from the secondary case(s) have been transferred. The case status and owner remain unchanged. The merged cases are now marked as Canceled and linked in the Case Timeline . 3. Important Considerations Merging is irreversible – verify case details before merging. All activities from secondary cases will be linked to the primary case. SLAs on the primary case remain active; merged cases lose their SLA tracking. Security roles must allow merging cases.

processes.title: Send knowledge article to customer
processes.description: As a Customer Service Representative (CSR), I want to send a relevant Knowledge Article to a customer, So that they can quickly find answers and resolve their issue. Steps to Send a Knowledge Article to a Customer in D365 Customer Service Sharing a Knowledge Article with a customer helps provide quick resolutions and improve case efficiency. This guide outlines the steps to find, attach, and send a Knowledge Article in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service . 1. When to Send a Knowledge Article The article contains troubleshooting steps relevant to the case. The customer has a frequently asked question. The issue can be resolved using self-help instructions. The agent wants to provide additional reference material. 2. Steps to Send a Knowledge Article in D365 Customer Service Step 1: Open the Case Record Navigate to Service > Cases in D365. Select the case where you want to send an article. Open the case details page. Step 2: Search for a Knowledge Article In the Case Form , locate the Knowledge Search pane (usually on the right side). Type relevant keywords related to the issue. Select the most appropriate Knowledge Article. Click Associate to link the article to the case. Step 3: Send the Knowledge Article to the Customer Option 1: Send via Email Click Email a link or Attach to Email (based on your setup). A new email window will open with the article attached or linked. Personalize the email with: Case Number Customer Greeting Brief Explanation of the Article Click Send . Option 2: Send via Chat (Omnichannel for Customer Service) If the customer is engaged in a live chat, select the article. Click Send as a Chat Message . The article link will be sent instantly in the chat. Option 3: Copy & Share the Public URL Open the Knowledge Article. Copy the public URL (if available). Paste it into an email, chat, or case notes for the customer. 3. Tracking and Managing Sent Articles Check Email Activity – Ensure the article was sent successfully. Monitor Customer Engagement – If the customer hasn’t responded, follow up. Log Article Usage – Track how often a Knowledge Article is used.

processes.title: Swarm on case with team
processes.description: As a Customer Service Agent, I want to collaborate with my team using a case swarm, So that I can resolve complex issues faster with expert input. Steps to SWARM on a Case with a Team in D365 Customer Service A Case Swarm is a collaborative approach where multiple agents, teams, or experts work together on a complex case to expedite resolution. In Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service , SWARMING ensures that difficult cases get the attention they need from the right people. 1. When to SWARM on a Case The case is complex and requires input from multiple experts. A high-priority or VIP customer case needs immediate resolution. The assigned agent lacks the expertise to resolve the issue alone. The issue spans multiple departments (e.g., IT, Billing, Customer Support). 2. Steps to Initiate a Case SWARM in D365 Customer Service Step 1: Identify the Need for a Swarm Open the Case Record and review the issue details. Check if previous troubleshooting attempts were unsuccessful. Determine the required expertise (technical support, billing, etc.). Step 2: Start a Swarm Discussion in Microsoft Teams In the Case Record , click the "Collaborate" (Microsoft Teams Integration) button. Select Start a Teams Chat or Meeting with relevant agents. Tag subject matter experts and provide a brief case summary. Attach relevant case details, notes, or customer history. Step 3: Assign Tasks to Team Members Within D365 Activities , create Tasks for each contributor. Assign owners, set due dates, and track progress. Use Power Automate to notify team members automatically. Step 4: Update the Case with Findings & Next Steps As each participant provides input, log updates in the Case Timeline . Summarize key takeaways from the swarm session. Assign follow-ups or escalation steps if needed. Step 5: Communicate with the Customer Once a resolution path is determined, update the customer. If additional time is needed, provide an estimated resolution timeframe. Send a Knowledge Article if applicable. Step 6: Close the Swarm & Monitor Case Progress Mark internal tasks as Completed once team contributions are finalized. If resolved, close the case and request customer feedback. If unresolved, escalate the case to higher support levels.

processes.title: Track additional information against a case
processes.description: As a Customer Service Representative (CSR), I want to attach documents, add notes, and create relationships between cases and other records, So that I can maintain a complete and organized case history for better resolution tracking. Steps to Track Additional Information Against a Case in D365 Customer Service To ensure comprehensive case management , agents often need to attach documents, add notes, update the timeline, and create relationships between cases or other records in Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service (D365 CE) . This guide outlines the steps to track and manage additional case-related information efficiently. 1. Accessing the Case in Customer Service Workspace Step 1: Open the Case in Customer Service Workspace Navigate to Customer Service Workspace in D365. Click on Cases from the left-hand navigation panel. Use the search bar or filters to find the case you need. Click on the case to open the record. 2. Attaching Documents to a Case Step 1: Upload a File to the Case Timeline In the Timeline section, click + Add Note . Type a brief description of the document. Click Attach File , select the file from your system, and click Upload . Click Save to link the document to the case. Step 2: Upload to SharePoint (if enabled) Scroll to the Documents section in the case form. Click Upload and select the file. The document is now stored in the linked SharePoint folder. 3. Updating the Timeline on a Case Step 1: Add a Note to the Timeline In the Case Record , navigate to the Timeline section. Click + Add Note . Enter relevant case details, updates, or progress tracking. (Optional) Use the "@" symbol to mention a colleague for collaboration. Click Save – the note will now be visible in the Case Timeline . Step 2: Log an Activity (Email, Phone Call, Task, etc.) In the Timeline , click + Add Activity . Choose the appropriate activity type (e.g., Phone Call, Email, Task ). Enter the necessary details: For Phone Calls : Log the conversation details. For Emails : Compose and send an email directly from the case. For Tasks : Assign follow-ups to agents. Click Save – the activity is now recorded in the Case Timeline . 4. Creating Relationships to Other Records or Cases Step 1: Link a Case to Another Case (Parent/Child Relationship) Open the Case Record that will be the "Child" case. Scroll to the Related Cases section. Click + New Case Relationship . Select the Parent Case from existing records. Click Save & Close . Use Case: When a case is related to a larger issue, linking it as a Child Case allows tracking under one Parent Case . Step 2: Link a Case to Other Records (Contacts, Accounts, Work Orders, etc.) Open the Case Record . Navigate to the Related Records section. Select the type of record you want to link (e.g., Contacts, Accounts, Work Orders, Opportunities ). Click + Add Existing Record or + New Record if it doesn’t exist. Click Save to establish the relationship. Use Case: If a case is related to a specific customer account, asset, or work order , linking ensures better traceability. 5. Best Practices Use SharePoint Integration for secure and centralized document storage. Keep Notes Organized by adding timestamps and tagging relevant agents. Log All Interactions to maintain a full history of customer communications. Automate Case Documentation – Use Power Automate to generate reports when a case is updated.

processes.title: Concept to market
processes.description: Concept to market is the process of managing a service offering from its inception to its eventual end of life. The process typically begins with the development of a service offering idea, which is then refined and tested to ensure that it meets customer needs. After the service is launched, it's important to monitor its performance and make necessary adjustments to keep it competitive in the marketplace. As the service offering matures, it might be necessary to update or refresh the design to maintain customer interest. Eventually, the service offering might reach the end of its marketable life and be retired from the market. Throughout the concept to market process, careful attention must be paid to customer needs, market trends, and technological advancements to ensure that the service offering remains relevant and successful. In service-based organizations or organizations that sell services alongside tangible products, Dynamics 365 offers a variety of products to help support the design and development of new service offerings and control the downstream transactions that occur in the organization. For example, when you use Dynamics 365 Field Service, you can define service offerings that are sold by using Dynamics 365 Sales or Supply Chain Management. For complex services, such as professional services, you can define the services in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management or Sales, and use Dynamics 365 Project Operations to help manage the lifecycle of your customer relationship. Additionally, you can mix and match services with tangible products on orders, include services in your production process, or outsource services by using Procurement and sourcing, Project Operations, or Field Service, to give just a few examples. Important: The process that is defined here doesn't include the process for designing tangible products. Learn more at Design to retire introduction. Every organization has variations of the concept to market process. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization that is looking to implement a technology solution to support the concept to market process for services.

processes.title: Design to retire
processes.description: Design to retire is the process of managing a product from its inception to its eventual end of life. The process typically begins with the development of a product offering idea, which is then refined and tested to ensure that it meets customer needs. After the product is launched, it's important to monitor its performance and make necessary adjustments to keep it competitive in the marketplace. As the product matures, you might want to update or refresh the design to maintain customer interest. Eventually, the product reaches the end of its useful life, and you retire it from the market. Throughout this process, product management requires careful attention to customer needs, market trends, and technological advancements to ensure that the product remains relevant and successful. For the engineering-type products that are common in the manufacturing industry, the product and lifecycle management process can involve managing complex bills of materials (BOMs) or formulas. A BOM or formula lists all the parts and components that go into a product, and their relationships to each other. Management of a BOM requires careful attention to ensure that all components are available in the correct quantities, and that account lead times, availability, and cost are also considered. Some organizations offer products that are variable or configurable. In such cases, you can use the product configurator in Dynamics 365 to enable customers to select specific features and options for a product. The options that a customer can choose from are dynamically updated and control the BOM. For retail organizations, the design to retire process often also involves merchandising. Merchandising is the process of selecting and presenting products to customers in a way that maximizes sales. It might include designing product packaging, creating promotional materials, and managing inventory levels to ensure that products are available when customers want them. Dynamics 365 Commerce includes several capabilities that help support the process of enhancing product information with attributes, categorizing products for easy navigation on a website, and relating products to each other. Examples include up-selling and cross-selling of products, and the use of AI to suggest products based on an analysis of products that other customers purchased. Effective product and lifecycle management requires collaboration among multiple teams, including engineering, manufacturing, marketing, and sales, to ensure that the product is successful throughout its lifecycle. Important: The process that is defined here doesn't include the process for designing production routes. Learn more about that process at Plan to produce introduction. Every organization has variations of the design to retire process. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization that is looking to implement a technology solution to support the design to retire process.
