processes.title: Manage active products
processes.description: Management of the product lifecycle within an organization is of paramount importance for businesses that deal with tangible products, whether they are involved in buying, selling, distributing, or manufacturing. Strategic orchestration of the product lifecycle ensures optimal efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and customer satisfaction. When organizations use Dynamics 365 to maintain product information, the system plays a pivotal role by seamlessly integrating various products, such as Dynamics 365 Customer Service, Sales, Field Service, Project Operations, and Supply Chain Management. This comprehensive integration provides a unified approach and enables organizations to streamline operations, enhance collaboration, and make informed decisions throughout the entire product lifecycle. The process of managing a product's lifecycle involves several critical business processes, each of which contributes to the overarching success of the data and downstream process. These business processes include analyzing product margins of products that are sold or produced. Many signals can come from upstream processes in the case-to-resolution process. These processes send signals that inventory should be removed, or that item usage should be restricted in sales, procurement, production, or servicing operations. For organizations that manufacture products, it's critical to ensure that you: Define and document clear engineering policies. Maintain accurate product versions and details. Process the requested changes with rigor to ensure compliance with established policies and regulations. Furthermore, the capability to seamlessly request, process, and retire a product underscores the agility and adaptability that Dynamics 365 affords. Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management includes robust product information management capabilities that seamlessly integrate with other products in the suite. Therefore, organizations can navigate the complexities of the product lifecycle with precision and ensure sustained success and adaptability in the dynamic business landscape. The business processes for managing the product lifecycle in a Dynamics 365 implementation should be addressed in the early to mid-design and configuration stages of the project.

processes.title: Introduce products
processes.description: The ability for an organization to create new products in their offerings plays a pivotal role in the growth and innovation of the organization. The business process area involves strategic development, launch and integration of fresh offerings into the market, ensuring that the organization remains competitive and responsive to the evolving customers' needs. The process of introducing new offerings into the market can vary drastically from industry to industry and geography to geography, among other factors. However, one thing that is certain among all organizations, is that the process can be costly, time consuming, and has a direct impact on the organization's bottom line. For this reason, having strong technology solutions like Dynamics 365, Microsoft 365, and the Power Platform are essential to ensure that business decision makers have the right information to make the right decisions. Organizations can diversify their portfolio, tap into new revenue streams, and strengthen market presence by introducing new products. The Dynamics 365 product suite offers a variety of tools and products to help support this process and products across multiple industries. For example, Dynamics 365 Customer Service offers capabilities to support tangible products that are offered to customers. Dynamics 365 Commerce offers the capabilities to track sales in the point of sale, online, in a call center, or with integrations from Dynamics 365 Sales or other third-party solutions that help you manage your sales cycle. Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management supports the product lifecycle of manufactured products, distributed products, and much more. With complex support for various types of products across the portfolio, it's important to select the right technologies to support your business needs. When introducing new products, it's important to consider that careful execution of the market research, ideation, rigorous testing, and seamless coordination across departments is executed well. Dynamics 365 Marketing offers tools to help with many steps, and when used alongside our productivity tools like Microsoft Teams, Planner, and Outlook, and Dynamics 365 Customer Voice, as a few examples, organization can successfully implement solutions to support the process leading to increased customer satisfaction, increased brand reputation, and sustainable growth. When organizations are looking to implement technological solutions to support the introduction of new products business process, we recommend that these activities are prioritized and planned early in the process. The product data that is captured as part of the business process is critical to many of the downstream processes and poor implementation can cause data quality issues which can lead to other issues later in the project and in the overall business cycle. Keep in mind that product data is considered master data and should be carefully planned and integrated into all downstream business processes. If you are planning to use a third-party solution for product master data, you can integrate your solution in the first phases of your product and you can look to replace the third-party solution in a later phase. However, careful considerations for the functionality needed should be taken early in the project to avoid reworking later.

processes.title: Set product prices
processes.description: Managing product pricing is a pivotal aspect of organizational success, influencing profitability and competitive positioning. In today's dynamic business landscape, effective product pricing requires a comprehensive approach, and when using the suite of Dynamics 365 products organizations can achieve these goals. From Dynamics 365 Commerce to Customer Service, Field Service, Project Operations, Sales, and Supply Chain Management, these interconnected tools provide a robust framework for optimizing product pricing strategies. Dynamics 365 enables organizations to seamlessly align pricing structures with market demands and competitive landscapes, fostering transparent relationships with clients. The suite facilitates agile responses to dynamic market changes, ensuring adaptability and strategic refinement to stay ahead. Specifically, in Dynamics 365 Commerce, businesses can apply advanced pricing models for both business to business (B2B) and business to consumer (B2C) scenarios, across channels such as online, in store, and in the back office, enhancing their merchandising strategies and delivering personalized pricing experiences to diverse customer segments. The process of managing product pricing involves a series of interconnected business processes crucial for organizational efficiency. Beginning with the definition of a robust product catalog and strategy, organizations can introduce new products seamlessly, strategically positioning them in the market. The management of product pricing involves meticulous determination of prices and eligibility for discounts, ensuring offerings align with market demands. Simultaneously, defining product costing becomes paramount for maintaining profitability. The holistic approach extends to managing the entire product lifecycle, from introduction to retirement, ensuring continuous refinement and strategic adaptation. This integrated process within Dynamics 365 empowers organizations to navigate the complexities of product pricing with agility and foresight, contributing to sustained success. In an organization focused on products, especially when downstream processes such as procure to pay, prospect to quote, order to cash, plan to produce, project to profit, case to resolution, service to cash, and/or record to report are part of the Dynamics 365 implementation, early consideration of business processes related to managing product pricing is essential. The data and output of these processes impact various downstream operations and defining them early in the project ensures overall project success. If Dynamics 365 won't serve as the system of record for product data, integrations to the designated system should be considered early in the planning phase.

processes.title: Develop product strategy
processes.description: All organizations group and categorize or segment their products into logical grouping for various reasons. Dynamics 365 includes several capabilities that you can consider implementing together at the beginning of a project. The terms categorization, merchandising, and segmentation of products and services are all related concepts. Although all three terms are often used interchangeably, they do have distinct meanings and functions in the system as well. The following list outlines the differences:- Categorization refers to the process for grouping products or services based on shared characteristics. Segmentation refers to the process of dividing a market (of typically customers) into smaller groups (or segments) based on shared characteristics or interests. Merchandising refers to the process of presenting products or services in an appealing and attractive way to the customers. It's important for an organization to consider carefully how it categorizes, segments, and merchandises the products and services it offers. During the implementation of a business solution, an organization often already has a way of doing this already. It's important to consider if the current mechanism for categorizing products and services meets all the business requirements, because the implementation of a new technology solution is often a good time to consider making a change. The organization might want to consider questions such as the following list: How do you drive downstream business processes and automation? How do you report and analyze your data including operational reporting and financial reporting? How has your business grown since the original mechanism of categorization, segmentation, or merchandising was developed? How do you anticipate your business will grow in the future? The answers to these questions should help inform your process for defining the way you implement a technology solution to support the categorization of products and services. This business process area should always be considered early in a Dynamics 365 implementation project. Also consider the number of changes that might be happening to the data in this area as well. This can make integrations, data migration, and other aspects of your project more complex. When an organization starts a Dynamics 365 implementation, it's important to carefully consider how you define the product lines in the system. This includes tasks like setting up item groups and product categories in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management and product families in Dynamics 365 Sales. The business process areas for categorizing either products or services also include the definition of product policies. We recommend that you group similar items together based on the expected behaviors they need in the system. This includes settings like item model groups, reservations, storage, and tracking dimensions, and more in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Also, if your organization offers multiple types of products or services, you should define the rules and configurations for each type of product or service that you offer. For example, in the chemical or food and beverage industry, you might use catch weight items. In some industries, consigned inventory is common and requires more setup, configuration, and considerations. Similarly, the service industry has considerations to make for the services that they offer, including warranties, installation, and so on. Many organizations also charge extra fees or service charges for tangible items that are sold which might require more considerations. Dynamics 356 supports various flexible configurations to support many types of products, services, and extra fees and charges that might be charges to customers or imposed by suppliers. Once you have a basic definition for organizing products or services, you can categorize and build hierarchical structures and catalogs or assortments for the downstream processes. Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management and Commerce support multiple flexible hierarchies for procurement, sales, channel management, and more. In Dynamics 365 Sales, you can create hierarchies of products or services with product families. Dynamics 365 Commerce uses assortments to define product mix for a retail channel such as the call center, retail store, or online store. One or more assortments are then combined and assigned to a catalog for each retail channel. This process often uses product attributes that further describe the product. However, attributes can describe categories or retail channels as well, for example. When you group common or similar items together into categories, you can more easily manage the attributes. Attributes serve an important function in merchandising and for customers to find products that meet their requirements. Attributes can be easily added at any time, but starting with a good baseline for your project to help you meet reporting requirements is critical to downstream analytics. With tools to mass update attribute values, you can easily manage the values at any time and adapt to the changing customer needs and supply chain. With Dynamics 365 Customer Service, you can create and manage subjects to manage complex hierarchies that can represent products, brands, or types of issues that are reported by your customers, for example. With Dynamics 365 Customer Insights, segments help you organize customers into groups based on their buying habits and one common segment is typically related to the products customers purchase. However, organizations can define many segments based on many different attributes of the products that are purchased.

Integration with Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps ensures that product changes are reflected in the ERP and communicated to stakeholders. 3 * Product Retirement: Retirement decisions and documentation can be managed collaboratively in Teams and SharePoint, with workflows in Power Automate to update product lifecycle states in Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps and notify relevant teams. 4 * Base Tools Used: Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, Outlook, Excel, Power Automate, Planner, and Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps product management modules.

processes.title: Forecast to plan
processes.description: The term forecast to plan typically describes a collection of business processes that an organization implements to estimate demand and determine how much supply is required to meet those demands. The term forecast means a prediction of future events, typically sales. The plan is the organization's articulation and refinement of the forecast to determine exactly what to buy and produce. Note: For the purposes of this end-to-end process and related business process, we are primarily focused on forecasting and planning of products and services, as opposed to general ledger budgeting and financial planning. The forecast to plan business process is typically part of an organization's larger efforts to buy and sell products or services. It's deeply related to all of the other end-to-end business processes that inform the forecasting and planning strategies. And then the execution of the plan supports the completion of the other operational processes. The upstream or downstream relationship of the forecast to plan business process to the other business processes is highly dependent on the operational strategies of the business. Learn more at Solution architecture design: Vision and strategies. For example, in a make to order environment, the forecast to plan process is a downstream process from forecast to plan. While in a make to stock environment, it's an upstream process. Organizations may also use multiple operational strategies, which is fully supported in Microsoft business apps. The high-level strategy for forecast to plan processes should be planned at the early phases of a larger ERP implementation. The design and decisions made about this process have an impact on downstream processes including integrations, data that must be migrated, and so on. If your organization doesn't have a forecasting or planning process, or the forecast to plan approach is out of scope for early phases of your project, add forecast to plan business processes into your design later. Important: The process defined here does not include the details for forecasting and planning financials including cash flow forecast. Learn more at Record to report introduction. The process defined here also does not include the details for forecasting and planning human resources. Learn more at Hire to retire introduction. Every organization has variations to the forecast to plan processes. In this article, we define the basic benefits and outcomes for any organization looking to implement a technology solution to support the forecast to plan process.

processes.title: Develop business strategy
processes.description: The term forecast to plan typically describes a collection of business processes that an organization implements to estimate demand and determine how much supply is required to meet those demands. The term forecast means a prediction of future events, typically sales. The plan is the organization's articulation and refinement of the forecast to determine exactly what to buy and produce. Note: For the purposes of this end-to-end process and related business process, we are primarily focused on forecasting and planning of products and services, as opposed to general ledger budgeting and financial planning. The forecast to plan business process is typically part of an organization's larger efforts to buy and sell products or services. It's deeply related to all of the other end-to-end business processes that inform the forecasting and planning strategies. And then the execution of the plan supports the completion of the other operational processes. The upstream or downstream relationship of the forecast to plan business process to the other business processes is highly dependent on the operational strategies of the business. Learn more at Solution architecture design: Vision and strategies. For example, in a make to order environment, the forecast to plan process is a downstream process from forecast to plan. While in a make to stock environment, it's an upstream process. Organizations may also use multiple operational strategies, which is fully supported in Microsoft business apps. The high-level strategy for forecast to plan processes should be planned at the early phases of a larger ERP implementation. The design and decisions made about this process have an impact on downstream processes including integrations, data that must be migrated, and so on. If your organization doesn't have a forecasting or planning process, or the forecast to plan approach is out of scope for early phases of your project, add forecast to plan business processes into your design later. Important: The process defined here does not include the details for forecasting and planning financials including cash flow forecast. Learn more at Record to report introduction. The process defined here also does not include the details for forecasting and planning human resources. Learn more at Hire to retire introduction. Every organization has variations to the forecast to plan processes. In this article, we define the basic benefits and outcomes for any organization looking to implement a technology solution to support the forecast to plan process.

processes.title: Hire to retire
processes.description: The hire to retire process, also known as the employee lifecycle, is a critical business process that involves various activities from recruiting and onboarding employees to their separation from a company. In the context of Dynamics 365, the hire to retire process is facilitated and streamlined using various HR modules and tools available in the system. A key portion of the process is defining your organizational structure and planning and then recruiting your workforce. In this stage the organization identifies its hiring needs, employee benefits, and compensation plans, and then begins talent acquisition, the recruiting of qualified candidates. Dynamics 365 includes features to help managers request positions, to recruit, and to streamline communications between departments. It also includes integration capabilities to existing Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) to help you integrate your data into job boards and external sites. Once a candidate is hired, the onboarding process begins. Dynamics 365 includes onboarding features that help automate the onboarding process for new employees and to help your internal teams to prepare for the new hire. The next stage of the process is managing the employee lifecycle, which includes performance management, career development, and succession planning. Dynamics 365 includes employee development capabilities such as the performance management module that automates the performance appraisal process by enabling managers to set goals, track progress, provide feedback, and conduct performance reviews. The system also includes a Learning module that allows employees to access training and development materials and track their progress towards career goals. With the Learning Management System (LMS) APIs you can quickly and easily surface the right courses to your workforce at the right time. HR managers can use tools such as skill gap analysis to identify and develop high-potential employees and create career development plans for them. Dynamics 365 also includes tools to help with the day-to-day operations of the organization including managing time, leave and absence, and expenses for your workforce. For the HR team, we have features to help you stay compliant, perform audits, track safety incidents, and more. And of course, Dynamics 365 enables streamlined end-to-end integrations with partnering payroll systems via a payroll integration API. The final stage of the process is separation. Dynamics 365 includes a Benefits management module that enables HR managers to manage employee benefits and retirement plans, ensuring that retiring employees receive the benefits they are entitled to. The system also includes features to help workers who are transitioning (into new roles or management, for example) or offboarding that helps to streamline the process of separating employees from the organization, including the exit interview process and the collection of company property that are tracked through loaned items. The Microsoft 365 productivity suite can also be leveraged to help improve collaboration and communication within teams and across organizations, streamline business processes and workflows, enhance data security and compliance, and increase overall productivity and efficiency. With its diverse range of tools and applications such as Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and more, Microsoft 365 offers a comprehensive solution for businesses of all sizes to achieve their goals and objectives. Other capabilities can be leveraged through use with tools such as Dynamics 365 Customer Voice, extension through the Power Platform, and integration with products such as Power BI, Dynamics 365 Finance, and Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Every organization has variations of the hire to retire process. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology solution to support the hire to retire process.

processes.title: Manage time and attendance
processes.description: Managing employee time and attendance is a critical aspect of organizational efficiency, playing a pivotal role in ensuring optimal workforce productivity and compliance. In today's dynamic business environment, the use of Dynamics 365 products, such as Human Resources, Project Operations, Field Service, and Supply Chain Management, can help organizations streamline these crucial processes. These tools enable an interconnected approach to time and attendance management including leave and absence management, fostering a more cohesive and efficient work environment. The process of managing employee time and attendance encompasses several key business processes that are supported by Dynamics 365. Organizations typically start by defining and managing time and attendance policies to align with their specific requirements. Dynamics 365 Human Resources supports flexible configuration for leave and absence policies and plans including sick time, paid time off, selling or borrowing leave, and the leave accrual process. In addition, you can use Dynamics 365 Human Resources to record employee absences and facilitate requests for time off, all seamlessly integrated into the employee self-service experience. In addition, Dynamics 365 Commerce supports the ability to create and managing shifts. Depending on your industry and time-reporting needs, Dynamics 365 allows employees to create and submit timesheets. This includes time clocks functionality with Dynamics 365 Commerce, Human Resources, and Supply Chain Management. For more complex manufacturing environments, you can use job card terminals on the production floor or the Time and attendance module in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, providing a comprehensive overview of their work hours and production completed. Supervisors can then efficiently review and approve timesheets, ensuring accuracy and compliance. When you use Dynamics 365 Field Service or Project Operations, you can record time against specific work orders or projects for detailed time reporting that can be easily allocated to the right financial resources for billing, cost recognition, and revenue recognition. The flexibility of the Dynamics 365 platform also allows for easy adjustments and corrections to timesheets, ensuring that the time and attendance data remains accurate and reflective of the dynamic nature of business operations. Determining the high-level architecture of your solution early in the implementation for your time and attendance business processes is important, but you can leave the configuration and setup to the later stages of your project.

processes.title: Manage performance and growth
processes.description: Managing employee performance and growth is integral to the success of any organization, serving as a cornerstone for fostering a motivated and skilled workforce. In today's dynamic business landscape, Dynamics 365 plays a pivotal role in streamlining this process. Specifically, Dynamics 365 Human Resources and Customer Voice synergize to provide a comprehensive solution. Dynamics 365 Human Resources facilitates the definition of performance and review processes, competency requirements, career paths, and learning plans. Meanwhile, Customer Voice helps in gathering valuable feedback, contributing to a holistic view of employee performance. This integration empowers organizations to align their workforce strategies with real-time insights, ensuring a more effective approach to employee development. When you use Dynamics 365 Human Resources together with Dynamics 365 Project Operations, Supply Chain Management, or Field Service, you can manage the skills required to perform work including project work, production work, or field work. When you use Dynamics 365 Human Resources together with Dynamics 365 Commerce, you can manage the shifts and training for the frontline workforce in a brick and mortar or call center stores. Adding in Dynamics 365 Guides provides augmented reality to help train and upskill employees while using Dynamics 365 Remote Assist can be used to assist field workers in their work to monitor or upskill. While Dynamics 365 Customer Service includes features and ability to integrate with telephony system to monitor calls and monitor the customer service that is being delivered to customers. Now, delving into the intricacies of managing employee performance and growth, a series of interconnected business processes come into play. These processes encompass defining performance and review procedures including the goal setting process and documenting employee performance. Skill management is broken up into several business process areas including establishing required competencies for roles, maintaining a repository of skills and competencies, analyzing gaps between skills required for the jobs to be done and the skills of the workforce. The employee growth process including learning, and succession planning containing process areas such managing course offerings, creating learning plans, assigning courses, recording employee progress of assigned learning, and analyzing/reporting on employee learning. These processes also include outlining employee career paths and formulating succession plans. This comprehensive list of processes is supported within Dynamics 365 and help organizations not only automating but also optimizing the entire employee management lifecycle, promoting efficiency and strategic decision-making for organizations aiming to cultivate a high-performance culture. The features and functionality for managing employee performance and growth aren't mandatory to run Dynamics 365 Human Resources; any of the features can be added at any time. Some downstream features such as skills competencies may be required for downstream scheduling processes, for example, in Dynamics 365 Field Service, Project Operations, and Supply Chain Management. In these cases, the skill definition and management processes should be planned earlier in the project to define the flow of data for the downstream processes.

processes.title: Manage workplace compliance
processes.description: In today's dynamic business landscape, the implementation of occupational health and safety processes is essential for maintaining a safe and productive work environment. With Dynamics 365, organizations can streamline and enhance their safety management processes. The defined processes can cover areas such as the following list: Hazard identification Safety protocol documentation Safety condition analysis Safety audits Staff training Injury or illness reporting Treatment seeking Cost-of-care determination Safety communication These processes collectively contribute to a safer and healthier workplace. When you use Dynamics 365 with Microsoft 365 products, such as Viva Learning or Viva Engage, you can streamline business processes and improve your overall health and safety metrics. These processes serve a twofold purpose in any organization. First, they ensure the well-being of employees, reducing the risk of workplace accidents and health-related issues. Second, they help organizations meet legal and regulatory requirements, avoid potential liabilities, and enhance their reputation as responsible corporate citizens. Dynamics 365 implementations facilitate the systematic execution of these processes, providing an efficient and centralized platform for managing safety-related data, incidents, and compliance. One notable advantage of implementing occupational health and safety processes within Dynamics 365 and Microsoft 365 is their flexibility. None of these processes are mandatory prerequisites for the system's operation, allowing organizations to tailor their safety management to their specific needs and timelines. These processes can be easily integrated into the system at any stage of its operation or even incrementally added as the organization evolves. This adaptability ensures that companies can respond to changing safety requirements, growth, and new regulations without major disruptions to their operations. This way, Dynamics 365 becomes a valuable tool for long-term safety and compliance management.

processes.title: Develop people strategy
processes.description: The hire to retire process, also known as the employee lifecycle, is a critical business process that involves various activities from recruiting and onboarding employees to their separation from a company. In the context of Dynamics 365, the hire to retire process is facilitated and streamlined using various HR modules and tools available in the system. A key portion of the process is defining your organizational structure and planning and then recruiting your workforce. In this stage the organization identifies its hiring needs, employee benefits, and compensation plans, and then begins talent acquisition, the recruiting of qualified candidates. Dynamics 365 includes features to help managers request positions, to recruit, and to streamline communications between departments. It also includes integration capabilities to existing Applicant Tracking Systems (ATS) to help you integrate your data into job boards and external sites. Once a candidate is hired, the onboarding process begins. Dynamics 365 includes onboarding features that help automate the onboarding process for new employees and to help your internal teams to prepare for the new hire. The next stage of the process is managing the employee lifecycle, which includes performance management, career development, and succession planning. Dynamics 365 includes employee development capabilities such as the performance management module that automates the performance appraisal process by enabling managers to set goals, track progress, provide feedback, and conduct performance reviews. The system also includes a Learning module that allows employees to access training and development materials and track their progress towards career goals. With the Learning Management System (LMS) APIs you can quickly and easily surface the right courses to your workforce at the right time. HR managers can use tools such as skill gap analysis to identify and develop high-potential employees and create career development plans for them. Dynamics 365 also includes tools to help with the day-to-day operations of the organization including managing time, leave and absence, and expenses for your workforce. For the HR team, we have features to help you stay compliant, perform audits, track safety incidents, and more. And of course, Dynamics 365 enables streamlined end-to-end integrations with partnering payroll systems via a payroll integration API. The final stage of the process is separation. Dynamics 365 includes a Benefits management module that enables HR managers to manage employee benefits and retirement plans, ensuring that retiring employees receive the benefits they are entitled to. The system also includes features to help workers who are transitioning (into new roles or management, for example) or offboarding that helps to streamline the process of separating employees from the organization, including the exit interview process and the collection of company property that are tracked through loaned items. The Microsoft 365 productivity suite can also be leveraged to help improve collaboration and communication within teams and across organizations, streamline business processes and workflows, enhance data security and compliance, and increase overall productivity and efficiency. With its diverse range of tools and applications such as Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, OneDrive, Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and more, Microsoft 365 offers a comprehensive solution for businesses of all sizes to achieve their goals and objectives. Other capabilities can be leveraged through use with tools such as Dynamics 365 Customer Voice, extension through the Power Platform, and integration with products such as Power BI, Dynamics 365 Finance, and Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Every organization has variations of the hire to retire process. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology solution to support the hire to retire process.

processes.title: Inventory to deliver
processes.description: The inventory to deliver business process involves managing the flow of goods from receipt into a warehouse or distribution center through to delivery to the customer. This end-to-end process includes receipt of goods, quality management, inventory management, inventory costing, order fulfillment, and shipping. Important: The process defined here doesn't include the procurement process, which involves purchasing raw materials or finished goods from suppliers. It only includes the receipt of goods in the warehouse. The process also doesn't include production, which involves converting raw materials into sub-assemblies or finished goods. This process does include the issuing of raw materials into production and the receipt of finished goods into inventory. Every organization has variations to the inventory to deliver process. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology solution to support their inventory to deliver business processes.

processes.description: In Dynamics 365 (Dynamics 365), "Use marking" refers to the process of establishing a permanent link between a supply transaction and a demand transaction for the same item. Marking is used to ensure accurate costing, particularly when using FIFO (First In, First Out) or LIFO (Last In, First Out) inventory costing methods. It also supports non-costing scenarios like tracing specific batches or serial numbers.

processes.description: In Dynamics 365, a bill of lading (BOL) is primarily used to document and manage the shipment of goods, serving as a contract between the shipper and carrier, a receipt for the goods, and a document of title. It provides a record of the shipment details, including the shipper, consignee, and a description of the goods, and is used for both inbound and outbound shipments. Bill of lading does not include a list of the item numbers, and exact quantity of each item. It only contains the NMFC or National motor freight codes that are nationally accepted to describe the contents of the container or truck. For further details of each item, dimensions, batch lot numbers, other forms are available to print alongside the BOL.

processes.title: Manage freight and transportation
processes.description: The Manage freight and transportation business process area encompasses the activities that are done in an organization's transportation management process. All distribution organizations must be able to track and manage transportation costs and operations so that they can optimize this critical part of the supply chain. Meeting this goal requires cross-organization collaboration among departments such as Logistics, Procurement, Planning, Sales, and Operations. The exact process for the Manage freight and transportation area varies from business to business and depends on the industry. However, the basic steps are the same: The need for transportation is identified. Identification of this need triggers planning activities, including rating and routing operations. Dock appointments can then be scheduled for pickup and/or delivery, and necessary logistics paperwork can be generated. After transportation is completed, freight invoices can be processed and reconciled against estimates. The definition of these steps is done as part of the Inventory to deliver end-to-end business processes and refined in the Define and manage warehouse operations business process area. It's essential that you define and establish the business process for Managing freight and transportation when you first begin to implement Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. This process is a fundamental element for any distribution company, because it forms the backbone of efficient supply chain operations.

processes.title: Scrap defective inventory
processes.description: In base Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, scrapping defective inventory is performed using an inventory adjustment journal. Warehouse staff identify items that are damaged, expired, or otherwise unfit for use. They create an inventory journal entry, select the relevant items and quantities, and specify a reason code (such as "scrap" or "defective"). Posting the journal reduces on-hand inventory and updates financial records, ensuring accurate stock and cost accounting. The process may include capturing supporting notes, attaching documentation, and, if configured, triggering workflow approvals for audit purposes.

processes.title: Scrap expired inventory using journals in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
processes.description: In base Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps, scrapping expired inventory is handled through inventory adjustment journals. Warehouse or inventory managers periodically review stock for expiration, identify expired items, and create an inventory adjustment journal. They select the expired items, enter the quantities to be scrapped, and use a reason code such as "expired." Posting the journal reduces the on-hand inventory and updates financial records accordingly. This process is straightforward, does not require quality orders, and can be supported by standard reporting and optional workflow approvals.

processes.title: Manage warehouse operations
processes.description: The inventory to deliver business process involves managing the flow of goods from receipt into a warehouse or distribution center through to delivery to the customer. This end-to-end process includes receipt of goods, quality management, inventory management, inventory costing, order fulfillment, and shipping. Important: The process defined here doesn't include the procurement process, which involves purchasing raw materials or finished goods from suppliers. It only includes the receipt of goods in the warehouse. The process also doesn't include production, which involves converting raw materials into sub-assemblies or finished goods. This process does include the issuing of raw materials into production and the receipt of finished goods into inventory. Every organization has variations to the inventory to deliver process. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology solution to support their inventory to deliver business processes.

processes.title: Order to cash
processes.description: The order to cash business process flow is a standard term used to describe the entirety of an organization's sales order process. The process is sometimes referred to as O2C or OTC. Generally speaking, the order to cash business process includes everything that happens in an organization from a customer places an order until the payment is received and settled with the invoice. IMPORTANT: The process defined here does not include the process for marketing to prospective customers, tracking leads and opportunities and the creation of quotes. Also note that the order to cash process described here does not include order fulfillment process. The process of fulfilling orders is described in the inventory to deliver process. Every organization has variations to the order to cash business process. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology solution to support the order to cash business process. Impact on the organization The order to cash business process is important for all organizations because it directly impacts your customer service experiences, workforce planning, inventory management practices, and cashflow. Technology solutions that you implement to support your order to cash business process should be flexible to allow your organization to grow and adjust as both the market and supply chain evolve. Having a periodic review of your order to cash business processes can ensure that your technology aligns with your business goals and objectives.

processes.title: Develop sales policies
processes.description: The process area refers to the structured definition and governance of rules, strategies, and procedures that guide how an organization sells its products or services. Core Components of Developing Sales Policies Sales Strategy Definition: This includes setting the overall direction for sales efforts such as defining target markets, value propositions, and competitive positioning. It ensures that sales activities align with business growth objectives. Sales Channels and Teams: Organizations define which channels (e.g., direct, partner, digital) they will use and how sales teams are structured. This includes assigning roles, territories, and responsibilities. Sales Targets and Incentives: Policies are established to determine sales quotas, performance metrics, and compensation structures. These are often aligned with financial planning and HR systems to ensure consistency and motivation. Sales Process Governance: This involves defining the steps from lead qualification to quote generation and order fulfillment. It ensures consistency in how opportunities are pursued and closed Compliance and Risk Management: Sales policies also address regulatory compliance, pricing controls, discounting rules, and approval workflows to reduce risk and ensure accountability. Implementation in Dynamics 365 Microsoft's guidance outlines how Dynamics 365 supports this process area through modules like Sales, Customer Insights, and Finance: Process Flow Mapping: The Define a sales strategy process flow includes subprocesses such as: Define sales channels Define sales team Determine sales targets Establish commission and incentive structures Define sales process Cross-Functional Integration: The process connects with other business areas like: Hire to Retire (for workforce planning) Forecast to Plan (for demand planning) Record to Report (for budgeting and financial alignment) Benefits of Implementation: Strategic alignment between sales execution and business goals Increased productivity through specialization Motivated teams via rewards and recognition

processes.title: Develop order management policies
processes.description: This process is designed to define the rules, conditions, and configurations that govern how sales orders are handled across different channels such as call centers, eCommerce platforms, and traditional sales operations. It ensures consistency, compliance, and efficiency in order processing, fulfillment, and customer service. These scenarios reflect the need to tailor policies based on the operational context whether it's a centralized warehouse, a distributed retail network, or an online storefront. Functional Elements in Dynamics 365 Microsoft Learn outlines two main types of policies used in Intelligent Order Management: Filter Policies: These validate data as it flows through orchestration. For example, a filter policy might route orders from a specific region to a designated fulfillment center. Execution Policies: These update or enrich data during orchestration. For instance, assigning a fulfillment location when an order exceeds a certain quantity. Each policy includes: Policy Name and Type Criticality (Information vs. Critical) Status (Published or Unpublished) Associated Entity (Order, Order Product, Fulfillment Order, etc.) These policies are configured in the Orchestration > Policies section of Dynamics 365 Intelligent Order Management. Strategic Value Developing clear order management policies: Reduces fulfillment errors and delays Enables automation and orchestration of order flows Supports omnichannel consistency Minimizes customizations by leveraging standard Microsoft capabilities

processes.title: Define customer classifications
processes.description: The process refers to the structured segmentation of customers into meaningful groups based on shared characteristics, behaviors, or financial attributes. This classification supports targeted sales strategies, credit risk management, and operational efficiency across the customer lifecycle. Defining customer classifications allows organizations to: Segment customers by attributes such as industry, geography, size, payment behavior, or strategic value. Apply differentiated policies for pricing, credit limits, collections, and service levels. Improve reporting and analytics by enabling grouped insights into customer performance, profitability, and risk. Support automation in workflows like invoicing, dunning, and sales forecasting by applying rules based on classification. In Dynamics 365 Finance, customer classification is typically managed through: Customer Groups. These are configured in the system to assign shared financial and operational settings (e.g., posting profiles, payment terms, tax groups) to multiple customers. This is done via: Accounts receivable > Setup > Customer groups Accounts receivable > Setup > Customer posting profiles Customer Definitions Entity: This data entity supports importing and updating customer records, including classification fields like: CUSTOMERGROUPID (required)PARTYTYPE (Organization or Person) PAYMENTTERMS, SALECURRENCYCODE, SALESTAXGROUP, etc. These fields help define the customer's financial and operational profile. Customer Statistics and Risk Scoring: Classification can also feed into analytics such as customer turnover, aging, and risk scoring

processes.title: Define customer classifications in Dynamics 365 Business Central
processes.description: The Enter Sales Orders business process defines how organizations capture and manage sales orders across various channels and scenarios. It supports both traditional and modern sales models and is a core part of the Order to Cash cycle. SUPPORTED SALES CHANNELS * Manual Entry: Sales orders entered directly by back-office staff using Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management or Business Central. * Point of Sale (POS): Store associates enter orders at the register using Dynamics 365 Commerce. * Call Centers: Assisted sales and remote order entry. * eCommerce (B2B/B2C): Online orders captured automatically via integrated platforms. * Quotes to Orders: Sales professionals convert quotes into orders using Dynamics 365 Sales. * Agreements to Orders: Orders generated from contractual agreements or recurring commitments. SUPPORTED SALES TYPES * Products: Tangible goods across retail, wholesale, and manufacturing. * Services: Consulting, subscriptions, maintenance, and leasing. * Gift Cards: Issued and redeemed through POS or eCommerce. * Royalty-Based Items: Sales that trigger royalty payouts, common in media and publishing. ADVANCED SCENARIOS * Intercompany Trade: Automatically generated orders between legal entities. * Brokered Sales: Orders facilitated by third-party brokers with custom integrations. * Dual Write: Real-time synchronization between Dynamics 365 apps and Dataverse. * EDI Orders: Electronic Data Interchange for automated B2B order processing. PROCESS FLOW 1. Initiate Order: Capture customer intent via POS, eCommerce, call center, or manual entry. 2. Validate Terms: Apply pricing, discounts, and contract terms. 3. Confirm Order: Generate and confirm the sales order in the system. 4. Sync Systems: Use Dual Write or EDI to ensure data consistency across platforms. 5. Monitor & Adjust: Track order status, apply changes, and manage exceptions. STAKEHOLDERS * Sales Associate: Enters orders via POS or call center. * Sales Manager: Oversees quote conversion and agreement-based orders. * Order Fulfillment Lead: Coordinates delivery and logistics. * Finance Controller: Ensures compliance with revenue recognition and royalty tracking. * IT Integration Lead: Manages Dual Write, EDI, and broker integrations. DYNAMICS 365 SUPPORT * Dynamics 365 Commerce: POS, gift cards, eCommerce, loyalty. * Dynamics 365 Sales: Quote-to-order conversion. * Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management: Manual entry, intercompany, royalty tracking. * Dynamics 365 Business Central: Back-office order management. * Dynamics 365 Intelligent Order Management: Orchestration and fulfillment. * Dual Write & EDI: Real-time sync and automated B2B processing.

Enhanced Reporting: Hierarchies and attributes support better analytics and forecasting.

processes.title: Develop sales pricing strategy
processes.description: The Develop Sales Pricing Strategy business process defines how an organization sets, manages, and evolves its pricing structures to align with market conditions, business goals, and customer expectations. It is a critical component of the broader Order to Cash cycle and directly influences profitability, competitiveness, and customer satisfaction. Core Components Regular Sales Pricing : Establishing base prices for products and services based on cost, market demand, and strategic positioning. Discounting : Designing and applying volume discounts, promotional offers, and loyalty-based incentives. Freight and Other Charges : Incorporating shipping costs, handling fees, and surcharges into final pricing. Coupons and Promotions : Managing time-bound, customer-specific coupon codes and promotional pricing. Price Adjustments : Revising prices based on market shifts, competitive analysis, and internal profitability reviews. Process Flow Analyze Market Data : Gather insights on competitors, customer behavior, and cost structures. Evaluate Pricing Strategy : Assess alignment with business goals and financial targets. Implement Pricing : Configure systems to apply pricing rules across channels. Revise Strategy : Monitor performance and adjust pricing as needed. Stakeholders Involved Pricing Manager : Designs and maintains pricing structures. Sales Operations Manager : Ensures pricing aligns with sales goals and is correctly applied. Finance Controller : Validates pricing for profitability and compliance. E-commerce Manager : Manages digital pricing, coupons, and tiered pricing models. Dynamics 365 Support Microsoft Dynamics 365 provides robust tools to support this process: Configuration & Automation : Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management : Enables configuration of base prices, discounts, freight charges, and promotional pricing across products and channels. Dynamics 365 Commerce : Supports coupon management, tiered pricing, and loyalty programs for online sales. Dynamics 365 Sales : Integrates pricing strategies into lead generation and opportunity management. Data-Driven Decision Making : Built-in analytics dashboards help pricing managers evaluate performance and identify opportunities for price adjustments. Integration with Power BI allows deeper insights into pricing trends, customer behavior, and profitability. Operational Efficiency : Automated workflows ensure consistent application of pricing rules across sales channels. Real-time updates allow agile responses to market changes and promotional campaigns.

processes.title: Define trade allowances
processes.description: The Define Trade Allowances business process outlines how organizations create and manage promotional incentives offered to customers in exchange for meeting specific volume or behavioral goals. These allowances are commonly used in industries such as consumer packaged goods (CPG), food and beverage, wholesale distribution, and retail. Core Components Bill-Backs Retroactive payments made to customers based on actual sales performance. These are calculated after the sale and processed as deductions in accounts receivable. Off-Invoice Discounts Immediate reductions applied directly to the invoice at the time of sale. These are simple to administer and provide instant value to the customer. Promotional Funds Budgeted amounts allocated to support trade allowance programs. These funds are tracked and reconciled to ensure alignment with financial policies. Lump Sum Payments One-time payments made to customers for agreed-upon promotional activities or services, such as in-store displays or advertising. Traditional Rebates Periodic payments based on cumulative purchases or performance metrics. These are often used to reward long-term customer loyalty. Process Flow Identify Allowance Requirements Define the types of trade allowances needed based on business goals and customer expectations. Analyze Trade Data Review historical sales, customer behavior, and market trends to inform allowance design. Develop Allowance Criteria Set eligibility rules, performance thresholds, and funding limits. Evaluate Allowances Assess the financial impact and strategic alignment of proposed programs. Implement Allowances Configure systems and processes to apply allowances across sales channels. Revise Allowances Monitor performance and adjust programs as needed to optimize effectiveness. Stakeholders Trade Promotion Manager Designs and manages trade allowance programs, including eligibility, funding, and tracking. Accounts Receivable Manager Processes customer claims and ensures accurate financial reconciliation. Sales Director Negotiates terms with customers and monitors program effectiveness. Finance Controller Oversees budgeting and compliance with financial policies. Dynamics 365 Support Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Enables setup and automation of trade allowance agreements, bill-back claims, and promotional fund tracking. Accounts Receivable Integration Processes deductions and reconciles short-pays against approved claims. Analytics and Reporting Built-in dashboards and Power BI integration support performance analysis and forecasting.

processes.title: Define order risk management strategy
processes.description: The Define Risk Management Strategy business process helps organizations identify, assess, and mitigate fraud and operational risks across sales channels and fulfillment processes. It is a critical component of the broader Order to Cash cycle and supports financial integrity, customer trust, and operational resilience. Core Components Order Holds Apply automated or manual holds on sales orders based on credit exposure, fraud risk, or policy violations. Fraud Detection Use rule-based and AI-driven tools to detect suspicious transactions, bot activity, and payment anomalies. Return Abuse Monitoring Track patterns of excessive or fraudulent returns and apply exception handling policies. Payment Risk Scoring Evaluate transactions using risk scores to determine approval, hold, or escalation paths. Bot Detection Identify and block automated attacks or scraping attempts on e-commerce platforms. Exception Handling Manage edge cases such as mismatched payments, duplicate orders, or unusual customer behavior. Process Flow Identify Risk Areas Define risk categories such as fraud, credit exposure, and operational vulnerabilities. Analyze Risk Data Review historical incidents, transaction patterns, and customer behavior. Develop Risk Rules Create detection logic, thresholds, and escalation paths. Implement Controls Configure systems to enforce risk rules and automate responses. Monitor and Revise Continuously evaluate effectiveness and adjust strategies based on performance and emerging threats. Stakeholders Fraud Risk Manager Designs detection rules, monitors alerts, and manages escalations. Finance Controller Oversees credit policies, order holds, and financial exposure thresholds. E-commerce Manager Implements fraud prevention strategies for online channels. Customer Service Lead Monitors return abuse and exception handling policies. Dynamics 365 Support Dynamics 365 Fraud Protection Provides real-time fraud detection, risk scoring, and bot protection. Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Supports order holds, credit policies, and exception handling. Dynamics 365 Commerce Enables fraud detection for online channels, including bot detection and payment risk scoring.

processes.title: Define accounts receivable strategy
processes.description: The Define Accounts Receivable Strategy business process outlines how an organization establishes policies and rules for invoicing, payment terms, and cash discounting. This strategy ensures financial transparency, supports efficient collections, and aligns with broader business goals. It does not include the operational execution of invoicing or payment processing. Core Components Cash Discounting Rules Define discount terms to incentivize early payments. Examples include: 3% discount if paid within 10 days 1% discount if paid within 30 days Discounts can be configured with or without sales tax, depending on compliance needs. Invoicing Strategy Establish invoice formats, approval workflows, and posting rules. This includes: Automated invoice generation Invoice posting workflows Customer account adjustments These elements ensure timely billing and reduce manual errors. Payment Rules Set flexible payment terms based on: Fixed periods (e.g., net 30, net 60) Installment schedules Percentage allocations Rules should be aligned with customer segmentation and financial policies. Process Flow Define Strategy Requirements Identify business goals, customer expectations, and compliance needs. Design Terms and Discounts Configure payment terms and discount policies based on historical data and market practices. Establish Approval Workflows Implement controls for invoice posting and payment journal approvals. Integrate with Financial Models Ensure strategy is embedded in customer and financial data models from the start. Monitor and Refine Use analytics to assess performance and adjust strategy as needed. Stakeholders Accounts Receivable Manager Oversees invoicing, payment application, and reconciliation. Finance Controller Ensures compliance with financial policies and validates discounting and payment rules. ERP Implementation Lead Aligns strategy with Dynamics 365 configuration and data models. Dynamics 365 Support Finance & Business Central Automates invoice generation, payment term configuration, and discount application. Workflow Management Supports approval processes for invoice posting and customer adjustments. Analytics & Reporting Dashboards and Power BI integration help monitor AR performance and cash flow.

processes.title: Define credit and collections strategy

It is a critical part of the Order to Cash cycle and supports financial governance, cash flow health, and customer relationship management. Core Components Credit Limits Set thresholds for customer credit exposure based on risk profiles, historical payment behavior, and financial analysis. Credit Holds Automatically or manually block orders that exceed credit limits or violate credit policies. Interest Notes Apply interest charges to overdue balances based on predefined rules and rates. Collection Letters Generate structured communications to remind customers of overdue payments, escalating in tone and urgency. Fees and Penalties Define and apply late payment fees, reinstatement charges, and other penalties as part of the collections process. Process Flow Define Credit Policies Establish rules for credit limits, approval workflows, and risk thresholds. Configure Collections Strategy Set up interest calculation methods, collection letter sequences, and fee structures. Automate Monitoring Use aging snapshots, customer pools, and collection agents to track overdue accounts. Execute Collections Activities Generate letters, apply interest, and escalate cases as needed. Review and Refine Monitor effectiveness and adjust policies based on performance and business needs. Stakeholders Credit Manager Oversees credit limit policies and approval workflows. Collections Coordinator Manages overdue accounts, sends collection letters, and tracks customer responses. Finance Controller Ensures compliance with financial policies and oversees interest and fee application. Accounts Receivable Manager Reconciles payments, applies holds, and manages customer account status. Dynamics 365 Support Dynamics 365 Finance Supports credit limit configuration, credit holds, interest notes, and collection letter automation. Collections Workspace Provides centralized views of aging balances, payment history, and remaining credit. AI-Driven Features Automates email generation and prioritizes collection actions using customer data. Case Management Tracks collection activities and escalations using case categories and approval workflows.

processes.title: Analyze sales performance
processes.description: Analyze sales performance provides a disciplined, data‑driven cadence for measuring sales outcomes and diagnosing the drivers across accounts receivable health, cash flow, customer risk, revenue, and the effectiveness of order management processes. Scope and objectives Establish a single view of sales performance across channels, regions, products, and customer segments. Translate operational signals (orders, fulfillment, returns, cancellations, holds) into financial impact (revenue, margins, DSO, cash position). Detect emerging risk in AR and customer credit, and surface proactive actions for collections, pricing, and policy changes. Provide an executive and operational rhythm for continuous improvement of order management processes. Key analysis areas Sales performance: bookings vs. billings, revenue recognition, margin mix, product/channel/region performance, promo impact. Accounts receivable: aging, DSO, promise‑to‑pay effectiveness, write‑off trends, dispute root causes, concentration risk. Cash flow: collections velocity, forecasted cash, variance vs. plan, impact of payment terms and early‑pay discounts. Customer risk: credit utilization, delinquency, fraud signals, chargebacks/NSF, exposure by tier/segment. Order management health: order cycle times, hold rates and reasons, change/cancel rates, returns/RMA drivers, fulfillment SLAs. High - level process Define metrics and targets Standardize KPIs, thresholds, and definitions (e.g., revenue vs. gross sales, DSO formula, “on‑time fulfillment”). Assemble the data foundation Land sales, order, AR, cash, pricing, and policy data; ensure harmonized calendars, currencies, and dimensions. Produce the executive and operational dashboards Build scorecards for leaders and diagnostic views for sales ops, AR, and order management teams. Profile performance and variances Compare actuals vs. plan and prior periods; isolate variance drivers (volume, mix, price, returns, timing). Diagnose AR and cash drivers Attribute DSO changes to disputes, promises, aging buckets, terms shifts, and customer/segment mix. Evaluate customer risk Refresh risk scores, credit utilization, and delinquency trends; flag concentrations and escalating exposure. Inspect order management processes Analyze holds, lead times, changes/cancels, backorders, and returns; connect bottlenecks to revenue and cash impact. Recommend and track actions Generate prioritized actions (collections sequences, term changes, pricing/promo adjustments, policy updates), assign owners, and set due dates. Close the loop Measure action effectiveness, update targets, and incorporate learning into the next review cycle. Roles and responsibilities Sales leadership: Own sales outcomes, approve corrective actions, and set targets. Sales operations/RevOps: Maintain metrics, perform variance analysis, drive pipeline and pricing insights. Finance/AR: Lead AR, cash, and revenue analytics; partner with collections on promises, disputes, and write‑offs. Order management/SCM operations: Improve order flow, reduce holds and returns, align fulfillment with demand. Risk and credit management: Monitor exposure, adjust limits/policies, and coordinate with collections. Data & analytics: Curate data models, dashboards, and advanced analytics; ensure data quality and governance. Dynamics 365 support Finance: AR aging, DSO, cash forecasting, revenue recognition, collection letters, interest notes, disputes, business events. Sales: Opportunity/pipeline to bookings, price lists/discounts, forecast accuracy, seller productivity insights. Supply Chain Management & Commerce: Order lifecycle analytics, hold reasons, returns/exchanges, channel performance, promo impact. Customer Insights (Data & Journeys): Segmentation, lifetime value, churn/propensity, campaign attribution for sales. Microsoft Fabric/Power BI: Unified semantic models, scorecards, drill‑through diagnostics, scheduled refresh, row‑level security. Copilot/agents: Narrative summaries of performance, anomaly detection, suggested next‑best actions (e.g., target customers for outreach, policy exceptions to review). Data and telemetry foundations Master dimensions: calendar, product, customer, region/route‑to‑market, channel, sales org. Conformed measures: revenue, gross margin, returns, AR buckets, write‑offs, DSO, cash collected, order cycle time. Event streams: order created/changed/canceled, hold applied/released, invoice posted, collection letter issued, payment posted, interest note posted, dispute opened/closed. Operational controls and governance Metric definitions and change control to prevent KPI drift. Segregation of duties for pricing changes, credit limit adjustments, write‑offs, and term overrides. Audit trails for policy changes and manual adjustments. Privacy and retention controls for customer financial data. Inputs and outputs Inputs: sales orders/invoices, returns, price and discount tables, AR transactions, collections activities, credit limits and exposure, cash receipts, inventory/fulfillment status. Outputs: executive scorecards, variance narratives, prioritized action lists with owners and due dates, refreshed targets, and a closed‑loop action effectiveness log. KPIs (illustrative) Sales and margin: revenue vs. plan, gross margin %, mix impact, promo ROI, average selling price trends. AR and cash: DSO, current vs. >90‑day balances, promise‑kept rate, dispute rate and time‑to‑resolve, cash forecast accuracy. Customer risk: credit utilization %, high‑risk balance share, delinquency transition rates, chargeback/NSF rate. Order management: order‑to‑invoice cycle time, hold rate and top reasons, change/cancel rate, return rate and top root causes. Process effectiveness: action closure rate, impact per action (revenue/cash), time‑to‑detect/time‑to‑correct anomalies. Cadence and operating rhythm Weekly operational reviews at team level for actions and blockers. Monthly business reviews for performance vs. plan and policy decisions. Quarterly planning to refine targets, adjust incentives, and align investment to the most material improvement opportunities. Implementation tips Start with a minimal KPI set tied to decisions, then expand. Favor conformed dimensions and a single semantic model to avoid conflicting truths. Pair diagnostic dashboards with Copilot narratives to accelerate insight consumption. Treat exceptions as productized workflows (e.g., credit limit review, returns spike playbook) with standard owner/SLAs.

processes.title: Analyze accounts receivable
processes.description: Analyze accounts receivable provides a disciplined, data-driven review of receivables health and cash velocity—measuring days outstanding, turnover, bad debt, collection effectiveness, invoicing and payment productivity—so leaders can act early to protect revenue, reduce risk, and improve working capital. Applies to: Dynamics 365 Finance Dynamics 365 Business Central Dynamics 365 Sales (forecast/pipeline context) Dynamics 365 Commerce (POS tender impacts) Power BI/Fabric (semantic models, dashboards) Copilot for Finance (summaries, next-best actions, anomaly detection) Core KPIs and definitions (what to measure) Days Sales Outstanding (DSO): average number of days to collect credit sales. AR Turnover Ratio: number of times receivables are collected per period. Bad Debt Ratio: write-offs (or provisions realized) relative to AR or credit sales. Collection Effectiveness Index (CEI): effectiveness of converting collectible AR during a period. Average Days Delinquent (ADD): slippage from agreed terms. % Current / % > 30 / > 60 / > 90: aging mix and trend. Dispute Rate and Time-to-Resolution: share of invoices disputed; cycle time to close. Promise-to-Pay Kept Rate: kept commitments ÷ total promises, by segment/collector. Customer Invoicing Productivity: invoices posted per FTE; first-pass yield; invoice cycle time; error-rework rate. Payment Productivity (Cash Application): payments posted per FTE; auto-match rate; straight-through processing rate; unapplied cash; lockbox efficiency. Write-off Rate: amount written off ÷ credit sales (or ending AR). Chargeback/NSF Rate: returned or reversed payments as a percent of receipts. Credit Utilization & Exposure: used vs. available credit; exposure at risk. Dilution: returns/credits/allowances as % of billings. Interest Income from Finance Charges: assessed vs. collected. Deductions/Claims Rate: trade allowances, rebates, and unauthorized deductions as % of sales. Standard AR, collections, and deductions reports/workspaces Aging and Exposure: Customer aging report; aging snapshots; customer exposure by risk/terms; credit limit utilization; expected cash by bucket. Collections: Collections workspace (worklists, pools), Collections status, Collection letter sequence output, Promise-to-pay tracking, Broken promise rollups. Interest/Finance Charges: Interest notes generated/posted; finance charge statements; interest income by customer/segment. Deductions/Trade: Rebate accrual and settlement reports; trade allowance claims/deductions; deduction reasons and recovery rate; net sales after allowances. Cash Application: Payment journal exceptions; auto-matching effectiveness; unapplied cash; short-pay analysis; lockbox/EDI hit rates. Customer Statements & Transaction Detail: statements, open item lists, transaction aging detail, charge/credit memos. Credit/Risk: Credit management hold list; risk groups; exposure changes; expired limits. Dimensions and drill paths (how to slice) Legal entity, currency, region, customer/account, customer group/segment, salesperson/account owner, channel (POS/online/B2B), payment method, terms, invoice type, dispute/deduction reason, product family/line. High‑level process Define metric dictionary and targets Standardize KPI formulas (e.g., DSO, CEI), fiscal calendars, and thresholds; publish goals by segment/channel. Assemble a trusted AR model Land invoices, credit memos, payments, interest notes, collection letters, deductions/rebates; harmonize dimensions and currencies. Produce aging snapshots and baseline KPIs Generate aging by bucket and trend; compute DSO, turnover, ADD, bad debt ratio; highlight mix shifts. Analyze collection effectiveness and cash velocity Calculate CEI; compare against targets; identify pools/collectors with low effectiveness or rising broken promises. Diagnose risk and credit exposure Review credit utilization, holds, expired limits; correlate over-limit orders with aging slippage and write-offs. Assess customer invoicing productivity and quality Invoices per FTE, cycle time, first-pass yield; pinpoint root causes of rework (pricing, tax, master data, EDI). Assess payment productivity and cash application Payments per FTE, auto-match rate, unapplied cash backlog; analyze short-pays and remittance quality. Inspect deductions, rebates, trade allowances, and interest Track accrual accuracy, claim timeliness, recovery %, and interest collected vs. assessed; quantify net revenue impact. Identify anomalies and root causes Outliers in buckets, sudden CEI drops, spike in disputes/NSFs; trace to customers, terms, campaigns, or operational changes. Recommend and track actions Targeted collections strategies, term changes, credit limit reviews, invoice quality fixes, auto-match rules, deduction recovery playbooks; assign owners and due dates. Close the loop and recalibrate Measure impact on DSO/CEI/cash; update thresholds, pools, and playbooks; feed insights to sales, pricing, fulfillment. Roles and responsibilities AR/Collections Manager: Owns policy, CEI/DSO targets, portfolio strategy. Collections Lead/Agents: Execute worklists, promises, escalations; maintain activity hygiene. Cash Application Lead: Drives auto-match, unapplied cash cleanup, exceptions. Credit Manager: Oversees exposure, risk groups, limit reviews, holds. Finance Controller: Ensures compliance (revenue, bad debt), approves write-offs/waivers. Sales/Account Owners: Partner on sensitive accounts; align commitments and term changes. Data & Analytics: Curates semantic models, KPI logic, dashboards, alerts. Dynamics 365 support Finance Collections workspace (pools, worklists), customer aging, collection letters, interest notes, credit management hold list, customer statements, bad debt write-off proposals, payment journals, bank/lockbox reconciliation, business events for interest posted/collection letter created. Business Central Aged accounts receivable, customer ledger entries, reminders (dunning), finance charge memos, customer statements, payment reconciliation journals, dimensions for analysis. Commerce/POS Tender mix, voids/returns/exception monitoring impacting deductions and cash; store-level aging exposure where applicable. Trade/Rebate/Allowance management Accruals, claims, settlements, deduction tracking; net sales after allowances reporting. Power BI/Fabric AR analytics (aging, DSO, CEI, exposure), cash application performance, deduction recovery; scorecards with alerts; row-level security. Copilot for Finance Collections coordinator summary, prioritized actions, auto-drafted collection emails with invoice context, anomaly flags on CEI/aging slippage, narrative KPI summaries. Operational controls and governance Policy controls: terms, dunning/interest rules, approval thresholds for waivers/write-offs, deduction recovery SLAs, regional compliance. Segregation of duties: configuration vs. posting vs. waivers vs. write-offs. Auditability: calculation details for interest/letters, promise histories, approval logs; event logs for posted artifacts. Privacy/retention: safeguard customer financial data; retain only as required. Inputs and outputs Inputs: invoices, credit memos, payments, interest notes, collection letters, rebate/allowance accruals and claims, credit limits, exposures, promises, disputes, unapplied cash. Outputs: aging/DSO/CEI dashboards, risk/exposure views, invoicing and payment productivity scorecards, deduction and interest reports, prioritized action lists with owners and due dates. KPI target examples DSO: decreasing trend with bucket mix improving (e.g., >90-day share CEI: ≥ 85–95% depending on segment. Auto‑Match Rate: ≥ 80–90% with lockbox/EDI optimization. First‑Pass Invoice Yield: ≥ 95% after master data/EDI fixes. Promise‑kept Rate: ≥ 85% on targeted portfolios. Deduction Recovery: ≥ defined SLA; reduce open deductions aging by N days.
