Standard AR, collections, and deductions reports/workspaces * Aging and Exposure: Customer aging report; aging snapshots; customer exposure by risk/terms; credit limit utilization; expected cash by bucket. * Collections: Collections workspace (worklists, pools), Collections status, Collection letter sequence output, Promise-to-pay tracking, Broken promise rollups. * Interest/Finance Charges: Interest notes generated/posted; finance charge statements; interest income by customer/segment. * Deductions/Trade: Rebate accrual and settlement reports; trade allowance claims/deductions; deduction reasons and recovery rate; net sales after allowances. * Cash Application: Payment journal exceptions; auto-matching effectiveness; unapplied cash; short-pay analysis; lockbox/EDI hit rates. * Customer Statements & Transaction Detail: statements, open item lists, transaction aging detail, charge/credit memos. * Credit/Risk: Credit management hold list; risk groups; exposure changes; expired limits. Dimensions and drill paths (how to slice) * Legal entity, currency, region, customer/account, customer group/segment, salesperson/account owner, channel (POS/online/B2B), payment method, terms, invoice type, dispute/deduction reason, product family/line. High‑level process 1. Define metric dictionary and targets * Standardize KPI formulas (e.g., DSO, CEI), fiscal calendars, and thresholds; publish goals by segment/channel. 2. Assemble a trusted AR model * Land invoices, credit memos, payments, interest notes, collection letters, deductions/rebates; harmonize dimensions and currencies. 3. Produce aging snapshots and baseline KPIs * Generate aging by bucket and trend; compute DSO, turnover, ADD, bad debt ratio; highlight mix shifts. 4. Analyze collection effectiveness and cash velocity * Calculate CEI; compare against targets; identify pools/collectors with low effectiveness or rising broken promises. 5. Diagnose risk and credit exposure * Review credit utilization, holds, expired limits; correlate over-limit orders with aging slippage and write-offs. 6. Assess customer invoicing productivity and quality * Invoices per FTE, cycle time, first-pass yield; pinpoint root causes of rework (pricing, tax, master data, EDI). 7. Assess payment productivity and cash application * Payments per FTE, auto-match rate, unapplied cash backlog; analyze short-pays and remittance quality. 8. Inspect deductions, rebates, trade allowances, and interest * Track accrual accuracy, claim timeliness, recovery %, and interest collected vs. assessed; quantify net revenue impact. 9. Identify anomalies and root causes * Outliers in buckets, sudden CEI drops, spike in disputes/NSFs; trace to customers, terms, campaigns, or operational changes. 10. Recommend and track actions * Targeted collections strategies, term changes, credit limit reviews, invoice quality fixes, auto-match rules, deduction recovery playbooks; assign owners and due dates. 11. Close the loop and recalibrate * Measure impact on DSO/CEI/cash; update thresholds, pools, and playbooks; feed insights to sales, pricing, fulfillment. Roles and responsibilities * AR/Collections Manager: Owns policy, CEI/DSO targets, portfolio strategy. * Collections Lead/Agents: Execute worklists, promises, escalations; maintain activity hygiene. * Cash Application Lead: Drives auto-match, unapplied cash cleanup, exceptions. * Credit Manager: Oversees exposure, risk groups, limit reviews, holds. * Finance Controller: Ensures compliance (revenue, bad debt), approves write-offs/waivers. * Sales/Account Owners: Partner on sensitive accounts; align commitments and term changes. * Data & Analytics: Curates semantic models, KPI logic, dashboards, alerts. Dynamics 365 support * Finance * Collections workspace (pools, worklists), customer aging, collection letters, interest notes, credit management hold list, customer statements, bad debt write-off proposals, payment journals, bank/lockbox reconciliation, business events for interest posted/collection letter created. * Business Central * Aged accounts receivable, customer ledger entries, reminders (dunning), finance charge memos, customer statements, payment reconciliation journals, dimensions for analysis. * Commerce/POS * Tender mix, voids/returns/exception monitoring impacting deductions and cash; store-level aging exposure where applicable. * Trade/Rebate/Allowance management * Accruals, claims, settlements, deduction tracking; net sales after allowances reporting. * Power BI/Fabric * AR analytics (aging, DSO, CEI, exposure), cash application performance, deduction recovery; scorecards with alerts; row-level security. * Copilot for Finance * Collections coordinator summary, prioritized actions, auto-drafted collection emails with invoice context, anomaly flags on CEI/aging slippage, narrative KPI summaries. Operational controls and governance * Policy controls: terms, dunning/interest rules, approval thresholds for waivers/write-offs, deduction recovery SLAs, regional compliance. * Segregation of duties: configuration vs. posting vs. waivers vs. write-offs. * Auditability: calculation details for interest/letters, promise histories, approval logs; event logs for posted artifacts. * Privacy/retention: safeguard customer financial data; retain only as required. Inputs and outputs * Inputs: invoices, credit memos, payments, interest notes, collection letters, rebate/allowance accruals and claims, credit limits, exposures, promises, disputes, unapplied cash. * Outputs: aging/DSO/CEI dashboards, risk/exposure views, invoicing and payment productivity scorecards, deduction and interest reports, prioritized action lists with owners and due dates. KPI target examples * DSO: decreasing trend with bucket mix improving (e.g., >90-day share < X%). * CEI: ≥ 85–95% depending on segment. * Auto‑Match Rate: ≥ 80–90% with lockbox/EDI optimization. * First‑Pass Invoice Yield: ≥ 95% after master data/EDI fixes. * Promise‑kept Rate: ≥ 85% on targeted portfolios. * Deduction Recovery: ≥ defined SLA; reduce open deductions aging by N days.

processes.title: Analyze cash flow
processes.description: Analyze cash flow establishes a disciplined cadence for understanding liquidity, forecasting near- and mid‑term cash needs, explaining variances, and publishing daily cash position and treasury reports with a strong focus on AR-driven inflows. Applies to Dynamics 365 Finance and/or Business Central Power BI and Microsoft Fabric (semantic models, scorecards) Copilot for Finance (narratives, anomaly detection, reconciliation assistance) Bank connectivity (statements/feeds), Treasury operations Core outputs Cash flow statements (direct and indirect methods) Short-term forecast (e.g., 13‑week rolling), medium-term (12–18 month rolling) Daily cash position and liquidity headroom vs. facilities Variance analysis (actual vs. forecast, bank vs. GL) Treasury reporting: covenant headroom, FX exposure/hedge coverage, investment and debt ladders AR-focused inflow projections: expected cash from aging, promises‑to‑pay, subscriptions, and seasonality Core KPIs and definitions Operating cash flow; Free cash flow (Operating CF − Capex) Cash conversion cycle (Days Inventory + DSO − DPO) DSO and Collection Effectiveness Index (CEI) as inflow quality signals Forecast accuracy (MAPE), bias (over/under), and driver-level variance Liquidity coverage ratio, minimum cash threshold, facility headroom Cash burn and runway (months of cash at current net burn) Bank reconciliation timeliness and exceptions aged AR‑specific: expected receipts coverage vs. plan, promise‑kept rate impact on cash, interest income collected, deductions/short‑pay leakage Standard AR and treasury reports to include Daily cash report (opening, inflows, outflows, closing; by bank, currency, legal entity) 13‑week cash forecast and waterfall (baseline, AR slippage, deductions, timing shifts) AR collections forecast (aging-based, promise‑to‑pay, ML‑assisted where available) Variance analysis pack (actual vs. forecast by driver: volume, price, timing, FX) Interest/finance charge collections summary Rebates and trade allowances cash impact (accruals, claims, settlements, net sales effect) Deductions aging and recovery trend; unapplied cash aging Covenant dashboard (EBITDA, DSCR, leverage; headroom and stress scenarios) FX exposure and hedge coverage by currency/tenor; investment/debt maturity ladders High‑level process 1) Define metrics and cadence Standardize KPI formulas (e.g., MAPE, CEI), fiscal calendars, and reporting frequencies (daily, weekly, monthly). 2) Build the cash model and data foundation Land and harmonize actuals (GL, AR, AP, payroll, tax), bank statements/feeds, and dimensions (entity, currency, bank, customer, product). Establish bank‑GL reconciliation rules. 3) Publish the daily cash position Opening balances, intraday movements, expected cutoffs, and end‑of‑day closing by bank/account/currency with liquidity and facility utilization. 4) Produce short‑term forecast (e.g., 13‑week) Start from AR aging and promises‑to‑pay; apply collection patterns, seasonality, churn/renewal, interest receipts, and expected deductions; incorporate AP, payroll, tax, capex, debt service. 5) Produce medium‑term rolling forecast (12–18 months) Tie to revenue plans, backlog, renewals, and pricing changes; model working capital drivers (DSO/DPO/DIH) and macro assumptions (FX, rates). 6) Perform variance analysis Actual vs. forecast by driver (volume, price/mix, timing, FX, collections slippage, deductions). Reconcile bank vs. GL; surface structural vs. timing differences. 7) Scenario and stress testing Run what‑ifs (AR slip by n days, FX shocks, rate moves, delayed rebates, deduction spikes) and assess covenant headroom and liquidity actions required. 8) Action and funding plan Accelerate AR (collections playbooks, early‑pay discounts), adjust credit terms/limits, deploy dunning/interest policies, consider factoring/securitization, swing lines, or invest surplus cash; align hedging for FX and rates. 9) Governance and reporting Daily cash email/dashboards, weekly treasury review (13‑week), monthly management/board pack with actions and owners; document forecast changes and approvals. 10) Continuous improvement Track forecast accuracy and bias, cycle times, reconciliation exceptions, and data quality; refine models, drivers, and policy settings. Roles and responsibilities Treasurer/Treasury Manager: Owns liquidity plan, covenant compliance, hedging, investments/borrowings AR Manager/Collections Manager: Owns inflow quality (DSO, CEI, promises‑kept), deduction recovery FP&A: Owns forecast integration with plan, scenario design, and driver analytics Controller: Oversees reconciliations, posting accuracy, close governance, and SOX controls Cash Application Team: Reduces unapplied cash, improves auto‑match rates Sales/Operations: Provides pipeline, promotions, order/returns signals that affect inflows Dynamics 365 support Finance: Cash flow forecast and cash position workspaces; bank reconciliation; credit & collections (aging, pools, promises‑to‑pay, interest notes); business events for postings; Finance Insights cash flow forecasting (ML) Business Central: Cash flow forecast (assisted setup), payment reconciliation journals, reminders/finance charge memos, customer statements Power BI/Fabric: Unified semantic model, scorecards, variance bridges, bank vs. GL recon views, row‑level security Copilot for Finance: Narrative summaries of cash movements and variances, anomaly detection, suggested reconciliation and collections actions Power Automate: Bank file ingestion, alerting for threshold breaches (balances, covenants), and workflowed forecast changes Operational controls and compliance Bank account governance (open/close, signatories), dual approvals on wires/ACH, payment factory or centralized disbursement policies Forecast change control with audit trail; segregation of duties (setup, posting, approvals) Reconciliation SLAs and exception aging; retention and privacy controls for bank and customer data; SOX/IFRS/GAAP alignment for cash flow statements Inputs and outputs Inputs: GL and subledgers (AR/AP), bank statements/feeds, AR aging and promises, deductions and rebates, FX rates, debt/investment schedules, facilities and covenants, forecast drivers Outputs: Daily cash report; 13‑week and 12–18 month forecasts; variance bridges; covenant dashboard; FX exposure and hedge coverage; AR collections forecast; action plan with owners and due dates KPI target examples Forecast accuracy (13‑week inflows): ≥ 85–90% with decreasing bias Daily bank‑GL reconciliation: > 99% matching within 24 hours; exceptions aged DSO: steady reduction with > 90‑day bucket trending down; CEI ≥ target by segment Unapplied cash: Liquidity headroom: ≥ policy minimum (e.g., 1.5× next 4 weeks’ net outflows) If you want, I can turn this into: A one‑page “Daily Cash” report template A 13‑week cash forecast model (with driver inputs for AR timing, FX, and deductions) A Power BI scorecard with variance bridges and covenant headroom tracking

processes.title: Analyze customer risk
processes.description: Analyze customer risk quantifies exposure across your portfolio by continuously monitoring credit risk, flagging suspicious sales activity, and measuring detection/response effectiveness (e.g., average time to detect fraud) so leaders can protect revenue while minimizing false positives. Applies to Dynamics 365 Finance (credit management, blocking rules, hold list, bad-debt/write-off proposals) Dynamics 365 Commerce (POS exceptions, returns, check/charge abuse, channel/affiliate risk) Dynamics 365 Fraud Protection (purchase protection, account protection, loss prevention) Dynamics 365 Sales (account health, pipeline risk signals, seller behavior outliers) Dynamics 365 Business Central (credit limits, reminders/finance charges, customer blocking) Microsoft Fabric/Power BI (risk models, dashboards, alerting), Copilot for Finance/Customer Service (summaries, guided actions) Core risk indicators and definitions Credit exposure: credit utilization %, exposure at risk, past-due trend, delinquency transition rates (Current→30→60→90+), DSO movement, broken promise rate. Customer risk scoring: internal risk groups, probability-of-default score, behavioral segments (payment method, geography, tenure, channel). Fraud and abuse signals: suspicious order rate, chargeback rate, refund/return abuse rate, account takeover rate, duplicate/high-velocity order patterns, high-risk BIN/device/geo, payment decline loops, manual review rate, false positive rate. Speed and quality metrics: average time to detect fraud (MTTD), average time to respond/resolve (MTTR), percent of fraud blocked pre-authorization vs post-capture, investigation SLA adherence. Revenue impact ratios: fraud loss as % of revenue, dilution (returns/credits/allowances) %, net recovery rate on investigations, write-off/bad-debt ratio. High - level process Define risk model and thresholds Standardize credit and fraud KPI formulas, segment-specific thresholds, escalation criteria, and SoD-approved override limits. Publish a metric dictionary and governance cadence. Assemble trusted risk data Land AR aging/limits/holds, orders/POS receipts/returns, payment outcomes, fraud signals (device, IP, velocity, risk score), chargebacks, deductions, and seller/channel metadata into a governed model with conformed dimensions (customer, channel, product, region, payment type). Monitor credit risk daily Track utilization vs limit, delinquency transitions, DSO variance, broken promises, and impending limit expirations. Auto-build collector/watch lists and pre-emptive limit reviews for deteriorating segments. Detect suspicious sales activity in real time Evaluate orders against rules and ML scores for high-risk payment/geo/device/velocity patterns; route for step-up verification, block, or manual review; capture reasons and artifacts for audit. Triage and decide actions Investigators review claims, link orders, and payment evidence; choose actions: cancel order(s), place customer/order hold, step-up verification, partial fulfillment, or allow with monitoring. Document decisions and expected cash impact. Update credit posture Adjust credit limits/risk groups, apply or release customer/order holds, and schedule enhanced monitoring for recovered accounts. Synchronize changes to collections worklists and seller guidance. Communicate and coordinate Notify Sales/Customer Service of decisions with safe talking points; provide customers with next steps (re-verify payment, alternate tender, documentation). Measure detection and response Report MTTD/MTTR, pre- vs post-authorization block mix, false positives, approval rates, and downstream effects on conversion and CSAT; calibrate rules/models accordingly. Govern and improve Run weekly operational reviews and monthly model/rule councils; track drift, stability, and ROC/PR curves; test-and-learn on thresholds to reduce loss while preserving approval rates. Roles and responsibilities Credit Risk Manager: Owns credit policies, risk groups, limit frameworks, and hold/release governance. Fraud Operations Lead: Owns detection playbooks, investigation quality, escalation to payments/banks, and model/rule tuning backlog. Collections Manager: Aligns holds and promises-to-pay with risk posture; feeds payment behavior to risk scoring. Finance Controller: Ensures compliance, approves high-impact policy changes and write-offs; oversees auditability. Sales/Channel Operations: Executes seller guidance (e.g., require PO, alternate payment) and monitors partner/affiliate risk. Data & Analytics: Maintains semantic models, dashboards, alerts, backtests, and feature stores for risk models. Dynamics 365 support Finance: Credit management (risk groups, blocking/exclusion rules, centralized hold list, reasons), AR aging/promises, interest/fees, write-off proposals, business events for holds/letters/interest notes. Commerce: POS exception logging (voids/returns/overrides), call center check-holds, channel/affiliate/loyalty abuse patterns, suspended transactions, promo misuse analytics. Fraud Protection: Real-time risk scores, rules/velocity checks, device fingerprinting, chargeback insights, decision rationale, and case management integration. Sales: Account health views, unusual order patterns by rep/territory, win/loss anomalies tied to unusual discounts/terms. Business Central: Credit limits, reminders/finance charges, customer blocking, and dunning integration. Power BI/Fabric: Portfolio risk dashboards, early-warning lists, MTTD/MTTR trackers, false-positive/negative analysis, and executive scorecards. Copilot: Narrative risk summaries, anomaly explanations, suggested next-best actions (e.g., step-up verification, hold release), and investigator call/email drafting. Operational controls and governance Policy controls: Written criteria for blocks, cancellations, step-up verification, and hold durations; regional variations (e.g., SCA/PSD2) and PCI DSS alignment. Segregation of duties: Separate configuration of rules/limits from investigation and from approval/release actions; dual control on limit increases and mass releases. Auditability: Persist risk scores, rule hits, artifacts (device/IP/payment), decision reasons, and approver identity; retain timelines for legal and card-network disputes. Privacy/retention: Minimize and protect PII/payment data; enforce retention schedules and access controls by role and geography. Inputs and outputs Inputs: AR aging and limits, orders/POS, payment authorization/settlement results, chargebacks/NSFs, returns/credits/allowances, device/IP/geo telemetry, customer master/segments, seller/channel metadata. Outputs: Risk dashboards and alerts, prioritized investigation queues, hold/cancel/step-up decisions, limit changes, seller guidance, weekly ops packs, and monthly loss/approval/false-positive scorecards. processes.title: Monitor customer credit risk scores in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: Analyze customer risk quantifies exposure across your portfolio by continuously monitoring credit risk, flagging suspicious sales activity, and measuring detection/response effectiveness (e.g., average time to detect fraud) so leaders can protect revenue while minimizing false positives. Applies to * Dynamics 365 Finance (credit management, blocking rules, hold list, bad-debt/write-off proposals) * Dynamics 365 Commerce (POS exceptions, returns, check/charge abuse, channel/affiliate risk) * Dynamics 365 Fraud Protection (purchase protection, account protection, loss prevention) * Dynamics 365 Sales (account health, pipeline risk signals, seller behavior outliers) * Dynamics 365 Business Central (credit limits, reminders/finance charges, customer blocking) * Microsoft Fabric/Power BI (risk models, dashboards, alerting), Copilot for Finance/Customer Service (summaries, guided actions) Core risk indicators and definitions * Credit exposure: credit utilization %, exposure at risk, past-due trend, delinquency transition rates (Current→30→60→90+), DSO movement, broken promise rate. * Customer risk scoring: internal risk groups, probability-of-default score, behavioral segments (payment method, geography, tenure, channel). * Fraud and abuse signals: suspicious order rate, chargeback rate, refund/return abuse rate, account takeover rate, duplicate/high-velocity order patterns, high-risk BIN/device/geo, payment decline loops, manual review rate, false positive rate. * Speed and quality metrics: average time to detect fraud (MTTD), average time to respond/resolve (MTTR), percent of fraud blocked pre-authorization vs post-capture, investigation SLA adherence. * Revenue impact ratios: fraud loss as % of revenue, dilution (returns/credits/allowances) %, net recovery rate on investigations, write-off/bad-debt ratio. High - level process 1. Define risk model and thresholds * Standardize credit and fraud KPI formulas, segment-specific thresholds, escalation criteria, and SoD-approved override limits. Publish a metric dictionary and governance cadence. 2. Assemble trusted risk data * Land AR aging/limits/holds, orders/POS receipts/returns, payment outcomes, fraud signals (device, IP, velocity, risk score), chargebacks, deductions, and seller/channel metadata into a governed model with conformed dimensions (customer, channel, product, region, payment type). 3. Monitor credit risk daily * Track utilization vs limit, delinquency transitions, DSO variance, broken promises, and impending limit expirations. Auto-build collector/watch lists and pre-emptive limit reviews for deteriorating segments. 4. Detect suspicious sales activity in real time * Evaluate orders against rules and ML scores for high-risk payment/geo/device/velocity patterns; route for step-up verification, block, or manual review; capture reasons and artifacts for audit. 5. Triage and decide actions * Investigators review claims, link orders, and payment evidence; choose actions: cancel order(s), place customer/order hold, step-up verification, partial fulfillment, or allow with monitoring. Document decisions and expected cash impact. 6. Update credit posture * Adjust credit limits/risk groups, apply or release customer/order holds, and schedule enhanced monitoring for recovered accounts. Synchronize changes to collections worklists and seller guidance. 7. Communicate and coordinate * Notify Sales/Customer Service of decisions with safe talking points; provide customers with next steps (re-verify payment, alternate tender, documentation). 8. Measure detection and response * Report MTTD/MTTR, pre- vs post-authorization block mix, false positives, approval rates, and downstream effects on conversion and CSAT; calibrate rules/models accordingly. 9. Govern and improve * Run weekly operational reviews and monthly model/rule councils; track drift, stability, and ROC/PR curves; test-and-learn on thresholds to reduce loss while preserving approval rates. Roles and responsibilities * Credit Risk Manager: Owns credit policies, risk groups, limit frameworks, and hold/release governance. * Fraud Operations Lead: Owns detection playbooks, investigation quality, escalation to payments/banks, and model/rule tuning backlog. * Collections Manager: Aligns holds and promises-to-pay with risk posture; feeds payment behavior to risk scoring. * Finance Controller: Ensures compliance, approves high-impact policy changes and write-offs; oversees auditability. * Sales/Channel Operations: Executes seller guidance (e.g., require PO, alternate payment) and monitors partner/affiliate risk. * Data & Analytics: Maintains semantic models, dashboards, alerts, backtests, and feature stores for risk models. Dynamics 365 support * Finance: Credit management (risk groups, blocking/exclusion rules, centralized hold list, reasons), AR aging/promises, interest/fees, write-off proposals, business events for holds/letters/interest notes. * Commerce: POS exception logging (voids/returns/overrides), call center check-holds, channel/affiliate/loyalty abuse patterns, suspended transactions, promo misuse analytics. * Fraud Protection: Real-time risk scores, rules/velocity checks, device fingerprinting, chargeback insights, decision rationale, and case management integration. * Sales: Account health views, unusual order patterns by rep/territory, win/loss anomalies tied to unusual discounts/terms. * Business Central: Credit limits, reminders/finance charges, customer blocking, and dunning integration. * Power BI/Fabric: Portfolio risk dashboards, early-warning lists, MTTD/MTTR trackers, false-positive/negative analysis, and executive scorecards. * Copilot: Narrative risk summaries, anomaly explanations, suggested next-best actions (e.g., step-up verification, hold release), and investigator call/email drafting. Operational controls and governance * Policy controls: Written criteria for blocks, cancellations, step-up verification, and hold durations; regional variations (e.g., SCA/PSD2) and PCI DSS alignment. * Segregation of duties: Separate configuration of rules/limits from investigation and from approval/release actions; dual control on limit increases and mass releases. * Auditability: Persist risk scores, rule hits, artifacts (device/IP/payment), decision reasons, and approver identity; retain timelines for legal and card-network disputes. * Privacy/retention: Minimize and protect PII/payment data; enforce retention schedules and access controls by role and geography. Inputs and outputs * Inputs: AR aging and limits, orders/POS, payment authorization/settlement results, chargebacks/NSFs, returns/credits/allowances, device/IP/geo telemetry, customer master/segments, seller/channel metadata. * Outputs: Risk dashboards and alerts, prioritized investigation queues, hold/cancel/step-up decisions, limit changes, seller guidance, weekly ops packs, and monthly loss/approval/false-positive scorecards. KPIs and target examples * Credit exposure: % high-risk balance; delinquency transition rate trending down; DSO change within target band. * Fraud performance: Average time to detect fraud (MTTD) and average time to respond (MTTR) decreasing; chargeback rate ≤ target; fraud loss as % revenue decreasing. * Decision quality: False-positive rate ≤ target; approval rate maintained or improved in low-risk segments; percent blocked pre-authorization increasing with stable conversion. * Operational efficiency: Investigation SLA hit rate; average time to release legitimate holds; case re-open rate; rules/model drift within control limits.

processes.title: Analyze revenue
processes.description: Analyze revenue delivers a governed, end‑to‑end view of revenue performance and predictability—covering totals, mix, recurring revenue health, growth trends, forecasts, and variances—so leaders can act quickly to protect margins and accelerate durable growth Applies to : Dynamics 365 Finance, Business Central, Sales, Commerce, Project Operations, Subscription Billing; Microsoft Fabric and Power BI for models and scorecards; Copilot (narratives, anomaly detection, next‑best actions) Typical dimensions (slicers): Time (day/week/month/quarter/fiscal), Product/Service/SKU, Category/Family, Customer/Account/Segment, Channel (POS/e‑commerce/call center/direct/partner), Region/Country/Currency, Sales org/Rep/Territory/Partner, Project/Contract/Subscription/Plan, Campaign/Promotion, Industry Typical revenue types: Booked, Billed (invoiced), Recognized (IFRS 15/ASC 606), Recurring (MRR/ARR), One‑time, Usage/Consumption, Services (T&M/fixed fee), Deferred/Unbilled, Backlog/RPO Bold section headers requested below Core KPIs and definitions Total revenue and revenue mix: total recognized revenue; mix by product/service, category, channel, region, customer segment, and seller. Revenue growth: YoY, QoQ, 3/12‑month rolling growth, organic vs. FX‑neutral growth, like‑for‑like/comparable sales. Revenue by product or service: SKU/family/portfolio performance; attach/cross‑sell rates; promo lift vs. baseline. Category analysis: category contribution, margin mix shift, price/volume/mix decomposition. Customer revenue: top‑N concentration, share‑of‑wallet, expansion/contraction, cohort retention revenue. Recurring revenue: MRR, ARR, net dollar retention (NDR), gross retention, expansion/contraction/churn revenue, logo churn, renewals due/past‑due, average revenue per account (ARPA/ARPU). Forecast and pipeline: in‑period revenue forecast; sales‑to‑revenue conversion; coverage ratios; backlog/RPO burn. Forecast quality: MAPE, bias (over/under), hit‑rate by segment/channel/product; forecast vs. plan/commit. Variance to forecast/plan: volume, price, mix, timing/recognition, returns/credits/rebates, delivery slippage, FX, accounting reclassifications. Returns/credits/rebates and trade allowances: gross‑to‑net waterfall, accrual accuracy, claim aging, deduction recovery rate. Profitability tie‑ins: gross margin %, contribution margin, promo ROI, discount leakage. Standard reports and scorecards Executive revenue scorecard: totals, growth, mix, forecast vs. plan, variance bridge with drivers. Revenue by product/service: hierarchy drill (portfolio → family → SKU) with price/volume/mix and promo impact. Customer revenue and retention: top customer trends, cohort curves, NDR/gross retention, churn and reactivation. Recurring revenue dashboard: MRR/ARR waterfall (new, expansion, contraction, churn), renewals runway. Channel/POS revenue: store/region conversion, UPT, tender mix, returns/voids, promo uplift. Bookings–Billings–Backlog/RPO view: conversion cadence and risk flags. Forecast quality pack: MAPE, bias, funnel conversion, aging of forecast changes. Gross‑to‑net revenue waterfall: list price → discounts → rebates/trade allowances → returns → net revenue. FX and multi‑currency views: constant‑currency restatements and FX variance bridges. High‑level process Define metrics and targets Publish a metric dictionary (formulas for revenue, growth, MRR/ARR, NDR, MAPE, variance drivers); set targets by segment/channel/product; lock fiscal calendars and currency policies (spot vs. average vs. constant). Assemble the trusted revenue model Land sales orders, invoices, revenue schedules, returns/credits, rebates/trade allowances, subscription events, backlog/RPO, pipeline, and POS receipts; harmonize dimensions and currencies; stamp revenue recognition attributes and FX basis. Produce baselines and gross‑to‑net Reconcile booked→billed→recognized; build gross‑to‑net waterfalls; validate deferred/unbilled schedules; ensure accruals for rebates/allowances are complete. Monitor totals, mix, and growth Track total revenue and growth; analyze price/volume/mix and category shifts; surface concentration risk and margin‑dilutive patterns. Analyze revenue by product/service, category, channel, and customer Drill to SKU/category; review promo effects; evaluate channel and customer segment performance; tie outcomes to assortment, pricing, and fulfillment signals. Assess recurring revenue health Generate MRR/ARR and cohort views; calculate NDR/gross retention; quantify expansion/contraction; track renewal pipeline and churn drivers. Build and reconcile revenue forecasts Combine opportunity pipeline and rev‑rec rules (for projects/subscriptions) with statistical/time‑series and driver‑based models; generate scenario cases (base, upside, downside). Explain variance to forecast/plan Produce bridges with standardized drivers (volume, price, mix, timing/recognition, returns/credits/rebates, delivery slippage, FX); separate one‑offs from run‑rate. Recommend and track actions Propose pricing/promo adjustments, portfolio actions, renewal saves, deduction cleanup, and delivery de‑bottlenecking; assign owners, due dates, and expected impact; close the loop. Govern and continuously improve Run weekly operational and monthly business reviews; monitor forecast accuracy/bias; refine models, dimensions, and policy settings; update the metric dictionary as changes are approved. Roles and responsibilities Revenue/Sales Finance: Owns revenue policy adherence, forecast, variance analysis, gross‑to‑net integrity. Sales Operations/RevOps: Maintains pipeline hygiene, conversion analytics, quota/coverage modeling. Product/Commercial: Acts on category and price/pack architecture insights; manages promo ROI. Subscription/Billing Operations: Owns MRR/ARR, renewals, proration, and contract changes. Order Management/Fulfillment: Addresses timing and delivery drivers behind revenue variance. Accounting/Controller: Ensures rev‑rec compliance, FX policy, adjustments, and close governance. Data & Analytics: Curates semantic models, scorecards, row‑level security, alerting, and model MLOps. Dynamics 365 support Finance and Business Central: Revenue recognition schedules, invoicing, returns/credits, rebates/trade allowances, deferred/unbilled revenue, multi‑currency, bank and GL reconciliation, standard P&L/by‑dimension reports. Sales: Pipeline to revenue conversion, forecast categories, win/loss and discount analytics feeding forecast. Commerce/POS: Store/channel revenue, conversion and UPT, promo uplift, refunds/voids exception analytics. Project Operations: Milestone‑ and percentage‑of‑completion‑based rev‑rec for services. Subscription Billing: Plans, proration, amendments, renewals; MRR/ARR, NDR calculation support. Finance Insights, Power BI, Fabric: Forecast models, scorecards, variance bridges, constant‑currency views; automated refresh and alerting. Copilot: Narrative summaries (“what changed and why”), anomaly detection, suggested actions (e.g., price/mix changes, renewal saves), auto‑drafted exec notes. Operational controls and governance Policy compliance: IFRS 15/ASC 606 frameworks for recognition; approval workflows for manual adjustments; documented FX treatment. Metric governance: Versioned metric dictionary; change control for KPI formulas and targets. Data quality & access: Master data stewardship, duplicate prevention, revenue cutoff checks; role‑based security and audit trails. Period close integrity: Reconciliation between subledgers and GL, lock periods, reproducible snapshots for “as‑of” reporting. Key inputs and outputs Inputs: Sales orders/opportunities, invoices/credit memos, revenue schedules, returns/allowances/rebates, subscription events, POS receipts, backlog/RPO, FX rates, promo calendars. Outputs: Executive revenue scorecards, product/category/channel/customer reports, recurring revenue dashboard, bookings–billings–backlog/RPO, forecast packs with bridges, constant‑currency views, gross‑to‑net waterfall, action register with owners/impact. KPI target examples (illustrative) Revenue growth: ≥ plan with ±2% tolerance; FX‑neutral growth tracked separately. Forecast accuracy (MAPE): ≥ 85–90% at portfolio level; bias within ±3%. Net dollar retention: ≥ 110% for target subscription cohorts; gross retention ≥ 95%. Gross‑to‑net leakage: Stable or improving; deduction aging >90 days trending down. Promo ROI: Positive lift without margin erosion in priority categories.

processes.title: Analyze order management processes
processes.description: Analyze order management processes provides a governed, end-to-end view of order health and flow—measuring sales cycle length, order status, order cycle time, order accuracy, backlog, cancellations/changes, and monitoring returns and refunds—so leaders can remove bottlenecks, protect revenue, and improve customer experience. Applies to: Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, Intelligent Order Management, Commerce (POS and call center), Sales, Finance, Business Central, Microsoft Fabric/Power BI, and Copilot. Typical analysis dimensions: time period; order type (B2B, B2C, subscription, project); channel (eCommerce, POS, call center, sales order); customer/segment/region; product/SKU/category; fulfillment site/warehouse/carrier; priority/service level; payment/terms; sales rep/team/partner. Components Data foundation: harmonized order lifecycle events (create, promise, release, pick, pack, ship, deliver, invoice), holds/exceptions, changes/cancellations, returns/RMAs, refunds/chargebacks, credit checks, and inventory/ATP signals. Target outcomes: shorter cycle time and lead-times; higher perfect-order rate; lower backlog and aging; fewer changes/cancellations; reduced returns/refunds; accurate EDD (expected delivery date); higher first-time-right invoicing; predictable cash conversion. Governance: a single metric dictionary; standardized event timestamps; clear SLAs for each step; exception taxonomies; role-based access and auditability. Copilot/agent support: narrative summaries, anomaly detection, next-best-actions for order exceptions, auto-drafted customer updates (e.g., EDD changes), and hold-release guidance. Standard workspaces and reports: Order status & aging dashboard; Perfect order scorecard; Backlog & backorder heatmap; Change/cancellation tracker; Hold list & root-cause; Returns & refunds analytics; EDD accuracy & promise adherence; Pick/pack/ship cycle monitor; Invoice accuracy and fallout. Adjacent signal tie-ins: credit risk/holds, fraud or suspicious activity, capacity constraints, pricing/promotions, and returns/refund policies. Continuous improvement loop: identify variance; diagnose root cause; implement actions; measure impact; update playbooks. Success measures: faster cycle time and EDD accuracy; improved perfect-order rate; reduced >X-day backlog; lower return/refund ratios; fewer order changes; fewer invoice defects; higher customer satisfaction; stable revenue conversion. Risks to manage: incomplete timestamps, inconsistent status taxonomies, siloed channel data, unmanaged exception queues, EDI/API error leakage, and over-zealous holds creating churn. Security & compliance: SoD for order changes, hold releases, refunds; audit logs; protection for PII/payment data; retention policies. Operating cadence: daily ops huddles for exceptions; weekly backlog/aging review; monthly policy/playbook adjustments. Implementation tips: begin with a minimal metric set and a reliable event model; fix timestamp quality; use a standard order-state machine; pair dashboards with action queues; publish a metric dictionary. Handoff & ownership model: data ops curates the model; order management leads the queue; sales ops/CS own customer comms; warehouse/transport own physical flow; finance owns invoicing accuracy. Core KPIs and definitions Sales cycle length: time from quote/OPP-to-order (optionally include lead-to-order); or from order-created-to-confirmed. Order cycle time (OCT): order-created to delivered (and sub-cycle times: create→release, release→pick, pick→pack, pack→ship, ship→deliver, deliver→invoice). Order status distribution: open, on hold (credit, fraud, check, manual), released, picking, packed, shipped, delivered, invoiced, closed; percent by status and aging. Order accuracy / perfect order rate: delivered on time, in full, damage-free, correct documentation (label, ASN, invoice). EDD accuracy / promise adherence: actual vs promised delivery; early/late variance. Backlog and backorder: count/value; aging; at-risk orders; capacity/inventory drivers. Cancellation/change rate: percent of orders/lines changed or canceled; reasons (price, availability, lead-time, address, payment). First-time-right invoicing: invoice error rate; credit/rebill rate; EDI failure rate. Return/refund metrics: return rate (% of orders/lines); RMA reasons; refund rate; return cycle time; chargeback/NSF incidence. Hold efficiency: time-to-release; repeat holds; false-positive holds; capacity vs risk-based holds. Fill rate: line-level and order-level; partial-fill incidence. Cost to serve per order: handling, shipping, exceptions/rework. Throughput and capacity: orders per day, pick/pack/ship capacity; labor/slotting constraints. Standard reports and workspaces Order status & aging dashboard with drilldowns by channel, customer, SKU, site. Backlog and backorder heatmap with risk-based prioritization. Perfect order scorecard and EDD adherence tracker. Change/cancellation and reason code analysis. Holds queue (credit/fraud/check/manual) with time-to-release and reason analytics. Returns/RMAs/refunds dashboard with reason and time-to-refund. Pick/pack/ship cycle monitor with warehouse bottleneck analysis. Invoice accuracy and fallout tracking (credit/rebill, EDI rejects). High‑level process Define metrics and thresholds Publish a metric dictionary (cycle definitions, perfect order rules, EDD tolerance, backlog aging bands, return reasons). Set targets/thresholds by channel, segment, and product class. Assemble a trusted event model Land harmonized order lifecycle events, exceptions/holds, changes/cancellations, RMAs/refunds, and invoicing events. Conform dimensions (customer, product, channel, site, carrier) and time/calendar. Instrument milestones and EDD logic Ensure create/confirm/release/pick/pack/ship/deliver/invoice timestamps. Capture promise dates and updates; store reason codes for changes/holds/returns. Build scorecards and action queues Pair dashboards with prioritized exception queues (aging backlog, at-risk EDD, long-running holds, repeat fallouts). Monitor sales cycle length and intake velocity Track order intake vs plan; cycle length by channel/segment; identify demand spikes vs capacity. Analyze order status and aging Identify stalled states; quantify time in state; segment by hold reason, site, carrier, SKU class. Measure order accuracy and fallout Calculate perfect order; track pick/pack/ship/invoice errors; link to training, slotting, or content issues. Inspect backlog and capacity constraints Tie backlog aging to ATP/CTP, supplier lead-times, WMS capacity, and carrier performance; simulate relief options. Monitor returns and refunds Trend return/refund rates and reasons; separate quality vs expectation vs size/color/fit vs damage; track refund timeliness. Diagnose exceptions and control efficacy Review hold false-positives; EDD misses vs early ships; invoice fallouts; EDI/API failures; define preventive controls. Recommend and track actions Inventory reallocation, expediting, alternative carriers, slotting changes, schedule/labor plans, address validation, credit policy tweaks, proactive customer comms. Close the loop Measure impact; update targets and playbooks (e.g., backorder comms, hold release criteria, pack validation). Roles and responsibilities Order Management Lead: owns flow policy, backlog risk, and playbooks. Sales Operations: owns intake quality and customer comms for changes/EDDs. Warehouse/Logistics: owns pick/pack/ship performance, carrier SLAs. Customer Service/Call Center: owns holds/returns/refunds communication and experience. Credit & Risk: owns hold criteria and release SLAs (credit/fraud). Finance/AR: owns invoicing accuracy and credit/rebill governance. Data & Analytics: owns models, dashboards, alerts, and metric dictionary. Dynamics 365 product support Supply Chain Management: sales order management, ATP/CTP, order holds, WMS, shipment, carrier integration, invoicing. Intelligent Order Management: orchestration, multi-node allocation, exception management, rule-based rerouting. Commerce: POS and call center orders, suspended transactions, returns/exchanges. Sales: order capture, quote-to-order conversion, seller attribution. Finance/Business Central: invoicing, credit/rebill, returns/credit memos, reminders. Copilot: anomaly summaries, next-best-actions for holds/EDD misses/refunds; auto-drafted customer updates. Power BI/Fabric: unified semantic model, scorecards, alerts, and drill-through to transaction/event detail. Operational controls SLAs: promise adherence, time-in-state, hold-release, refund timelines. Approvals: order changes, cancellations, refunds, credit/rebill, rush/expedite. SoD: between order entry, pricing overrides, hold releases, and refunds. Auditability: timestamp integrity, reason codes, approval trails. Data quality: address and item master validation, EDI/API retry governance. Inputs and outputs Inputs: order master and events; holds/exceptions; changes/cancellations; WMS events; carrier events; returns/RMAs/refunds; invoicing/credit note events; capacity calendars; ATP/CTP. Outputs: status/aging dashboards; perfect order scorecards; backlog and EDD risk queues; returns/refund reporting; hold-efficiency analytics; action registers with owners and due dates. KPI target examples Order cycle time: −10–20% vs baseline by channel/segment. Perfect order rate: ≥ 95% (with channel-specific thresholds). EDD accuracy: ≥ 97% on-time promise adherence; Backlog aging > X days: ↓ by 30–50% for priority SKUs/customers. Return/refund rate: channel/category-targeted reductions with no CSAT erosion. Invoice first-time-right: ≥ 98–99%; EDI reject rate Hold time-to-release: median

processes.title: Manage credit and collections
processes.description: In many organizations, not least organizations with a business-to-business sales model, setting credit limits is an important process that helps organizations remain competitive. Credit limits can also help an organization minimize bad debt and the need to write off unpaid balances. When you manage the collection process carefully, it helps you get customers pay on time, increases the cash flow, and helps make the cash flow of the organization more predictable. The process for monitoring customer credit and collections often splits into two main focuses in a Dynamics 365 project: The first is around the master data configuration of your customers and the establishment of the credit limits, payment terms, and so on, for your customers. The second is the monitoring of orders and invoices for your customers to ensure that customers remain within their credit limits and rules your business has established to ensure that you can reduce the risk for fraudulent orders and accounts. Dynamics 365 Finance includes functionality to help you manage your customer master data including establishing credit limits, credit scores, and so on. The Finance app can also help you monitor orders for fraudulent activity, reconcile the credit limits to the customers' balances, and place orders or customers on hold based on your business rules. Large retailers, not least retailers that primarily do business online with consumers, typically have credit or fraud departments that monitor sales for fraudulent activity. Dynamics 365 Fraud Protection includes functionality to help customers manage fraud in three key pillars including account protection, loss prevention, and purchase protection. Fraud Protection uses artificial intelligence (AI) to help protect your business from fraud.

processes.title: Assess customer credit risk
processes.description: The Assess Customer Credit Risk business process defines how organizations evaluate the financial reliability of customers before extending or adjusting credit. This process mitigates risk, protects revenue, and enforces internal credit and collections policies. Core Components Identify Credit Risk Factors Evaluate payment history, open receivables, exposure across legal entities, industry risk, external ratings/scores, and customer disputes. Analyze Customer Credit Data Use internal AR aging, credit limit usage, risk groups/classes, and external bureau data to determine creditworthiness; leverage scoring models and thresholds. Implement Fraud and Abuse Checks Apply fraud detection for account takeover, purchase risk, and velocity anomalies; route suspicious accounts or orders for manual review to avoid credit misuse. Set Initial Credit Limits and Terms Establish customer-specific limits, terms of payment, and grace rules based on risk analysis, business policy, and segment/channel needs. Configure Blocking Rules and Exceptions Define credit management blocking and exclusion rules to automatically stop orders that exceed limits or violate policy; document exception paths and approvals. Revise Assessment Reassess periodically (e.g., monthly/quarterly) or on triggers (DSO spikes, limit utilization, disputes, external rating changes) and adjust limits/terms accordingly. Process Flow Identify Risk Factors Gather financial and behavioral data, including payment history, open receivables, exposure, industry risk, and external ratings or scores. Analyze Credit Data Use internal aging reports, credit limit usage, and external bureau data to determine creditworthiness. Apply scoring models and thresholds to classify risk. Implement Fraud and Abuse Checks Apply fraud detection tools to identify suspicious activity, such as account takeover or unusual purchase patterns, and route flagged cases for manual review. Set Initial Credit Limits and Terms Establish customer-specific credit limits and payment terms based on risk analysis and business policy. Define grace periods and exception rules. Configure Blocking Rules and Exceptions Set up credit management blocking rules to stop orders that exceed limits or violate policy. Document exception paths and approval workflows. Approve Credit Terms Credit Manager proposes limits and terms. Finance Controller reviews for compliance and approves decisions. Notify Sales and Customer Service of final terms. Enforce and Monitor Apply blocking rules to sales orders when thresholds are met. Monitor alerts and hold queues, and manage releases or escalations according to policy. Review and Revise Reassess credit profiles periodically or when triggered by events such as overdue balances, disputes, or changes in external ratings. Adjust limits and terms as needed. Stakeholders Credit Manager Owns risk evaluation, scoring models, and limit setting; manages credit hold releases and exception governance. Finance Controller Ensures compliance with financial and audit policies; approves higher-risk decisions and policy changes. Sales Operations Analyst Aligns credit terms with sales strategy; communicates decisions and monitors impact on order flow. Customer Service/Call Center Lead Manages order holds communication with customers; coordinates documentation needed for releases. Risk/Fraud Analyst (as applicable) Designs fraud rules and reviews suspicious accounts/orders; collaborates with Credit on holistic risk posture. Dynamics 365 Support Dynamics 365 Finance (Credit management) Risk groups and scoring; customer credit limits; blocking and exclusion rules; centralized hold list across legal entities; release reason codes; approvals and audit trails. Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Sales order holds (manual and rule-driven) that prevent picking/packing/invoicing until credit issues are resolved; integration with Finance credit checks. Dynamics 365 Commerce (Call Center/POS) Check/credit-payment holds and Credit Limit Workbench for call center orders; POS transaction suspension for temporary holds; can combine with credit checks. processes.title: Manually set credit limits in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: When your organization does business with other businesses or has frequent repeat buyers, you might extend a certain amount of credit to the customer with payment terms as part of your customer agreement. You can define credit limits for your customers and check the credit limit when you process transactions such as free text invoices, sales order invoices, or sales order packing slips, for example. Credit limits help reduce the amount of unpaid balance a customer can have with your organization at a given time. Use this pattern when: Your business process requires a basic warning or error message on all documents for a sales order or free text invoice. You only have one credit limit per customer and no groups of customers have a credit limit defined. This pattern might not be suitable: You have multiple legal entities with the same customer in more than one legal entity that needs to share a credit limit. You have multiple customer accounts in a single legal entity that are the same logical organization or need the same credit limit. You use a call center to manage sales orders and are using the Credit limit page to manage customers that are exceeding their credit limit available in the Retail and commerce module. You require more robust rules for checking credit limits. For example, checking credit limits on release to warehouse, checking on pro-forma documents, allowing days of grace for credit limit checks on certain documents.

processes.title: Manage customer holds
processes.description: Manage customer holds governs the account-level blocking of a customer’s ability to transact—placing new orders, receiving shipments, or being invoiced—whenever risk, credit, or compliance conditions warrant a pause. The process standardizes when and how holds are applied, communicated, reviewed, and released so you can protect revenue, ensure policy and regulatory compliance, and minimize operational leakage across all channels. This process focuses on customer-level holds, not individual sales order holds. An account hold prevents new commercial activity across connected channels until remediation is complete. Typical triggers include persistent past-due balances, an expired or insufficient credit limit, repeated NSF or chargebacks, unresolved disputes, fraud or abuse indicators, and onboarding or KYC documentation gaps. Hold types Credit or policy holds are used when a customer’s credit posture requires reassessment or when policy thresholds have been breached. Manual administrative holds are applied for legal or exceptional situations (for example, litigation, tax certificate review, ownership changes) and are released only by authorized approvers. Workflow-driven holds are initiated by rules (such as “pending credit review” or “missing documentation”) and proceed through an approval workflow to ensure traceability and segregation of duties. High‑level process 1) Identify candidates for hold by monitoring aging, credit limit status, dispute and NSF history, fraud signals, and compliance flags. Compile a candidate list with the supporting evidence and current exposure. 2) Select the hold type and scope. Record the reason code, effective date, intended scope (entire customer account and related entities, if applicable), and the initial review window. 3) Apply the hold and notify stakeholders. Place the hold at the customer account level and alert Sales, Customer Service, Order Management, and Collections, including clear guidance for acceptable customer communications. 4) Enforce the hold across channels and systems. Confirm that eCommerce, POS/call center, and order capture engines respect the account block to prevent order entry, shipment, and invoicing while the hold is active. 5) Investigate and remediate. Collections and Credit partner with the customer to clear past‑due balances, establish payment plans, resolve disputes, or collect compliance documentation. Capture notes, promises, and target dates. 6) Review and release. When remediation criteria are met, run the approval workflow to remove the hold. Document the decision, rationale, approvers, and timestamps, then restore normal processing. 7) Audit and improve. Retain reason codes, timelines, and outcome metrics. Analyze false positives, recurrence, and time‑to‑release to refine policies, thresholds, and training. Roles and responsibilities The Credit Manager owns policy thresholds, exception governance, and approval standards for high‑risk releases. Collections Specialists lead remediation plans, customer communications, and documentation of outcomes. Sales or the Account Owner coordinates relationship‑sensitive messaging and aligns commercial commitments to the remediation plan. The Finance Controller or Compliance function ensures adherence to accounting, legal, and regulatory policies and approves sensitive or legally driven holds. Dynamics 365 product support In Dynamics 365 Finance, credit management policies, workflows, reason codes, and customer account settings enable account‑level blocking and governed release. Centralized visibility for order‑level credit holds exists as a separate, complementary process; keeping account‑level holds distinct avoids leakage and clarifies ownership. In Dynamics 365 Business Central, customer blocking codes, reminders, finance charge memos, and approval workflows provide account blocking and controlled release, with statements and finance charges supporting remediation. Copilot and collections workspaces can surface at‑risk accounts, propose next steps, and accelerate documentation. Operational controls and KPIs Policy controls should define hold reasons, durations, release authority, escalation paths, and regional legal variations. Segregation of duties separates the ability to apply or override holds from order entry and invoicing, with workflowed approval for releases. Key measures include the number of accounts on hold, revenue at risk, median time to release, recurrence rate, false‑positive rate, and audit pass rate. Improving these metrics typically comes from sharper trigger thresholds, clearer playbooks, and better cross‑team communication. Inputs and outputs Inputs include aging snapshots, credit limit status and expiry, disputes and NSF history, fraud or sanctions alerts, and onboarding or compliance status. Outputs include the applied hold (with reason codes), stakeholder notifications, approval audit logs, release decisions, and synchronized status updates across channels. Implementation notes Keep account‑level hold logic separate from sales‑order hold rules to avoid conflicting decisions and to target remediation at the right level. Standardize reason codes, review cadences, and approval workflows to strengthen traceability. Ensure hold status is visible in collections and sales workspaces so teams can move quickly to remediation without creating customer friction.

processes.title: Manually place a customer on hold in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: Credit and collections > Setup> Credit management setup > Account statuses We can create account statuses to identify the credit standing of a customer account. We can define a status and its effect on the invoicing and delivery on-hold processes. Account statuses can also be used to determine blocking rules for a customer Pay attention to the Invoice and delivery on hold field. There are several options: No – Customer is not blocked with any transactions. Invoice – Customer is blocked with posting picking lists, packing slips, invoices, including free text invoices All – Customer is blocked with posting all transaction types, including free text invoices, customer invoices, and payments. Payment – Invalid option for customer. Requisition – Invalid option for customer. Never – Customer is never put on hold for inactivity. In Accounts receivable, after opening the Customer account, navigate to Credit and collections > Invoicing and delivery on hold. We can create custom Order hold codes by navigating to Sales & marketing > Setup > Sales orders > Order code holds. Navigate to Credit and collections > Setup > Credit and collections parameters > Credit

processes.title: Monitor customer credit
processes.description: This process monitors ongoing customer credit exposure after credit has been granted, ensuring timely collections, proactive risk mitigation, and adherence to credit and collections policies. This process includes aging analysis, automated dunning (collection letters), handling returned/NSF payments, managing holds, and using Copilot/agent capabilities to prioritize outreach and accelerate cash collection. Applies to Dynamics 365 Finance, Dynamics 365 Business Central Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management and Commerce (order holds visibility) Microsoft Copilot for Finance and collections agents Power BI (credit and collections analytics) Core components Credit exposure monitoring: AR aging, limit utilization, overdue trends, promised-to-pay status Dunning and collection letters: reminder cycles, interest/fees, multi-level templates and schedules Returned/NSF payments: reversal of application, re-open invoices, assess fees, re-initiate collections Holds management: credit/fraud/order-level holds and release workflows Copilot/agents for collections: prioritize worklists, draft emails/letters, propose plans, summarize calls, schedule follow-ups Dispute and promise-to-pay tracking: reasons, due dates, escalations Analytics and alerts: dashboards for high-risk customers, expiring credit limits, broken promises, NSF rates High-level process flow Monitor exposure and signals Refresh AR aging and credit dashboards; track limit utilization, delinquency buckets, and high-risk segments. Surface customers with broken promises-to-pay, expiring limits, rapid balance growth, or repeated failed/NSF payments. Prioritize the collections worklist Rank customers and invoices by risk, amount, days past due, and likelihood-to-pay. Allocate accounts to collectors based on territory/segment, with clear SLAs. Execute dunning (collection letters) Generate the appropriate collection letter level (e.g., gentle reminder, formal notice, final notice) based on policy and days overdue. Include open invoices, due amounts, payment options, fees/interest (if applicable), and contact instructions. Dispatch via configured channels (email, print/mail) and log the activity on the customer and transactions. Engage customers and record outcomes Reach out via email/phone; capture notes, disputes, and promises-to-pay with dates and amounts. If a dispute is raised, create a case/work item and suspend dunning on disputed lines per policy. Handle returned/NSF payments When a payment is returned (e.g., NSF, ACH return, chargeback), reverse the payment application and re-open the affected invoices. Post NSF/return fees and interest (if your policy applies), and notify the customer with an updated statement or dunning letter. Evaluate temporary order/customer holds and stricter terms (e.g., prepayment) until the account stabilizes. Apply/adjust holds as needed For customers exceeding limits or with severe delinquency, apply customer-level or order-level holds per policy. Use defined release workflows and reason codes; document approvals and communications. Approve and set payment plans (when appropriate) Offer structured payment plans to viable customers; set schedules, due dates, and any conditional holds. Link plans to invoices; monitor adherence and auto-escalate when missed. Leverage Copilot/agent capabilities for collections Let Copilot prioritize the day’s worklist (highest impact customers/invoices) and suggest next-best actions. Auto-draft personalized collection emails/letters referencing overdue documents, prior commitments, and payment links. Summarize call/meeting notes, capture promises-to-pay, and create follow-up tasks with due dates. Recommend payment plan structures, fee/interest application, and escalation steps based on policy and history. Post cash, settle, and update exposure Apply incoming payments; settle invoices; update exposure, dunning status, and holds automatically. Reconcile exceptions (short pays, partials), and re-trigger letters or tasks if residuals remain. Review performance and refine strategy Track DSO, CEI, promise-to-pay adherence, dunning effectiveness by level, NSF rate/fees collected, and hold-to-release cycle time. Feed insights back to credit limits, terms, and dunning policies; adjust Copilot agent prompts and templates as needed. Roles and responsibilities Credit Manager: Oversees policy enforcement, holds governance, escalations, and approvals for payment plans/fee waivers. Collections Specialist/Agent: Works prioritized worklist, executes outreach, manages promises and plans, handles NSF follow-ups. Finance Controller: Ensures compliance with accounting and revenue policies; approves high-risk decisions and fee/interest rules. Sales Operations/Account Owner: Coordinates customer communications on large/strategic accounts; aligns on holds and commitments. Risk/Fraud Analyst: Monitors fraud/chargeback patterns and collaborates on holds and stricter terms when abuse is suspected. Dynamics 365 support Finance Collections worklist with customer/invoice filters, promises-to-pay, and aging buckets Collection letter sequences with fees/interest and configurable templates Returned/NSF payment handling: reverse applications, re-open invoices, post NSF/return fees, re-initiate dunning Credit management and centralized hold lists; reason codes and approval workflows Business Central Reminders (collection letters) and finance charge memos; payment reminders by levels Customer credit limits, blocking codes, workflows; handling of returned payments and re-opened invoices SCM and Commerce Visibility to order-level holds originating from credit/fraud conditions; call center check/hold scenarios and POS suspension/resume Copilot and collections agents Prioritized collections worklist, next-best-action suggestions Auto-drafted emails/letters and follow-up tasks; call summaries and promise capture Recommendations for payment plans and escalations; KPI snapshots in-context Power BI Credit exposure, limit utilization, aging trends, broken promises, NSF trends, and dunning effectiveness dashboards Operational controls and KPIs Controls Segregation of duties for hold releases, fee waivers, and plan approvals Letter level progression and suppression rules (e.g., disputes, active plans) NSF/returns policy (fees, temporary holds, term changes) and audit trails KPIs DSO, CEI, percent current, percent >30/>60/>90 days past due Promise-to-pay kept rate, average days to collect after final letter NSF/return rate and recovery, hold-to-release cycle time Agent productivity: contacts/day, right-party contacts, cash collected per agent Notes for implementation Align letter templates and fee/interest rules with regional regulatory requirements. Define clear suppression rules to avoid dunning customers in active dispute or compliant payment plans. Standardize NSF handling across payment methods (check, ACH, card chargeback) and ensure customers are notified promptly. Calibrate Copilot/agent prompts, email tones, and escalation thresholds to match your customer segments and brand voice.

processes.title: Collect interest
processes.description: Purpose Collect interest on overdue customer balances to encourage timely payment, recover carrying costs, and integrate interest charges seamlessly into collections and accounts receivable operations. Applies to Dynamics 365 Finance Dynamics 365 Business Central. Core components Interest calculation setup: interest codes, rates, calculation method (per month/year), grace periods, thresholds, compounding, and customer-specific overrides. Interest note lifecycle: generate, post, and communicate interest notes alongside dunning activities; include on customer statements. Collections integration: collection letter sequences and interest notes operate together within the overall collections process. Telemetry and events: business events for “Interest note posted” and “Collection letter created” support automation and downstream workflows. High-level process flow Identify candidates Use AR aging snapshots and collections worklists to surface customers with overdue balances that meet policy thresholds for interest charging. Determine interest rules Evaluate applicable interest code, rate, calculation method, grace period, and any customer-level overrides or exemptions. Calculate interest Run the interest calculation to compute charges at the transaction or account level according to your interest terms and aging. Generate interest notes Create interest notes for qualified overdue items; include reference to underlying invoices and the calculation basis. Post and notify Post interest notes to AR; send interest documentation with or adjacent to the correct collection letter level and include on customer statements. Engage customers Collections agents contact customers, capture outcomes (promise-to-pay, disputes), and, if needed, negotiate payment plans that include interest. Handle disputes and exceptions Use dispute workflows to validate claims (billing errors, legal restrictions) and waive or adjust interest where policy allows; retain audit trail. Apply payments and settle Apply receipts to interest notes and underlying invoices; re-trigger interest only on remaining overdue amounts as policy dictates. Automate and monitor Emit business events for posted interest notes; use dashboards to monitor interest recovery, aged balances with interest, and dunning effectiveness. Review policy Periodically reassess rates, grace periods, and dunning cadence to reflect market conditions and regulatory requirements. Roles and responsibilities Credit/Collections Manager: Owns policy, interest codes/terms, approval thresholds, and exception governance. Collections Agent: Executes worklists, generates/post interest notes, communicates charges, records promises, and manages disputes. AR Specialist: Applies cash, settles interest notes, and ensures statement accuracy. Finance Controller: Ensures compliance with accounting and legal policies; approves waivers beyond agent thresholds. Dynamics 365 product support Dynamics 365 Finance Interest codes/terms, automatic calculation, interest note generation/posting, inclusion on statements, integration with collection letter sequences. Business events for “Interest note posted” and “Collection letter created” to drive workflows and notifications. Collections workspaces, aging snapshots, and customer pools to prioritize outreach. Dynamics 365 Business Central Finance charge memos (interest), reminders (dunning), and customer-level rules for charges and thresholds. Copilot and agent capabilities Collections coordinator summaries, AR communications in Outlook/Teams, and guided next best actions accelerate prioritization and outreach. Operational controls Policy controls: grace periods, thresholds, compounding options, and customer exemptions documented and approved. Segregation of duties: separate configuration of interest terms, posting, and waiver approvals. Auditability: retain calculation details, notes, communications, and approval logs; leverage business events for traceability. Communications: align interest notifications with correct collection letter level to avoid over-communication or conflicting messages. Key inputs and outputs Inputs: AR aging snapshot, customer interest settings, interest codes/terms, policy thresholds. Outputs: posted interest notes, updated statements, customer communications, business events for downstream automation. KPIs Interest recovered versus charged, percent of overdue invoices with interest applied, days to collect after first interest note, dispute rate on interest notes, and promise-to-pay kept rate following interest communication.

processes.title: Manage customer collections
processes.description: Manage customer collections accelerates cash conversion by orchestrating outreach, payment arrangements, and escalations for delinquent accounts while balancing policy control with a consistent customer experience. Applies to Dynamics 365 Finance Dynamics 365 Business Central Core capabilities Collections worklists and pools organized by risk, region, portfolio, or collector; daily action queues. Aging exposure views and snapshots showing balance trends, limit utilization, and broken promises. Dunning communications with collection letter sequences, email templates, statements, and aligned interest/fees. Promises-to-pay and payment plans capturing commitments, due dates, installment schedules, and automated follow-ups. Dispute management to log issues, suspend dunning on disputed lines, route for resolution, and reconcile outcomes. Escalations including credit/order/customer holds, legal pathways, and policy-based exception approvals. Returned/NSF handling to reverse applications, reopen invoices, assess fees, and restart the cadence. Copilot/agent assistance for prioritized worklists, next-best actions, auto-drafted emails/letters, call summaries, reminder scheduling, and KPI snapshots. Analytics and automation across DSO, CEI, cure rates, and business events (e.g., letter posted, promise created). High-level process Prioritize portfolio: Refresh aging snapshots and worklists; segment by risk, amount, days past due, promise status, and expiring limits. Prepare targeted outreach: Select channel and tone; compile open items, short-pays, prior promises, and any interest/fee context; queue letters/emails and call scripts. Contact customers and record outcomes: Execute calls/emails; capture reasons for delay, disputes, promised amounts/dates, and preferred payment methods. Create or update promises-to-pay: Record commitment details; auto-schedule reminders and follow-ups; pause dunning for valid promises per policy. Offer and approve payment plans: Propose installment schedules for viable accounts; route exceptions for approval; attach conditions (e.g., partial order release). Manage disputes: Open cases, attach documents, suspend affected transactions, resolve, and resume collections on closure. Issue dunning communications: Generate and deliver the appropriate letter level and updated statements; align with interest notes and regional compliance. Apply cash and reconcile exceptions: Post receipts; settle invoices and fees; manage partials and short-pays; re-trigger collections for residuals. Enforce holds and escalate: When thresholds are breached, apply holds and escalate per playbook (credit/legal/third-party) with documented approvals. Review performance and refine strategy: Assess DSO, cure/broken-promise rates, contact effectiveness, and letter cadence; tune plans, playbooks, and agent guidance. Roles and responsibilities Collections Manager: Owns policy, portfolio performance, escalation standards, and exception governance. Collections Specialist/Agent: Works daily worklists, executes outreach, manages promises/plans, documents outcomes, coordinates disputes. Cash Application Specialist: Applies receipts, resolves short-pays, aligns settlements with plans/promises. Finance Controller: Ensures compliance and accounting treatment; approves fee waivers and exception plans; oversees write-off thresholds. Sales/Account Owner: Supports relationship-sensitive communications, negotiates commitments, and shares order context. Risk/Fraud Analyst: Monitors abuse/chargebacks; recommends stricter terms, prepayment, and block/hold criteria. Dynamics 365 support Finance: Collections workspace, customer pools, aging snapshots, collection letter sequences, interest notes, promises/payment schedules, centralized hold lists with reason codes, and business events. Business Central: Reminder levels, finance charge memos, customer ledger entries, approval workflows, blocking codes, and email dispatch. Copilot/Agents: Collections coordinator summary, prioritized actions, drafted emails/letters, call summaries, promise capture, recommended payment plans, and escalation suggestions. Power Platform: Power BI dashboards for exposure, cure rates, agent productivity; Power Automate to trigger reminders, tasks, and approvals. Operational controls Policy controls: Letter levels and cadence, grace periods, fee/interest rules, plan eligibility, escalation playbooks, regional legal templates, and retention rules. Segregation of duties: Separate configuration, posting, waivers, and exception approvals; enforce role-based overrides. Auditability: Store calculation details, notes, communications, approvals; rely on business events and logs for traceability. Communication alignment: Synchronize letters, interest notices, and agent outreach to prevent duplicates or conflicting messages. Compliance: Adhere to regional dunning, data privacy, and communication regulations. Key inputs and outputs Inputs: Aging snapshots, customer risk and limits, open invoices and fees, promise/plan status, dispute flags, returned-payment signals. Outputs: Posted collection letters, updated statements, documented promises/plans, applied holds/escalations, applied receipts/settlements, business events, and assigned tasks. KPIs DSO; CEI; >90-day past-due rate. Promise creation rate; promise-kept rate; cure rate by letter level. Dispute rate and resolution time. Write-off rate. Agent productivity (contacts/day, right-party contacts). Hold-to-release cycle time; cash collected vs. target.
