processes.title: Manage accounts receivable
processes.description: The 65.30 Manage Accounts Receivable process area encompasses all activities related to customer billing, revenue recognition, and financial settlement. It supports organizations in maintaining accurate financial records, ensuring timely payments, and managing customer-related financial transactions. This process excludes credit and collections, which are handled separately. Core Subprocesses Issue Sales Invoices Generate invoices from traditional sales orders, free text invoices, service orders, and project-based billing. Support integration with external systems for automated invoice distribution and compliance [1] . Issue Customer Credits Handle credits for returns, overbilling, service issues, and price matching. Credits may be tied to sales orders, free text invoices, or issued as standalone memos [2] . Subscription Billing Manage recurring billing cycles for subscriptions, including contract terms, renewals, and adjustments. Revenue Recognition Apply recognition schedules for deferred revenue across products, services, and long-term contracts. Support stubbed entries and historical migration for in-flight contracts [4] . Process Payments Record incoming payments from customers across channels. Apply payments to open invoices and manage payment journals. Handle Prepayments Accept and apply customer prepayments to future invoices or orders. Issue Refunds Process refunds for overpayments, returns, or service cancellations. Settle Transactions Match payments to invoices, apply adjustments, and reconcile accounts. Write Off Bad Debt Identify and write off uncollectible receivables in compliance with financial policies. Process Customer Rebates Apply approved incentive transactions and validate rebate claims. Ensure accurate financial reflection of rebates. Manage Trade Allowances Define and apply bill-backs, off-invoice discounts, promotional funds, lump sums, and traditional rebates. Manage Sales Commissions Calculate and distribute commissions based on invoiced sales, returns, and adjustments. Manage Bills of Exchange Handle promissory notes and other instruments used for customer payments. Dynamics 365 Support Finance & Business Central Core invoicing, credit issuance, payment processing, and revenue recognition. Project Operations Project-based billing and service-related credits. Commerce POS integration for refunds, credits, and invoice generation. Electronic Invoicing Integration with external systems for regulatory compliance and automation.

processes.title: Issue sales invoices
processes.description: This business process defines how organizations issue sales invoices across various scenarios using Dynamics 365 Finance, Business Central, and Project Operations. It supports accurate billing, revenue recognition, and customer account management. Supported Invoice Types Sales Order Invoices Generated from confirmed shipments, reflecting actual goods delivered. These invoices include item details, pricing, taxes, and shipping charges. They can be created manually or in bulk via batch jobs [1] . Free Text Invoices Used for billing services or miscellaneous charges not tied to a sales order. These can be one-time or recurring (e.g., subscriptions, retainers). Templates and default values streamline creation and ensure consistency [1] [2] . Project Invoices Created from time, expense, and fee transactions recorded against a project. Billing rules define how and when invoices are generated—such as time and materials, fixed price, or milestone-based billing. These support detailed breakdowns and customer-specific formats. Service Invoices Apply to scenarios where services are sold independently or alongside products. These may originate from service orders or manual entry and are integrated with service management workflows [1] . Integration Scenarios Invoices can be: Posted, printed, or emailed directly from Dynamics 365. Synchronized with external systems for further processing. Managed using extensible connectors for electronic invoicing and regulatory compliance. Process Flow Invoice Source Identification Determine whether the invoice is based on a sales order, project, service, or free text. Invoice Creation Use templates, billing rules, or manual entry to generate the invoice. Validation and Posting Apply tax rules, verify pricing, and post the invoice to the ledger. Distribution and Integration Send invoices to customers via email or integrate with external systems for processing. Monitoring and Adjustments Track invoice status, apply corrections, and manage disputes or adjustments. Stakeholders Accounts Receivable Specialist Manages invoice creation, posting, and customer communication. Project Manager Oversees project-based billing and ensures alignment with contract terms. Finance Controller Ensures compliance with revenue recognition and financial reporting standards. Service Coordinator Handles service-related invoicing and supports customer resolution. Dynamics 365 Support Finance & Business Central Core invoicing capabilities including free text and sales order invoices. Project Operations Project-based billing with configurable rules and formats. Electronic Invoicing Service Supports integration with external systems and regulatory compliance.

processes.title: Create and process free text invoices in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: This business process defines how organizations issue sales invoices across various scenarios using Dynamics 365 Finance, Business Central, and Project Operations. It supports accurate billing, revenue recognition, and customer account management. SUPPORTED INVOICE TYPES * Sales Order Invoices Generated from confirmed shipments, reflecting actual goods delivered. These invoices include item details, pricing, taxes, and shipping charges. They can be created manually or in bulk via batch jobs [1] [https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/BusinessApplicationsContentHub/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7b73D39CD4-B34A-4ABE-9786-BACD76BC814A%7d&file=65.30.010-issues-sales-invoices.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true&DefaultItemOpen=1]. * Free Text Invoices Used for billing services or miscellaneous charges not tied to a sales order. These can be one-time or recurring (e.g., subscriptions, retainers). Templates and default values streamline creation and ensure consistency [1] [https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/BusinessApplicationsContentHub/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7b73D39CD4-B34A-4ABE-9786-BACD76BC814A%7d&file=65.30.010-issues-sales-invoices.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true&DefaultItemOpen=1] [2] [https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dynamics365/finance/accounts-receivable/create-free-text-invoice-new]. * Project Invoices Created from time, expense, and fee transactions recorded against a project. Billing rules define how and when invoices are generated—such as time and materials, fixed price, or milestone-based billing. These support detailed breakdowns and customer-specific formats. * Service Invoices Apply to scenarios where services are sold independently or alongside products. These may originate from service orders or manual entry and are integrated with service management workflows [1] [https://microsoft.sharepoint.com/teams/BusinessApplicationsContentHub/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc=%7b73D39CD4-B34A-4ABE-9786-BACD76BC814A%7d&file=65.30.010-issues-sales-invoices.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true&DefaultItemOpen=1]. INTEGRATION SCENARIOS Invoices can be: * Posted, printed, or emailed directly from Dynamics 365. * Synchronized with external systems for further processing. * Managed using extensible connectors for electronic invoicing and regulatory compliance. PROCESS FLOW 1. Invoice Source Identification Determine whether the invoice is based on a sales order, project, service, or free text. 2. Invoice Creation Use templates, billing rules, or manual entry to generate the invoice. 3. Validation and Posting Apply tax rules, verify pricing, and post the invoice to the ledger. 4. Distribution and Integration Send invoices to customers via email or integrate with external systems for processing. 5. Monitoring and Adjustments Track invoice status, apply corrections, and manage disputes or adjustments. STAKEHOLDERS * Accounts Receivable Specialist Manages invoice creation, posting, and customer communication. * Project Manager Oversees project-based billing and ensures alignment with contract terms. * Finance Controller Ensures compliance with revenue recognition and financial reporting standards. * Service Coordinator Handles service-related invoicing and supports customer resolution. DYNAMICS 365 SUPPORT * Finance & Business Central Core invoicing capabilities including free text and sales order invoices. * Project Operations Project-based billing with configurable rules and formats. * Electronic Invoicing Service Supports integration with external systems and regulatory compliance.

processes.title: Issue customer credits
processes.description: The Issue Customer Credits process defines how organizations manage financial adjustments for customers across various sales channels. It supports accurate financial reconciliation, customer satisfaction, and operational efficiency. Core Scenarios Sales Order Credits Issued when goods are returned or orders are canceled after invoicing. Credits are created from the original invoice or through a return order process. Inventory and financial postings are automatically adjusted. Free Text Invoice Credits Used to correct or reverse charges not tied to a sales order. These can be manually created or copied from the original invoice with negative amounts. Recurring invoices can be adjusted using credit notes. Project-Based Credits Generated from time, expense, or fee transactions that require reversal. In Dynamics 365 Project Operations, credit notes are linked to billing rules and specific milestones. Service-Related Credits Applied when services are not delivered as expected or customer dissatisfaction arises. These credits ensure service quality and customer retention. POS Credits and Price Matching In Dynamics 365 Commerce POS, credit memos can be issued directly from return transactions. Price matching adjustments are supported through credit memo operations. Partial redemptions automatically generate new credit memos for remaining balances. Process Flow Initiate Credit Triggered by return, cancellation, service issue, or pricing discrepancy. Validate Eligibility Confirm policy compliance and customer entitlement. Create Credit Memo Generate credit from invoice, free text, or manually. Apply Credit Link to customer account, adjust balances, and optionally issue refunds. Track and Reconcile Monitor credit usage, partial redemptions, and financial impact. Stakeholders Accounts Receivable Specialist Manages credit issuance and reconciliation. Customer Service Representative Initiates credits and communicates with customers. Finance Controller Ensures compliance with financial policies and reporting. POS Associate Issues credit memos and handles price matching at the register. Dynamics 365 Support Finance & Business Central Core credit memo creation and posting. Commerce POS Credit memo issuance, redemption, and price matching. Project Operations Project-based credit note generation.

processes.title: Bill subscriptions
processes.description: The Bill Subscriptions business process defines how organizations manage recurring billing for subscription-based products and services. It supports both traditional subscription billing and continuity billing models, enabling predictable revenue and streamlined operations. Core Scenarios Traditional Subscription Billing Recurring charges for services or digital products (e.g., software, memberships) billed monthly, quarterly, or annually. Managed via billing schedules and contract terms Supports proration, usage-based billing, and multi-element arrangements Revenue recognition aligned with ASC 606 and IFRS 15 standards Continuity Billing Recurring shipments of physical goods (e.g., consumables, curated boxes) fulfilled through continuity orders. Automatically generated based on customer preferences Integrated with fulfillment and inventory systems Billing Concepts Frequency : Monthly, quarterly, annually, or custom intervals Pricing : Standard trade agreements, tiered pricing, escalations Item Types : Standard (fixed quantity), usage-based (variable), milestone-based (event-driven) Renewals : Automatic contract renewals supported Revenue Recognition Revenue can be deferred and recognized over time Allocation rules and schedules ensure compliance Integrated with general ledger for accurate financial reporting Integration Subscription billing integrates with CRM, eCommerce, and customer service platforms Supports external invoicing systems and electronic billing workflows Stakeholders Billing Specialist : Manages schedules, invoicing, and renewals Finance Controller : Oversees revenue recognition and compliance Subscription Product Manager : Designs offerings and pricing models Customer Service Representative : Handles billing inquiries and adjustments Dynamics 365 Support Finance : Subscription Billing module for complex billing scenarios Business Central : Recurring sales lines and invoice templates Commerce : Continuity orders and omnichannel fulfillment Project Operations : Subscription billing with deferrals and project integration

processes.title: Recognize revenue
processes.description: The Recognize Revenue business process defines how organizations account for earned revenue across standard sales and project-based scenarios. It ensures compliance with accounting standards such as ASC 606 and IFRS 15, supports financial transparency, and aligns revenue recognition with performance obligations. Core Scenarios Standard Sales Revenue Recognition Revenue is recognized when control of goods or services transfers to the customer. Recognition is based on fulfillment dates and performance obligations. Supports deferred revenue schedules and unbilled accounts receivable (A/R) for accrual-based accounting. Project Revenue Recognition Managed through Dynamics 365 Project Operations. Time and Materials : Revenue recognized as billable hours and expenses are incurred. Fixed Price : Revenue recognized via milestones, percentage of completion, or straight-line schedules. Cost-Plus : Revenue recognized based on actual costs plus markup. Recognition can occur independently of billing, supporting accrual accounting. Revenue Recognition Features Deferrals : Postpone revenue to match earned periods. Recognitions : Triggered when performance obligations are met. Audit Trails : Track adjustments, reversals, and recognition history. Integration : Syncs with external systems and general ledger for financial reporting. Process Flow Identify Revenue Source : Sales order, project billing, subscription. Apply Recognition Rules : Based on contract terms, fulfillment, or billing milestones. Post Revenue Entries : Update financial records and general ledger. Adjust and Reconcile : Handle reversals, corrections, and audit compliance. Stakeholders Finance Controller : Oversees recognition policies and compliance. Project Accountant : Manages project-based revenue alignment. Billing Specialist : Ensures correct invoicing and revenue schedules. IT Integration Lead : Supports data integration with reporting tools. Dynamics 365 Support Finance & Business Central : Core revenue recognition and deferral capabilities. Project Operations : Project-based billing and milestone tracking. Electronic Invoicing : Integration with external systems for automated processing.

processes.title: Process customer prepayments
processes.description: The business process defines how organizations record, apply, and manage customer prepayments—advance payments made before goods or services are delivered. This process is distinct from standard customer payments, which are typically applied after invoicing. Prepayments are common in industries requiring deposits, down payments, or full advance payments prior to fulfillment. Supported Scenarios Sales Order Prepayments A prepayment invoice is generated and posted before the order is fulfilled. The payment is applied to the sales order and deducted from the final invoice. Manual Journal Entry Prepayments can be recorded in a customer payment journal and held as an unapplied balance until matched to an invoice. POS and eCommerce In Dynamics 365 Commerce, prepayments are collected at the time of order placement for items not immediately fulfilled (e.g., special orders or pre-orders). Project Prepayments In project-based scenarios, prepayments are recorded against a project contract and applied to future billing milestones. Entry Channels Point of Sale (POS) Online checkout Call center-assisted entry Manual entry via journals Integration with external systems (e.g., lockbox, check scanning) Dynamics 365 Support Finance & Business Central Supports prepayment invoicing, journal entry, and application to orders or projects. Commerce Enables prepayment capture at POS and online checkout for special or high-value orders. Project Operations Allows prepayments to be linked to project contracts and applied to milestone billing.

processes.title: Process customer refunds
processes.description: The Process Customer Refunds business process defines how organizations manage and execute refunds across various channels and payment types. It ensures financial accuracy, customer satisfaction, and compliance with refund policies. Supported Refund Scenarios Sales Order Refunds Refunds issued for returned or canceled orders, typically tied to original invoices or return orders. Free Text Invoice Refunds Refunds for miscellaneous charges not linked to a sales order, often processed manually. Service Order Refunds Refunds for undelivered or unsatisfactory services, including partial or full service cancellations. POS Refunds In-person refunds processed at the point of sale, including cash, card, gift card, and loyalty point redemptions. Online and Call Center Refunds Refunds initiated through eCommerce platforms or customer service representatives. Journal Entry Refunds Manual refunds recorded in the customer payment journal or cash receipt journal. Lockbox and Check Scanning Refunds Refunds processed through bank lockbox imports or scanned checks using OCR and integrated systems. Process Flow Receive Refund Request Initiated by customer service, POS associate, or automated system. Validate Request Confirm eligibility based on return policies, payment method, and transaction history. Process Refund Create refund transaction, apply to customer account, or issue payment. Post Refund Update financial records and reconcile accounts. Confirm and Revise (if needed) Review refund accuracy and make adjustments if necessary. Stakeholders Accounts Receivable Specialist Processes refund transactions, reconciles accounts, and ensures documentation. Customer Service Representative Initiates refunds based on customer interactions and return approvals. Store Manager Approves in-person refunds and ensures compliance with store policies. Finance Controller Oversees refund policies, financial controls, and audit compliance. IT Integration Lead Manages refund processing through integrated payment gateways and external systems. Dynamics 365 Support Finance & Business Central Core refund processing, journal entry, and reconciliation. Commerce POS and eCommerce refund capture, loyalty integration. External Integrations APIs and data entities for lockbox, CRM, and payment gateway connectivity.

processes.title: Settle customer transactions
processes.description: This business process defines how organizations match payments, credit memos, and other financial entries to open invoices or debit transactions. Settlement ensures accurate customer account balances and supports financial reconciliation. Dynamics 365 Finance and Business Central support both automatic and manual settlement methods, as well as netting between customer and vendor accounts. Core Settlement Methods Automatic Settlement Payments are matched to open invoices based on predefined rules. Rules can prioritize oldest invoices, specific invoice types, or currency logic. Ideal for high-volume environments or when importing payments from lockboxes or integrated systems. Manual Settlement Used when automatic matching is not possible or when user control is required. Supports partial payments, overpayments, underpayments, and customer-specific instructions. Users manually select open transactions in the settlement form or during journal entry. Open Transaction Editing Allows corrections after posting. Users can unmark and reapply settlements to adjust how payments are matched. Netting (Customer and Vendor Balances) Netting Overview Netting offsets balances between customers and vendors when they are the same party. Minimizes unnecessary payments and transaction fees. Netting Agreement Defines customer-vendor pairs and posting parameters. Can be created manually or via data entities. Includes journal name, netting account, and effective date range. Manual Netting Users select open invoices for both customer and vendor. System calculates the minimal balance and posts a netting journal to settle both sides. Automatic Netting Triggered via batch jobs or process automation. Uses netting rules to automate selection and posting. Process Flow Identify Transactions – Open invoices, payments, credit memos. Apply Settlement Method – Automatic, manual, or netting. Post Settlement – Update ledger and subledger balances. Reconcile and Report – Ensure financial accuracy and audit trail. Stakeholders Accounts Receivable Specialist – Manages settlement entries and reconciliations. Finance Controller – Oversees compliance and financial reporting. Cash Clerk – Executes netting and journal postings. IT Integration Lead – Supports lockbox, check scanning, and external system integrations. Dynamics 365 Support Finance & Business Central – Core settlement, journal entry, and reconciliation. Netting Module – Customer/vendor balance netting, agreement setup, and automation. Process Automation Framework – Supports automatic netting and batch processing.

Manual Netting Users select open invoices for both customer and vendor. System calculates the minimal balance and posts a netting journal to settle both sides. Automatic Netting Triggered via batch jobs or process automation. Uses netting rules to automate selection and posting. Process Flow Identify Transactions – Open invoices, payments, credit memos. processes.description: The Manage Trade Allowances business process defines how organizations operate, monitor, and revise promotional incentives offered to customers in exchange for meeting specific volume or behavioral goals. These allowances are typically used in industries such as consumer packaged goods (CPG), food and beverage, wholesale distribution, and retail. Core Components Bill-Backs Retroactive payments based on customer performance, processed as deductions against accounts receivable. Off-Invoice Discounts Immediate reductions applied at the time of sale. Promotional Funds Budgeted amounts allocated to support trade allowance programs, tracked and reconciled for compliance. Lump Sum Payments One-time payments for agreed promotional activities such as advertising or in-store displays. Traditional Rebates Periodic payments based on cumulative purchases or performance metrics. Process Flow Identify Deductions Detect deductions on payments against trade allowance agreements. Operate Claims Process claims submitted by customers for promotional incentives. Verify Deductions Validate claims against agreements and promotional terms. Issue Refunds or Credits Apply approved claims to customer accounts. Update Records Maintain accurate financial and promotional tracking. Revise Programs Adjust trade allowance strategies based on performance and financial impact. Stakeholders Trade Promotions Manager Designs and manages trade allowance programs aligned with sales goals. Accounts Receivable Specialist Reviews and processes deductions, reconciles claims, and applies credits. Finance Controller Oversees accruals, liability accounts, and financial reporting. Sales Operations Analyst Tracks performance and ensures accurate application to sales orders. Dynamics 365 Support Supply Chain Management Enables configuration and automation of trade allowance agreements, bill-back claims, and promotional fund tracking. Finance Supports deduction processing, liability management, and financial reconciliation. Commerce Integrates promotional pricing and discounting into POS and eCommerce channels.

processes.title: Manage sales orders
processes.description: Before you start selling your products and services to customers, it's critical that you establish your business pricing and contracts. Depending on the types of customers you sell to, the process steps and stakeholders vary. For example, in a business-to-business (B2B) model, sales managers may be responsible for establishing and communicating your prices. In a business-to-consumer (B2C) model, pricing might be defined by merchandising, sales leadership, or company policy and published on your website. After you establish your prices and contracts, you can start recording your sales in Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Commerce, or Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, depending on your business requirements. The Dynamics 365 product family supports many sales models or channels, such as brick-and-mortar, e-commerce, call center, B2B, B2C, and more. An organization may be geographically dispersed or have more than one line of business. For example, a retail organization may have a manufacturing plant to produce some items and distribution centers that combine manufactured and purchased items. An organization may offer services and sell products to support them or sell products and offer after-sales services. An organization may also trade products, services, and resources across companies. Dynamics 365 supports all these scenarios. Learn about intercompany planning in Supply Chain Management or how to manage intercompany transactions in Business Central.

processes.title: Sell product subscriptions
processes.description: The Sell Product Subscriptions business process defines how organizations offer and manage recurring product sales, including both traditional subscriptions (tangible or intangible) and continuity orders . This process is part of the broader Order to Cash cycle and supports predictable revenue, customer retention, and operational efficiency. Core Components Traditional Subscriptions Includes recurring sales of tangible goods (e.g., magazines, consumables) and intangible services (e.g., software, memberships). Managed through subscription contracts with defined billing cycles and renewal terms. Continuity Orders Automatically generated orders based on a predefined schedule (e.g., monthly shipments of household items). These are integrated into digital storefronts and managed via Intelligent Order Management. Subscription Frequency Defined at the product level (e.g., monthly, quarterly, yearly). Determines how often fulfillment jobs are triggered [3] . Contract Management Subscription contracts include start/end dates, billing terms, and fulfillment rules. Only one product per subscription is currently supported, with multi-product support planned. Process Flow Identify Customer and Services Capture customer details and select subscription offerings. Negotiate Terms Define pricing, frequency, and renewal policies. Confirm Order Validate subscription setup and initiate billing schedule. Revise Order Adjust terms or frequency based on customer feedback or operational needs. Fulfill Subscription Use Intelligent Order Management to orchestrate deliveries across warehouses and carriers. Stakeholders Subscription Product Manager Designs offerings, pricing models, and renewal policies. Billing Specialist Manages invoicing, billing schedules, and revenue recognition. E-commerce Manager Integrates continuity orders into online sales flows. Order Fulfillment Lead Oversees logistics and delivery orchestration. Finance Controller Ensures compliance with accounting standards for recurring revenue. Dynamics 365 Support Dynamics 365 Finance Supports subscription billing setup, revenue recognition, and deferrals. Dynamics 365 Commerce Manages continuity orders and integrates subscription flows into e-commerce platforms. Dynamics 365 Intelligent Order Management Automates subscription fulfillment and order orchestration. Dynamics 365 Business Central Provides financial and operational support for subscription contracts.

processes.title: Enter sales orders
processes.description: The Enter Sales Orders business process defines how organizations capture and manage sales orders across various channels and scenarios. It supports both traditional and modern sales models and is a core part of the Order to Cash cycle. Supported Sales Channels Manual Entry : Sales orders entered directly by back-office staff using Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management or Business Central. Point of Sale (POS) : Store associates enter orders at the register using Dynamics 365 Commerce. Call Centers : Assisted sales and remote order entry. eCommerce (B2B/B2C) : Online orders captured automatically via integrated platforms. Quotes to Orders : Sales professionals convert quotes into orders using Dynamics 365 Sales. Agreements to Orders : Orders generated from contractual agreements or recurring commitments. Supported Sales Types Products : Tangible goods across retail, wholesale, and manufacturing. Services : Consulting, subscriptions, maintenance, and leasing. Gift Cards : Issued and redeemed through POS or eCommerce. Royalty-Based Items : Sales that trigger royalty payouts, common in media and publishing. Advanced Scenarios Intercompany Trade : Automatically generated orders between legal entities. Brokered Sales : Orders facilitated by third-party brokers with custom integrations. Dual Write : Real-time synchronization between Dynamics 365 apps and Dataverse. EDI Orders : Electronic Data Interchange for automated B2B order processing. Process Flow Initiate Order : Capture customer intent via POS, eCommerce, call center, or manual entry. Validate Terms : Apply pricing, discounts, and contract terms. Confirm Order : Generate and confirm the sales order in the system. Sync Systems : Use Dual Write or EDI to ensure data consistency across platforms. Monitor & Adjust : Track order status, apply changes, and manage exceptions. Stakeholders Sales Associate : Enters orders via POS or call center. Sales Manager : Oversees quote conversion and agreement-based orders. Order Fulfillment Lead : Coordinates delivery and logistics. Finance Controller : Ensures compliance with revenue recognition and royalty tracking. IT Integration Lead : Manages Dual Write, EDI, and broker integrations. Dynamics 365 Support Dynamics 365 Commerce : POS, gift cards, eCommerce, loyalty. Dynamics 365 Sales : Quote-to-order conversion. Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management : Manual entry, intercompany, royalty tracking. Dynamics 365 Business Central : Back-office order management. Dynamics 365 Intelligent Order Management : Orchestration and fulfillment. Dual Write & EDI : Real-time sync and automated B2B processing.

processes.title: Manage blanket sales orders
processes.description: This business process defines how organizations manage long-term sales commitments with customers using blanket sales orders , also referred to as sales agreements in Dynamics 365. These agreements allow customers to commit to purchasing large quantities of goods or services over time, with predefined pricing, quantities, and delivery schedules. Core Concepts Sales Agreements : Framework contracts that define terms for recurring sales over a period. They include pricing, quantity commitments, and delivery schedules. Release Orders : Individual sales orders created from the original agreement to fulfill specific shipments. These do not affect item availability until released. Types of Agreements : Quantity-based : Customer commits to purchasing a specific quantity. Value-based : Agreement is based on a total monetary value. Schedule-based : Delivery dates are predefined across multiple shipments. Process Flow Negotiate Contract Define pricing, quantity, and delivery terms with the customer. Confirm Contract Finalize and approve the agreement in the system. Create Release Orders Generate individual sales orders from the agreement as needed. Monitor Contract Performance Track fulfillment progress, remaining quantities, and revenue recognition. Revise Contract Adjust terms or quantities based on customer needs or business changes. Complete Fulfillment Close the agreement once all commitments are met. Stakeholders Sales Agreement Manager Negotiates and maintains long-term agreements. Order Fulfillment Coordinator Manages release orders and ensures timely delivery. Finance Analyst Monitors revenue recognition and pricing compliance. Customer Service Representative Handles customer inquiries and updates orders. Dynamics 365 Support Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Enables creation and tracking of sales agreements and release orders. Dynamics 365 Business Central Supports blanket sales orders with flexible scheduling and conversion to sales orders. Integration Features APIs and EDI support allow automated creation and fulfillment of release orders. Agreements can be configured for two-way or three-way match policies.

processes.title: Manage sales order changes
processes.description: This business process defines how organizations manage updates to sales orders across all channels and order types. It excludes cancellation scenarios, which are covered separately. Scope Sales order changes may include: Quantity adjustments Delivery date changes Shipping address updates Pricing modifications These changes apply to: Standard sales orders Call center orders eCommerce orders POS orders Intercompany orders Drop shipment orders Process Flow Initiate Change Request Triggered by customer service, sales, or fulfillment teams based on customer input or operational needs. Validate Change Ensure changes comply with pricing policies, inventory availability, and contractual terms. Apply Changes Update the sales order in Dynamics 365. Changes are tracked with audit trails and version history. Synchronize Related Documents For intercompany and drop shipment scenarios, changes to the sales order automatically update linked purchase orders. Notify Stakeholders Communicate changes to fulfillment, finance, and customer service teams to ensure alignment. Stakeholders Sales Operations Analyst Manages updates and ensures changes are communicated across teams. Order Management Specialist Applies changes and monitors downstream impacts. Finance Analyst Validates pricing and revenue implications. Customer Service Representative Coordinates with customers and confirms changes. Dynamics 365 Support Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Supports direct editing of sales orders with audit trails and change tracking. Dynamics 365 Commerce Enables call center agents to modify orders placed through assisted channels. Dynamics 365 Business Central Allows flexible editing including partial shipments and backorders. Intercompany & Drop Shipment Sync Automatically updates related documents across legal entities and vendors.

processes.title: Manage sales order holds
processes.description: The Manage Sales Order Holds business process defines how organizations temporarily pause order processing across various sales channels due to issues such as payment verification, credit checks, fraud detection, or manual review. This process is part of the broader Order to Cash cycle and ensures operational control and risk mitigation. Core Hold Types Standard Order Holds Applied manually or automatically based on business rules, such as missing information or pending approvals. Call Center Holds Used to pause orders initiated through assisted channels for customer verification or issue resolution. POS Holds (Suspended Sales) Transactions can be suspended in the Point of Sale (POS) system to manage customer flow or resolve discrepancies before finalizing the sale. Fraud Holds Triggered by fraud detection systems or manual review when suspicious activity is identified. Check Holds Applied when payment by check requires verification or clearance before order fulfillment. Process Flow Identify Order for Hold Triggered by system rules, manual review, or customer interaction. Place Order on Hold Sales order status updated to reflect hold type and reason. Review Hold Status Stakeholders assess whether the hold can be cleared. Clear Hold or Escalate If approved, the order proceeds; otherwise, escalated for further review. Update Order Status Order resumes processing or is flagged for additional action. Stakeholders Order Management Specialist Applies and releases holds based on business rules and customer interactions. Call Center Supervisor Manages holds on assisted orders and ensures timely resolution. POS Associate Suspends and resumes transactions in-store to maintain accuracy and flow. Fraud Risk Analyst Reviews fraud holds and determines next steps. Finance Controller Oversees check holds and ensures compliance with financial policies. Dynamics 365 Support Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management Enables configuration and automation of order holds across standard and intercompany scenarios. Dynamics 365 Commerce Supports POS transaction suspension and fraud detection workflows. Dynamics 365 Business Central Provides financial controls for check holds and manual order reviews.

processes.title: Manage store operations
processes.description: The Manage Store Operations business process defines how brick-and-mortar retail stores handle daily operational tasks using Dynamics 365 Commerce. It supports store associates and managers in executing financial transactions, customer interactions, and operational procedures through POS and back-office tools. Core Components Start-of-Day Operations Open shift, count starting cash, add float to drawer. End-of-Day Operations Close shift, reconcile cash, generate reports for review and approval. Cash Management Cash Drops: Reduce drawer cash during the day. Bank Drops: Deposit funds at end of day. Add Cash to Drawer: Replenish drawer as needed. Record Non-Sales Cash Movements: Track petty cash reimbursements, donations, etc. Customer Pickup Fulfill online or cross-channel orders in-store. Verify order and customer identity via POS. Complete pickup transaction. Price Adjustments Modify pricing at POS for promotions, corrections, or overrides. Safe Drops Securely transfer excess cash from drawer to store safe. Process Flow Open Store: Start shift, prepare cash drawer. Operate Store: Handle transactions, pickups, price changes, and cash movements. Close Store: End shift, reconcile cash, submit reports. Stakeholders Store Associate: Executes POS transactions, pickups, and cash handling. Store Manager: Oversees operations, approves reports, manages safe/bank drops. Finance Analyst: Reviews reports, reconciles cash, ensures compliance. Dynamics 365 Support Dynamics 365 Commerce: POS interface for transactions, pickups, and cash operations. Back-office tools for reporting and reconciliation. Omnichannel Fulfillment: Supports BOPIS (Buy Online, Pick Up In Store) and cross-channel order management.

processes.title: Process customer returns and exchanges
processes.description: This business process defines how organizations manage customer returns, exchanges, and related service scenarios across all sales channels. It supports both customer satisfaction and regulatory compliance, and is a critical part of the Order to Cash cycle. Core Scenarios Covered Returns Customers may return items through POS, eCommerce, or call center channels. Returns can be full or partial, and may involve restocking, scrapping, or refurbishing. Exchanges Items can be exchanged for identical or alternative products. Exchanges may be processed immediately or scheduled for later fulfillment. Credits and Refunds Refunds may be issued as store credit, gift cards, or direct payment. Price matching adjustments are also supported. Dynamics 365 enforces business rules and approval workflows for exceptions. Repair and Service Items not returned may be serviced or repaired. Service orders or technician dispatches can be initiated to resolve issues without requiring a return. Quality Management and Inspection Returned items undergo inspection to determine disposition. Dynamics 365 supports quarantine orders, inspection workflows, and disposition decisions to maintain inventory accuracy and product quality. Product Recalls and Tracing Recalled items are tracked and processed through specialized workflows. Traceability ensures compliance with safety and regulatory standards. Process Flow Initiate Return or Exchange Triggered by customer request via any channel. Validate Request Check eligibility, warranty, and return policies. Process Transaction Issue refund, credit, or exchange order. Inspect Returned Item Perform quality checks and determine disposition. Service or Repair (if applicable) Create service orders or dispatch technicians. Trace and Recall (if applicable) Execute recall workflows and trace affected inventory. Stakeholders Customer Service Representative Initiates returns, exchanges, and service requests. Store Associate Handles in-store returns and restocking. Warehouse Manager Manages returned inventory and inspections. Quality Control Analyst Inspects items and determines disposition. Dynamics 365 Support Commerce Manages POS and eCommerce returns, exchanges, and refunds. Supply Chain Management Supports inspection, quarantine, and disposition workflows. Field Service Enables repair orders and technician dispatches. Finance Handles credit issuance, refund processing, and approval workflows.

processes.title: Cancel sales orders
processes.description: This business process defines how organizations cancel sales orders across all channels and order types using Dynamics 365. It supports full and partial cancellations and includes voiding transactions at the Point of Sale (POS). The process ensures accurate inventory, financial reconciliation, and customer satisfaction. Supported Channels and Order Types POS (Point of Sale): Voiding sales directly at the register. eCommerce: Online cancellations initiated by customers or agents. Call Center: Assisted cancellations via customer service. Back Office: Manual cancellations by operations or finance teams. Omnichannel: Orders placed in one channel and canceled in another. Cancellation Scenarios Full Cancellation: Entire order is voided before fulfillment. Partial Cancellation: Specific lines or quantities are canceled while the rest of the order proceeds. processes.title: Allocate inventory to sales orders
processes.description: This business process defines how organizations assign available inventory to sales orders using manual or automatic methods. In Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management, this is referred to as reservations or marking . The goal is to ensure accurate fulfillment, prioritize customer needs, and maintain inventory integrity across channels. Core Concepts Reservation Inventory is reserved for specific sales orders either manually by users or automatically based on system rules. Reservations ensure that stock is held for committed orders and not consumed by others. Marking A method to link supply and demand directly. Marking ties inbound inventory (e.g., purchase orders) to outbound demand (e.g., sales orders), ensuring that specific stock is allocated to specific orders. This is especially useful in cross-docking scenarios. Manual vs. Automatic Allocation Manual : Users select inventory to reserve or mark for orders. Automatic : System applies rules to allocate inventory based on availability, priority, and delivery timelines. Process Flow Identify Inventory Determine available stock and inbound supply. Determine Reservation Method Choose between manual or automatic reservation. Apply Reservation or Marking Reserve inventory or mark supply to demand. Confirm Reservation Records Validate that inventory is correctly allocated. Update Inventory Requirements Adjust planning and fulfillment based on allocations. Complete Allocation Process Finalize reservations and proceed with order fulfillment. Stakeholders Inventory Manager Oversees inventory availability and ensures accurate allocation. Sales Operations Analyst Manages order prioritization and business rule compliance. Procurement Specialist Coordinates inbound supply to support allocation needs. Warehouse Associate Executes picking and packing based on reserved inventory. Dynamics 365 Support Supply Chain Management Supports reservations, marking, and inventory visibility. Business Central Enables manual and automated inventory allocation. Intelligent Order Management Enhances allocation logic with visibility add-ins and prioritization rules.

processes.title: Plan to produce
processes.description: The term plan to produce is used to describe a collection of business processes that an organization implements to support the planning and execution of the production process. Planning refers to the definition of production strategies, reviewing the long-term production plan, and building a production schedule. The production business process incorporates the activities before, during, and after the execution of the procedures that result from taking raw materials and creating sub-assemblies or finished goods. The plan to produce process covers several different approaches to manufacturing. For example, discrete manufacturing, process or batch manufacturing, lean manufacturing, and job-shop manufacturing. These are all considered different modes of manufacturing, but the core concepts in the business process are largely the same. The plan to produce process is highly interconnected to the other end to end business processes, such as forecast to plan, procure to pay, inventory to deliver, record to report, order to cash, and acquire to dispose. The upstream or downstream relationship of plan to produce to the other processes is highly dependent on the operational strategies of each organization. For example, plan to produce could be an upstream process of order to cash in a make-to-stock scenario, but would be a downstream process instead in a make to order scenario. Organizations also often use multiple different operational strategies when they offer different types of products. This choice is fully supported by Dynamics 365. Note: It is important to note that the inventory management processes related to plan to produce are not included in this process definition. They are located in the inventory to deliver process. Learn more at Inventory to deliver - introduction to the end-to-end business process. Note: It is important to note that the supply and demand planning process is part of the forecast to plan business process, and the planning in the plan to produce process begins with scheduling production. Learn more at Forecast to plan introduction. The high-level strategy for plan to produce processes should be planned at the early phases of a larger business solution. The design and decisions made about this process have an impact on downstream processes including integrations, data that must be migrated, and so on. The production process is often considered business-critical scope for implementing a technology solution, but may sometimes be slated for later phases when a finance-first implementation strategy is chosen. Every organization has variations to the plan to produce process. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a Microsoft technology solution to support the plan to produce process.

processes.title: Control production quality
processes.description: This process area is highly related to the Manage inventory quality process area in the Inventory to deliver end-to-end process. Controlling production quality covers the processes from inspecting manufactured goods to implementing corrective and preventive actions to improve product quality. For regulated industries, this business process area should be considered critical. It should be addressed initially and continuously referenced throughout the implementation to ensure compliance. In other organizations, this process area may be implemented alongside the Run production operations process area. Also, some companies run production quality processes externally to their systems and onboard to Dynamics 365 at a later date. If an organization has requirements to implement the control production quality process area, it's important to identify that as early as possible because it can increase implementation scope. It's also important to recognize that these processes are often executed in "best of breed" specialized systems that are unique by industry. In that case, integrations to such systems may be required as part of the Dynamics 365 implementation.

processes.title: Run production operations
processes.description: The run production operations business process area covers the activities in an organization's internal production process. Any manufacturing organization finds it critical to track and control production operations. The goal is to ensure consistent product quality and minimize production costs. Running production operations also requires coordination and communication between many departments, such as engineering, operations, quality, sales, planning, and procurement. The process for executing production operations varies from business to business, depending on industry and product, but it follows the same basic steps. At the beginning of production, materials are consumed into the process. A combination of people and tools or machines then run the specific production steps. Finally, the sub-assembly or finished good is created as the output of the process. The definition of these steps is done as part of the Design to retire end-to-end business processes and refined further in the define production strategies business process area. Define this business process at the beginning of an implementation of Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. It's a foundational process for any manufacturing company.

processes.title: Release production to the shop floor
processes.description: This process in Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations production module involves transitioning a planned or scheduled production order from the planning phase into active execution on the shop floor. This process starts when a production order is confirmed and all necessary materials, drawings, and documentation are prepared and provided to the production team. The release triggers procurement of any required raw materials not already in stock, and ensures that all relevant information—such as shop drawings, specifications, and instructions—is communicated to the appropriate supervisors or workers. In practice, this step formalizes the start of manufacturing activities, allowing workers to begin assembling, fabricating, or processing items according to the order’s requirements. The process also establishes accountability for tracking progress, managing inventory consumption, and updating order status as work proceeds. By releasing production to the shop floor, organizations ensure that production activities are coordinated, resources are allocated efficiently, and the transition from planning to execution is clearly documented, supporting accurate reporting, cost tracking, and timely fulfillment of customer or internal orders.

processes.title: Source to pay
processes.description: The source (previously procure) to pay process (also known as purchase to pay) is a term used to describe the entire process of purchasing goods or services from a supplier and paying for them. The process includes all the steps from the initial procurement request to the final payment to the supplier. The procure to pay process typically includes the following steps: Identify the need for goods or services: This process covers both indirect procurement, where the goods or services are not related to the good or service being sold, and direct procurement, where demand for the goods or services exists within the production or sales processes. Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management supports flexible procurement processes based on business needs. These processes include request for quotations (RFQs), purchase requisitions, contracts (purchase agreements or blanket orders), and purchase orders which can be planned or unplanned. Planned purchase orders can be generated automatically from supply or demand forecasts present. Learn more at Forecast to plan introduction. Supplier selection: T he procurement team evaluates potential suppliers and selects the one that meets the requirements. Dynamics 365 also includes functionality to help automate the supplier selection and portal capabilities to allow suppliers to apply online or even respond to requests for quotations. Purchase order creation: A purchase order is created and sent to the supplier. It specifies the goods or services required, the price, delivery date, and other terms and conditions. With Dynamics 365, the process may include a purchase requisition, purchase agreement (also known as a contract or blanket order), or a request for quotation. Invoice receipt and verification: The supplier sends an invoice for the goods or services, and the invoice is checked for accuracy and completeness. Dynamics 365 includes full AP automation capabilities with OCR through Azure Form Recognizer to assist with this process. Invoice approval: The invoice is approved for payment, and the accounts payable team processes the payment. Payment: The supplier is paid for the goods or services, usually by electronic funds transfer. Record keeping: All relevant documents, including the purchase order, invoice, and payment details, are recorded and stored for future reference. Reporting: Financial and operational report analysis help keep track of performance of the procure to pay process. You can include supply risk analysis, purchase order backorders, vendor performance, and spend analysis. The procure to pay process is a crucial aspect of business operations, and efficient execution can result in cost savings, increased transparency, and better supplier relationships. Important: The process defined here does not include the goods receipt process. Learn more at Inventory to deliver. Every organization has variations to procure to pay. Here, we define the basic outline for any organization looking to implement a technology solution to support the procure to pay process.

processes.description: Sourcing and procurement strategies are outlined for both materials and services that are needed within your organization. During this process, the sourcing or procurement teams collaborate with several different departments focusing on three primary areas: price/cost, lead time, and quality. This business process area mainly covers: Defining procurement process to outline overall procurement strategy for both material and services that are needed within your organization Defining procurement and sourcing policies to reduce financial risk that organization is taking and ensure compliance requirements are met and proper approvals are completed before any procurement transactions can be processed Creating and updating pricing contracts after vendor evaluation and selection, and analyzing product proposals. Developing procurement and sourcing strategies is a critical step at the beginning of your implementation. However, this will continue to be refined over time as your business and operations change and evolve to support your organization's goals and objectives. It's important to continually evaluate all procurement and sourcing strategies to ensure you're receiving the best pricing, lead time, and quality for your products and services.

processes.title: Develop procurement catalogs
processes.description: Develop procurement catalogs establishes a governed, user-friendly buying experience by organizing approved goods and services into internal catalogs, connecting to supplier webstores via punchout, enabling vendor self‑service contributions, and importing supplier product lists to keep content current and compliant. Scope and intended outcomes This process standardizes how employees discover items during requisitioning, ensures negotiated prices and terms are applied, shortens cycle time, and improves spend compliance. It spans catalog strategy and hierarchy design, internal catalog curation, external punchout enablement (cXML/OCI), vendor self‑service contributions through a portal, and scheduled imports to refresh products and prices. Core concepts to anchor the design Procurement catalogs can expose stock and non‑stock items or category-only lines for services; a category hierarchy supports both itemized and non‑itemized purchasing, and is typically defined early in the ERP program so downstream requisition and PO flows align. External (punchout) catalogs let requesters shop on a supplier’s site and return a validated cart to your requisition, commonly via cXML; this avoids duplicating large assortments while keeping approvals and accounting in your system of record. Vendor self‑service (supplier collaboration portal) reduces buyer workload by letting vendors maintain item attributes, confirmations, and price lists within governance boundaries. Vendor catalog import brings supplier items, pricing, and attributes into your internal catalogs using governed templates and mappings, ensuring searchability and price accuracy at scale. Catalog types you’ll typically combine Internal procurement catalogs: curated lists of items/services with categories, attributes, UOM, approved vendors, and trade/agreement pricing; ideal for frequently purchased goods and internal service menus. External punchout catalogs: supplier-hosted assortments accessed from your requisitioning UI; appropriate when assortments change frequently or are too large to maintain internally. Hybrid catalogs: internal for core SKUs plus punchout for long tails and specialized categories (e.g., MRO, IT accessories). Governance decisions and data model Define the procurement category hierarchy (depth, naming, coding), mandatory attributes, and approval policies by category. Establish catalog ownership (Category Manager, Buyer), SLAs for updates, and quality rules for item data (images, tax attributes, UNSPSC, substitutes). Align security so employees see only catalogs relevant to their role, region, cost center, and contract entitlements. Plan import formats and validations (e.g., cXML, CSV) and map supplier attributes to your canonical schema to support search facets and analytical rollups. Integration and experience design Requisition experience: employees browse catalogs filtered by policy; accounting is derived via category mapping and budgets can be checked before approval. Punchout: configure the supplier connection, authentication, and return cart mapping; decide which categories route to punchout versus internal items. Vendor self‑service: enable selected suppliers to propose items or maintain pricing via the collaboration portal under workflow and audit. High - level process Assess scope and policies: confirm which categories and suppliers will be catalog‑driven, which will use punchout, and which will remain free‑text or RFQ‑led; confirm approval thresholds and budget rules. Design the catalog hierarchy: define category tree, attribute sets, and required data for items and services (including non‑itemized service categories) to support requisitioning and analytics. Configure internal catalogs: create catalogs, assign products and categories, attach price/trade agreements, and set visibility/security for requester groups. Enable punchout suppliers: establish external catalog connections (e.g., cXML), map categories to the supplier’s scope, and test round‑trip cart and accounting defaults. Set up vendor self‑service: grant portal access, define what vendors can maintain (prices, lead times, substitutions), and route changes through workflow with audit. Import vendor products: agree on file formats and cadence; validate content against your schema; load items and prices; link to catalogs and categories; log exceptions for supplier remediation. Pilot and refine: run a pilot with key requesters and suppliers; measure findability, price coverage, and approval cycle time; adjust hierarchy, attributes, and visibility. Launch with guided buying: publish catalogs, provide “how‑to” tips in the requisition workspace, and communicate when to use internal vs. punchout. Operate and refresh: monitor price accuracy, broken links, and stale items; schedule vendor catalog imports; audit portal changes; retire duplicate or low‑use content. Expand coverage: add categories and new punchout partners; introduce supplier-managed content for fast‑moving categories under tighter guardrails. Roles and responsibilities Procurement Category Manager: owns hierarchy, curation standards, and catalog roadmap; approves supplier‑submitted changes. Buyer/Procurement Operations: configures catalogs, manages imports, resolves data exceptions, and monitors punchout uptime. Supplier (via portal): maintains agreed product and price data; responds to content quality feedback; complies with update schedules. Requester: follows catalog policies; uses approved catalogs or punchout; avoids free‑text when catalog coverage exists. Dynamics 365 product support Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management provides procurement category hierarchies, internal catalog setup, purchasing policies, and the supplier collaboration portal; it supports punchout catalogs and mapping of external carts back to requisitions. Vendor catalog import capabilities let you bring in supplier items and prices and attach them to your catalogs with governed templates. Source‑to‑pay solution guidance highlights “Punch‑out catalogs” and “Vendor collaboration portal” in the standard capability map, confirming fit within the L2/L3 process model. Operational controls and KPIs Institute change workflows, reason codes, and periodic reviews; segregate duties between content authors and approvers. Track: catalog coverage (% of spend via catalogs), punchout success rate, search-to-add time, price variance vs. contract, stale item rate, and supplier content SLA adherence.

processes.title: Create external punch out catalogs in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
processes.description: External punch out catalogs in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management allow organizations to connect directly to supplier-hosted catalogs via standard protocols (e.g., cXML, OCI). Users can "punch out" from Dynamics 365 to the supplier's website, select items, and return the shopping cart to Dynamics 365 for requisition and approval. This approach ensures real-time access to supplier offerings, negotiated pricing, and up-to-date product information, while maintaining control over the procurement process within Dynamics 365. Punch out catalogs support seamless integration with supplier e-commerce platforms, automating data exchange and reducing manual entry errors.

processes.title: Create vendor self-service catalogs in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
processes.description: Vendor self-service catalogs in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management empower suppliers to manage and update their own catalog offerings via a secure portal. Vendors can submit new products, update pricing, and maintain item details, subject to buyer review and approval. This self-service model reduces administrative overhead, improves data accuracy, and accelerates the onboarding of new items. The portal supports workflow-driven approvals, compliance checks, and integration with procurement processes, ensuring that only validated items are available for requisition.

processes.title: Develop supplier segments
processes.description: Develop supplier segments organizes the vendor base into meaningful groups so procurement can target sourcing strategies, enforce policies, track supplier diversity, and optimize buying outcomes across categories, regions, and business units. This process supports both portal-driven segmentation (via supplier collaboration) and manual maintenance in the ERP, and it explicitly includes supplier diversity attributes and purchasing demographics. Scope and outcomes The process defines the segmentation framework, enriches suppliers with the attributes that place them into segments, and keeps those segments current as suppliers onboard, update certifications, or performance shifts. Outcomes include clear segment definitions (e.g., strategic vs. transactional), validated diversity classifications, visibility into purchasing demographics (who buys from whom, where, and for what), and segment-specific playbooks for sourcing, risk, and performance management. Segmentation model (what to capture) Business identity: legal entity, parent/child relationships, tax IDs, NAICS/industry, geography. Commercial markers: category fit, price lists/trade agreements, contract status, capacity/lead times, delivery lanes. Risk and compliance: sanctions/KYC status, insurance, sustainability/ESG attestations, cybersecurity posture. Performance: on‑time delivery, quality metrics, responsiveness, dispute rate, claim history. Diversity: minority‑owned, women‑owned, veteran‑owned, disability‑owned, LGBTQ+‑owned, small/disadvantaged business, indigenous, local/regional designations; certification bodies; effective/expiry dates. Purchasing demographics: spend by business unit/region/cost center, category mix, order frequency, average PO value, tail vs. strategic spend share. Data sources (how it gets populated) Supplier collaboration portal self‑service forms for profile, certifications, banking, sustainability and diversity disclosures, with evidence uploads and dates. Manual entry in system for vendor groups, classifications, category assignments, and policy flags when portal is not in scope. Controlled imports (CSV/cXML/API) from supplier registries (e.g., diversity certifiers), CLM systems, and performance data from receiving/quality modules. Operating model Portal‑driven segmentation: suppliers submit/maintain profile and certifications; workflows validate and place suppliers into segments automatically based on rules. Manual in‑system segmentation: procurement analysts assign vendor groups, risk scores, diversity flags, and category memberships directly in ERP when collaboration is unavailable or during transition. Hybrid: start manual to establish baseline, then transition segments to portal upkeep; keep critical attributes under workflow (e.g., bank changes, diversity certification). High‑level process Define segment taxonomy and rules Set the canonical list of segments (e.g., strategic, preferred, qualified, tail), diversity attributes, and risk tiers; publish the decision rules and data dictionary. Configure master data and security Create vendor groups/classes, category associations, mandatory attributes, and approval workflows. Set role‑based access for who can view/change sensitive fields. Enable the supplier collaboration portal Publish onboarding questionnaires, required documents, and self‑service profile pages for diversity, sustainability, and banking; map each field to ERP attributes. Collect and validate data Intake portal submissions and imports; validate certifications (issuer, number, effective/expiry), run basic KYC/sanctions checks, and flag missing or expired evidence. Apply segmentation rules Assign segment, risk tier, and diversity status based on rules (e.g., spend thresholds, category fit, performance, certifications). Record effective dates and rationale. Enrich with purchasing demographics Link historic and rolling spend by BU/region/category to the supplier record; compute purchase frequency, order size, and tail‑spend indicators to refine segment placement. Approve and publish segments Route changes through workflow for procurement/category manager approval; publish segments to sourcing, requisitioning policies, and supplier performance dashboards. Govern usage in downstream processes Bind segments to policies (e.g., RFQ routing to “preferred,” auto‑blocks for “not qualified,” diversity‑spend targets in analytics, guided buying recommendations). Monitor and refresh Schedule reviews for expiring certifications, material performance shifts, M&A events; automatically notify suppliers via portal to update expiring documents. Improve the model Review segment drift vs. outcomes (savings, risk incidents, diversity‑spend attainment); refine rules and thresholds; retire unused attributes. Roles and responsibilities Procurement/category manager: owns taxonomy, thresholds, and approvals; resolves exceptions. Supplier onboarding/operations: validates submissions, runs checks, and manages workflows. Diversity & inclusion lead (or ESG): defines accepted certification bodies and target reporting. Risk/compliance: maintains KYC/sanctions rules, approves sensitive changes. Finance/AP: verifies banking and tax data; ensures SoD and auditability. Business stakeholders: supply purchasing demographics and feedback on supplier fit. Dynamics 365 support Vendor information management and vendor groups/classifications for segments, risk, and policies. Supplier collaboration portal for self‑service profile maintenance, confirmations, and document upload. Purchasing policies that reference vendor groups/segments to allow/deny categories or enforce RFQs. Trade agreements and approved vendor list to bind segments to price/contract usage. Analytics via Power BI/Microsoft Fabric to report diversity spend, segment performance, tail spend, and purchasing demographics. Supplier diversity and purchasing demographics (practical guidance) Diversity capture: model diversity as structured fields with certification authority, certificate ID, effective/expiry, and attach artifacts; differentiate self‑attested vs. certified. Targets and tracking: define percentage goals (e.g., percent of addressable spend to certified diverse suppliers) by category and region; monitor progress monthly. Purchasing demographics: publish a quarterly heatmap showing who buys from which segments by business unit and location; use it to rebalance work to diverse/preferred suppliers without increasing risk. Guardrails: enforce evidence-on-file rules for diversity claims and auto‑expire designations upon certificate expiry; route reinstatement through validation workflow. Operational controls and KPIs Controls: maker‑checker for profile changes; workflowed approvals for risk/diversity flags; automated reminders for expiring certifications; audit trails for attribute changes. processes.title: Collect supplier information in the vendor collaboration portal with Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
processes.description: Develop supplier segments organizes the vendor base into meaningful groups so procurement can target sourcing strategies, enforce policies, track supplier diversity, and optimize buying outcomes across categories, regions, and business units. This process supports both portal-driven segmentation (via supplier collaboration) and manual maintenance in the ERP, and it explicitly includes supplier diversity attributes and purchasing demographics. Scope and outcomes The process defines the segmentation framework, enriches suppliers with the attributes that place them into segments, and keeps those segments current as suppliers onboard, update certifications, or performance shifts. Outcomes include clear segment definitions (e.g., strategic vs. transactional), validated diversity classifications, visibility into purchasing demographics (who buys from whom, where, and for what), and segment-specific playbooks for sourcing, risk, and performance management. Segmentation model (what to capture) * Business identity: legal entity, parent/child relationships, tax IDs, NAICS/industry, geography. * Commercial markers: category fit, price lists/trade agreements, contract status, capacity/lead times, delivery lanes. * Risk and compliance: sanctions/KYC status, insurance, sustainability/ESG attestations, cybersecurity posture. * Performance: on‑time delivery, quality metrics, responsiveness, dispute rate, claim history. * Diversity: minority‑owned, women‑owned, veteran‑owned, disability‑owned, LGBTQ+‑owned, small/disadvantaged business, indigenous, local/regional designations; certification bodies; effective/expiry dates. * Purchasing demographics: spend by business unit/region/cost center, category mix, order frequency, average PO value, tail vs. strategic spend share. Data sources (how it gets populated) * Supplier collaboration portal self‑service forms for profile, certifications, banking, sustainability and diversity disclosures, with evidence uploads and dates. * Manual entry in system for vendor groups, classifications, category assignments, and policy flags when portal is not in scope. * Controlled imports (CSV/cXML/API) from supplier registries (e.g., diversity certifiers), CLM systems, and performance data from receiving/quality modules. Operating model * Portal‑driven segmentation: suppliers submit/maintain profile and certifications; workflows validate and place suppliers into segments automatically based on rules. * Manual in‑system segmentation: procurement analysts assign vendor groups, risk scores, diversity flags, and category memberships directly in ERP when collaboration is unavailable or during transition. * Hybrid: start manual to establish baseline, then transition segments to portal upkeep; keep critical attributes under workflow (e.g., bank changes, diversity certification). High‑level process 1. Define segment taxonomy and rules * Set the canonical list of segments (e.g., strategic, preferred, qualified, tail), diversity attributes, and risk tiers; publish the decision rules and data dictionary. 2. Configure master data and security * Create vendor groups/classes, category associations, mandatory attributes, and approval workflows. Set role‑based access for who can view/change sensitive fields. 3. Enable the supplier collaboration portal * Publish onboarding questionnaires, required documents, and self‑service profile pages for diversity, sustainability, and banking; map each field to ERP attributes. 4. Collect and validate data * Intake portal submissions and imports; validate certifications (issuer, number, effective/expiry), run basic KYC/sanctions checks, and flag missing or expired evidence. 5. Apply segmentation rules * Assign segment, risk tier, and diversity status based on rules (e.g., spend thresholds, category fit, performance, certifications). Record effective dates and rationale. 6. Enrich with purchasing demographics * Link historic and rolling spend by BU/region/category to the supplier record; compute purchase frequency, order size, and tail‑spend indicators to refine segment placement. 7. Approve and publish segments * Route changes through workflow for procurement/category manager approval; publish segments to sourcing, requisitioning policies, and supplier performance dashboards. 8. Govern usage in downstream processes * Bind segments to policies (e.g., RFQ routing to “preferred,” auto‑blocks for “not qualified,” diversity‑spend targets in analytics, guided buying recommendations). 9. Monitor and refresh * Schedule reviews for expiring certifications, material performance shifts, M&A events; automatically notify suppliers via portal to update expiring documents. 10. Improve the model * Review segment drift vs. outcomes (savings, risk incidents, diversity‑spend attainment); refine rules and thresholds; retire unused attributes. Roles and responsibilities * Procurement/category manager: owns taxonomy, thresholds, and approvals; resolves exceptions. * Supplier onboarding/operations: validates submissions, runs checks, and manages workflows. * Diversity & inclusion lead (or ESG): defines accepted certification bodies and target reporting. * Risk/compliance: maintains KYC/sanctions rules, approves sensitive changes. * Finance/AP: verifies banking and tax data; ensures SoD and auditability. * Business stakeholders: supply purchasing demographics and feedback on supplier fit. Dynamics 365 support * Vendor information management and vendor groups/classifications for segments, risk, and policies. * Supplier collaboration portal for self‑service profile maintenance, confirmations, and document upload. * Purchasing policies that reference vendor groups/segments to allow/deny categories or enforce RFQs. * Trade agreements and approved vendor list to bind segments to price/contract usage. * Analytics via Power BI/Microsoft Fabric to report diversity spend, segment performance, tail spend, and purchasing demographics. Supplier diversity and purchasing demographics (practical guidance) * Diversity capture: model diversity as structured fields with certification authority, certificate ID, effective/expiry, and attach artifacts; differentiate self‑attested vs. certified. * Targets and tracking: define percentage goals (e.g., percent of addressable spend to certified diverse suppliers) by category and region; monitor progress monthly. * Purchasing demographics: publish a quarterly heatmap showing who buys from which segments by business unit and location; use it to rebalance work to diverse/preferred suppliers without increasing risk. * Guardrails: enforce evidence-on-file rules for diversity claims and auto‑expire designations upon certificate expiry; route reinstatement through validation workflow. Operational controls and KPIs * Controls: maker‑checker for profile changes; workflowed approvals for risk/diversity flags; automated reminders for expiring certifications; audit trails for attribute changes. * KPIs: percent of spend through preferred/strategic segments; diverse‑supplier spend attainment; number of active diverse suppliers by category/region; average time to validate new supplier; share of tail spend; policy violations avoided; data completeness score for vendor profiles. Deliverables * Segmentation taxonomy and data dictionary. * Configured vendor groups/classifications and workflows. * Onboarding questionnaires and document lists (portal). * Diversity certification playbook and accepted issuers list. * Dashboards: diversity spend, purchasing demographics, segment performance.

Procurement teams can leverage built-in analytics and reporting to assess spend with diverse suppliers, support regulatory and corporate social responsibility initiatives, and inform sourcing strategies. The scenario is designed to facilitate transparency, compliance, and strategic supplier segmentation.
