processes.title: Develop procurement policies
processes.description: Develop supplier segments organizes the vendor base into meaningful groups so procurement can target sourcing strategies, enforce policies, track supplier diversity, and optimize buying outcomes across categories, regions, and business units. This process supports both portal-driven segmentation (via supplier collaboration) and manual maintenance in the ERP, and it explicitly includes supplier diversity attributes and purchasing demographics. Scope and outcomes The process defines the segmentation framework, enriches suppliers with the attributes that place them into segments, and keeps those segments current as suppliers onboard, update certifications, or performance shifts. Outcomes include clear segment definitions (e.g., strategic vs. transactional), validated diversity classifications, visibility into purchasing demographics (who buys from whom, where, and for what), and segment-specific playbooks for sourcing, risk, and performance management. Segmentation model (what to capture) Business identity: legal entity, parent/child relationships, tax IDs, NAICS/industry, geography. Commercial markers: category fit, price lists/trade agreements, contract status, capacity/lead times, delivery lanes. Risk and compliance: sanctions/KYC status, insurance, sustainability/ESG attestations, cybersecurity posture. Performance: on‑time delivery, quality metrics, responsiveness, dispute rate, claim history. Diversity: minority‑owned, women‑owned, veteran‑owned, disability‑owned, LGBTQ+‑owned, small/disadvantaged business, indigenous, local/regional designations; certification bodies; effective/expiry dates. Purchasing demographics: spend by business unit/region/cost center, category mix, order frequency, average PO value, tail vs. strategic spend share. Data sources (how it gets populated) Supplier collaboration portal self‑service forms for profile, certifications, banking, sustainability and diversity disclosures, with evidence uploads and dates. Manual entry in system for vendor groups, classifications, category assignments, and policy flags when portal is not in scope. Controlled imports (CSV/cXML/API) from supplier registries (e.g., diversity certifiers), CLM systems, and performance data from receiving/quality modules. Operating model Portal‑driven segmentation: suppliers submit/maintain profile and certifications; workflows validate and place suppliers into segments automatically based on rules. Manual in‑system segmentation: procurement analysts assign vendor groups, risk scores, diversity flags, and category memberships directly in ERP when collaboration is unavailable or during transition. Hybrid: start manual to establish baseline, then transition segments to portal upkeep; keep critical attributes under workflow (e.g., bank changes, diversity certification). High‑level process Define segment taxonomy and rules Set the canonical list of segments (e.g., strategic, preferred, qualified, tail), diversity attributes, and risk tiers; publish the decision rules and data dictionary. Configure master data and security Create vendor groups/classes, category associations, mandatory attributes, and approval workflows. Set role‑based access for who can view/change sensitive fields. Enable the supplier collaboration portal Publish onboarding questionnaires, required documents, and self‑service profile pages for diversity, sustainability, and banking; map each field to ERP attributes. Collect and validate data Intake portal submissions and imports; validate certifications (issuer, number, effective/expiry), run basic KYC/sanctions checks, and flag missing or expired evidence. Apply segmentation rules Assign segment, risk tier, and diversity status based on rules (e.g., spend thresholds, category fit, performance, certifications). Record effective dates and rationale. Enrich with purchasing demographics Link historic and rolling spend by BU/region/category to the supplier record; compute purchase frequency, order size, and tail‑spend indicators to refine segment placement. Approve and publish segments Route changes through workflow for procurement/category manager approval; publish segments to sourcing, requisitioning policies, and supplier performance dashboards. Govern usage in downstream processes Bind segments to policies (e.g., RFQ routing to “preferred,” auto‑blocks for “not qualified,” diversity‑spend targets in analytics, guided buying recommendations). Monitor and refresh Schedule reviews for expiring certifications, material performance shifts, M&A events; automatically notify suppliers via portal to update expiring documents. Improve the model Review segment drift vs. outcomes (savings, risk incidents, diversity‑spend attainment); refine rules and thresholds; retire unused attributes. Roles and responsibilities Procurement/category manager: owns taxonomy, thresholds, and approvals; resolves exceptions. Supplier onboarding/operations: validates submissions, runs checks, and manages workflows. Diversity & inclusion lead (or ESG): defines accepted certification bodies and target reporting. Risk/compliance: maintains KYC/sanctions rules, approves sensitive changes. Finance/AP: verifies banking and tax data; ensures SoD and auditability. Business stakeholders: supply purchasing demographics and feedback on supplier fit. Dynamics 365 support Vendor information management and vendor groups/classifications for segments, risk, and policies. Supplier collaboration portal for self‑service profile maintenance, confirmations, and document upload. Purchasing policies that reference vendor groups/segments to allow/deny categories or enforce RFQs. Trade agreements and approved vendor list to bind segments to price/contract usage. Analytics via Power BI/Microsoft Fabric to report diversity spend, segment performance, tail spend, and purchasing demographics. Supplier diversity and purchasing demographics (practical guidance) Diversity capture: model diversity as structured fields with certification authority, certificate ID, effective/expiry, and attach artifacts; differentiate self‑attested vs. certified. Targets and tracking: define percentage goals (e.g., percent of addressable spend to certified diverse suppliers) by category and region; monitor progress monthly. Purchasing demographics: publish a quarterly heatmap showing who buys from which segments by business unit and location; use it to rebalance work to diverse/preferred suppliers without increasing risk. Guardrails: enforce evidence-on-file rules for diversity claims and auto‑expire designations upon certificate expiry; route reinstatement through validation workflow. Operational controls and KPIs Controls: maker‑checker for profile changes; workflow approvals for risk/diversity flags; automated reminders for expiring certifications; audit trails for attribute changes. KPIs: percent of spend through preferred/strategic segments; diverse‑supplier spend attainment; number of active diverse suppliers by category/region; average time to validate new supplier; share of tail spend; policy violations avoided; data completeness score for vendor profiles. Deliverables Segmentation taxonomy and data dictionary. Configured vendor groups/classifications and workflows. Onboarding questionnaires and document lists (portal). Diversity certification playbook and accepted issuers list. Dashboards: diversity spend, purchasing demographics, segment performance.

processes.description: Develop supplier segments organizes the vendor base into meaningful groups so procurement can target sourcing strategies, enforce policies, track supplier diversity, and optimize buying outcomes across categories, regions, and business units. This process supports both portal-driven segmentation (via supplier collaboration) and manual maintenance in the ERP, and it explicitly includes supplier diversity attributes and purchasing demographics. Scope and outcomes The process defines the segmentation framework, enriches suppliers with the attributes that place them into segments, and keeps those segments current as suppliers onboard, update certifications, or performance shifts. Outcomes include clear segment definitions (e.g., strategic vs. transactional), validated diversity classifications, visibility into purchasing demographics (who buys from whom, where, and for what), and segment-specific playbooks for sourcing, risk, and performance management. Segmentation model (what to capture) * Business identity: legal entity, parent/child relationships, tax IDs, NAICS/industry, geography. * Commercial markers: category fit, price lists/trade agreements, contract status, capacity/lead times, delivery lanes. * Risk and compliance: sanctions/KYC status, insurance, sustainability/ESG attestations, cybersecurity posture. * Performance: on‑time delivery, quality metrics, responsiveness, dispute rate, claim history. * Diversity: minority‑owned, women‑owned, veteran‑owned, disability‑owned, LGBTQ+‑owned, small/disadvantaged business, indigenous, local/regional designations; certification bodies; effective/expiry dates. * Purchasing demographics: spend by business unit/region/cost center, category mix, order frequency, average PO value, tail vs. strategic spend share. Data sources (how it gets populated) * Supplier collaboration portal self‑service forms for profile, certifications, banking, sustainability and diversity disclosures, with evidence uploads and dates. * Manual entry in system for vendor groups, classifications, category assignments, and policy flags when portal is not in scope. * Controlled imports (CSV/cXML/API) from supplier registries (e.g., diversity certifiers), CLM systems, and performance data from receiving/quality modules. Operating model * Portal‑driven segmentation: suppliers submit/maintain profile and certifications; workflows validate and place suppliers into segments automatically based on rules. * Manual in‑system segmentation: procurement analysts assign vendor groups, risk scores, diversity flags, and category memberships directly in ERP when collaboration is unavailable or during transition. * Hybrid: start manual to establish baseline, then transition segments to portal upkeep; keep critical attributes under workflow (e.g., bank changes, diversity certification). High‑level process 1. Define segment taxonomy and rules * Set the canonical list of segments (e.g., strategic, preferred, qualified, tail), diversity attributes, and risk tiers; publish the decision rules and data dictionary. 2. Configure master data and security * Create vendor groups/classes, category associations, mandatory attributes, and approval workflows. Set role‑based access for who can view/change sensitive fields. 3. Enable the supplier collaboration portal * Publish onboarding questionnaires, required documents, and self‑service profile pages for diversity, sustainability, and banking; map each field to ERP attributes. 4. Collect and validate data * Intake portal submissions and imports; validate certifications (issuer, number, effective/expiry), run basic KYC/sanctions checks, and flag missing or expired evidence. 5. Apply segmentation rules * Assign segment, risk tier, and diversity status based on rules (e.g., spend thresholds, category fit, performance, certifications). Record effective dates and rationale. 6. Enrich with purchasing demographics * Link historic and rolling spend by BU/region/category to the supplier record; compute purchase frequency, order size, and tail‑spend indicators to refine segment placement. 7. Approve and publish segments * Route changes through workflow for procurement/category manager approval; publish segments to sourcing, requisitioning policies, and supplier performance dashboards. 8. Govern usage in downstream processes * Bind segments to policies (e.g., RFQ routing to “preferred,” auto‑blocks for “not qualified,” diversity‑spend targets in analytics, guided buying recommendations). 9. Monitor and refresh * Schedule reviews for expiring certifications, material performance shifts, M&A events; automatically notify suppliers via portal to update expiring documents. 10. Improve the model * Review segment drift vs. outcomes (savings, risk incidents, diversity‑spend attainment); refine rules and thresholds; retire unused attributes. Roles and responsibilities * Procurement/category manager: owns taxonomy, thresholds, and approvals; resolves exceptions. * Supplier onboarding/operations: validates submissions, runs checks, and manages workflows. * Diversity & inclusion lead (or ESG): defines accepted certification bodies and target reporting. * Risk/compliance: maintains KYC/sanctions rules, approves sensitive changes. * Finance/AP: verifies banking and tax data; ensures SoD and auditability. * Business stakeholders: supply purchasing demographics and feedback on supplier fit. Dynamics 365 support * Vendor information management and vendor groups/classifications for segments, risk, and policies. * Supplier collaboration portal for self‑service profile maintenance, confirmations, and document upload. * Purchasing policies that reference vendor groups/segments to allow/deny categories or enforce RFQs. * Trade agreements and approved vendor list to bind segments to price/contract usage. * Analytics via Power BI/Microsoft Fabric to report diversity spend, segment performance, tail spend, and purchasing demographics. Supplier diversity and purchasing demographics (practical guidance) * Diversity capture: model diversity as structured fields with certification authority, certificate ID, effective/expiry, and attach artifacts; differentiate self‑attested vs. certified. * Targets and tracking: define percentage goals (e.g., percent of addressable spend to certified diverse suppliers) by category and region; monitor progress monthly. * Purchasing demographics: publish a quarterly heatmap showing who buys from which segments by business unit and location; use it to rebalance work to diverse/preferred suppliers without increasing risk. * Guardrails: enforce evidence-on-file rules for diversity claims and auto‑expire designations upon certificate expiry; route reinstatement through validation workflow. Operational controls and KPIs * Controls: maker‑checker for profile changes; workflow approvals for risk/diversity flags; automated reminders for expiring certifications; audit trails for attribute changes. * KPIs: percent of spend through preferred/strategic segments; diverse‑supplier spend attainment; number of active diverse suppliers by category/region; average time to validate new supplier; share of tail spend; policy violations avoided; data completeness score for vendor profiles. Deliverables * Segmentation taxonomy and data dictionary. * Configured vendor groups/classifications and workflows. * Onboarding questionnaires and document lists (portal). * Diversity certification playbook and accepted issuers list. * Dashboards: diversity spend, purchasing demographics, segment performance.

processes.title: Define accounts payable policies
processes.description: Define accounts payable policies establishes a single, governed rulebook for how your organization receives, validates, approves, pays, and accounts for supplier invoices—covering invoice matching, exceptions, cash discounts, payment methods, prepayments, rebates/allowances, and audit controls so AP is fast, compliant, and predictable. Scope and objectives Standardize AP across legal entities for invoicing, payments, cash discounting, prepayments, supplier rebates/allowances, and exceptions, with clear approval matrices and segregation of duties (SoD). Encode policies as system behavior (workflows, tolerances, holds, and validations) in Dynamics 365 Finance to reduce cycle time and errors. Invoicing policies Invoice intake channels and requirements: define accepted channels (EDI/PEPPOL, vendor portal, email/OCR), mandatory header/line data, tax/VAT rules, and duplicate detection. In Dynamics 365 Finance, use invoice matching (two‑way/three‑way/totals) with variance tolerances; breaches route to workflow before posting. Matching and tolerances: set price/quantity/total thresholds by category or vendor; use three‑way matching where receiving is required; log and resolve discrepancies before posting. Non‑PO invoice policy: strictly limit categories that may bypass matching; enforce specialty approval and SoD; document required supporting evidence. Dispute management: define timelines and roles to resolve price/quantity defects and short‑shipments; hold invoices from payment until resolved. Payment policies Payment run cadence and proposal rules: standardize weekly/biweekly runs using payment proposals (due‑date and cash‑discount date logic) with review/approval checkpoints. Methods of payment: permit ACH/wire/promissory notes; define positive pay and file formats; restrict checks and mandate treasury review for new methods/partners. Configure Positive Pay and payment types/fees in AP. Centralized payments and cross‑company: enable centralized AP where appropriate; set bank validation and reversal policies; log approvals for manual wires. Single Payment Requests (ad hoc): prohibit use when a PO is required; enforce privacy/SSPA and anti‑corruption controls; require controller approval for prepayments. Cash discounting policies Terms and calculations: define standard terms, discount bases (tax included/excluded), and treatment of under/over‑payments; permit “outside window” discounts only under defined approvals. Configure “cash discount is calculated including tax” and cash‑discount administration settings. Payment selection: use payment proposals to prioritize invoices by discount date, then due date. Prepayments and advances Distinguish prepayment invoices vs. prepayments; require controller approval, proof‑of‑execution after service, and recovery for undelivered goods—no “parking of funds.” Supplier rebates and trade allowances Define eligibility, accrual method, required evidence, approval flow, and settlement cadence; align AP handling with procurement contracts/rebate programs. Data governance, risk, and compliance Vendor master controls: workflow for vendor creation and bank changes, SSPA/privacy prerequisites, sanctions screening, and diversity classifications where required. SoD and auditability: dual control for bank edits and payments over threshold; versioned policy repository; retention and traceable approvals (MSApprovals). KPIs and guardrails First‑pass match rate; invoice exception rate; average days to approve; on‑time payment rate; cash discount captured vs. lost; positive pay exceptions; duplicate‑invoice prevention rate; prepayment recovery rate. High - level process 1) Define policy framework and decision rights (owners, SoD, approval matrices). Publish a versioned AP Policy Handbook and change process. 2) Translate policies into system controls: configure matching methods/tolerances, required fields, workflows, and holds in AP. 3) Set payment governance: payment proposal criteria, payment methods, positive pay, centralized payments, and reversal rules. 4) Establish cash‑discount rules and selection logic; align treasury calendars to capture discounts. 5) Define prepayment controls and documentation (controller approvals, POE collection, recovery rules). 6) Codify non‑PO invoice exceptions and specialty categories; enforce workflows and documentation. 7) Implement vendor governance: onboarding, bank validation workflows, SSPA/privacy sanctions checks. 8) Roll out training, supplier guides (invoicing requirements, e‑invoice/EDI specs, positive pay remittance details). 9) Monitor and improve: track KPIs, audit exceptions, and refine thresholds; run quarterly policy reviews. Roles and responsibilities AP Manager: owns daily operations, exception queues, and KPI reporting; maintains matching and tolerance policies. Controller: owns approval matrices, prepayment and non‑PO exception governance, and audit readiness. Treasury: owns payment methods, bank relationships, positive pay, and wire approvals. Procurement: aligns invoice requirements to contracts, vendor terms, and rebates; ensures PO integrity and change‑management workflows. Risk/Compliance: monitors SoD, sanctions/privacy adherence, and policy enforcement. Dynamics 365 configuration pointers Accounts payable home: vendor payment setup (methods, fees, terms); positive pay; payment proposals; centralized payments; reversals. Invoice matching: define totals/two‑way/three‑way matching with variance icons and tolerance thresholds; block posting outside tolerance. Payment proposals: select by due date or cash‑discount date; schedule and review prior to posting. Cash discounts: configure discount codes/series, tax‑inclusive calculation, and under/over‑payment handling. Deliverables AP Policy Handbook (version‑controlled) and Approval/Signing Limit Matrix; Supplier Invoicing Guide; Payment Methods Playbook; Prepayment & POE Checklist; Matching & Tolerance Matrix; KPIs dashboard (Power BI).

Dynamics 365 configuration pointers * Accounts payable home: vendor payment setup (methods, fees, terms); positive pay; payment proposals; centralized payments; reversals. * Invoice matching: define totals/two‑way/three‑way matching with variance icons and tolerance thresholds; block posting outside tolerance. * Payment proposals: select by due date or cash‑discount date; schedule and review prior to posting. * Cash discounts: configure discount codes/series, tax‑inclusive calculation, and under/over‑payment handling. Deliverables * AP Policy Handbook (version‑controlled) and Approval/Signing Limit Matrix; Supplier Invoicing Guide; Payment Methods Playbook; Prepayment & POE Checklist; Matching & Tolerance Matrix; KPIs dashboard (Power BI).

processes.title: Defining payment policies in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: Defining payment policies in Dynamics 365 Finance encompasses setting rules for how and when supplier payments are processed. This includes establishing payment terms (e.g., net 30), payment methods (ACH, check, wire), approval requirements, batch processing schedules, and compliance with regulatory and audit controls. The system enables automated payment runs, positive pay file generation, segregation of duties, and integration with banking platforms. Payment policies also cover exception handling for failed payments, manual payments, and recurring payments. The objective is to ensure timely, accurate, and secure disbursement of funds, minimize risk, and maintain auditability.

processes.title: Define cash discounting policies in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: Defining cash discounting policies in Dynamics 365 Finance involves configuring rules that incentivize early payment to suppliers, such as offering discounts for payments made within a specified period (e.g., 2% 10, net 30). The system allows for automated calculation and application of discounts based on invoice terms, tracks eligibility, and ensures accurate posting of discounts taken. Policies can be tailored per vendor or vendor group, and reporting tools provide visibility into discount utilization and missed opportunities. The aim is to optimize working capital, reduce costs, and strengthen supplier relationships.

processes.title: Develop spend strategy
processes.description: Develop spend strategy aligns procurement budgets to business goals, enforces budget control and signing limits, and governs in‑year budget transfers so sourcing and purchasing decisions stay compliant, timely, and cost‑effective. Scope and objectives This process defines how procurement dollars are planned, approved, and steered across categories, business units, and regions. It codifies the rules for budget authoring and phasing, budget control checks during requisition and purchase order creation, monetary approval thresholds (signing limits), and the mechanics for budget transfers and amendments. Outcomes include predictable spend, higher budget adherence, fewer last‑minute waivers, and faster approvals without sacrificing control. Core policy levers Budget ownership and structure: Define who owns category and cost‑center budgets; align to fiscal calendar, entities, and dimensions (business unit, region, category). Spend guardrails: Set signing limits by role, risk, and category; require competitive sourcing or RFQ above thresholds; define change‑order time fences. Control mode: Choose hard‑stop (block over‑budget) vs. soft‑warning (allow with justification) with consistent exception handling and audit. Transfers and amendments: Permit controlled in‑year moves across cost centers/categories, with pre‑set caps, justification, and approvals. Cash discounting and payment timing: Encourage early‑pay where economics are favorable and within cash/working‑capital targets. Diversity and sustainability aims: Reserve portions of category budgets or set targets that influence award decisions without breaching policy. Budgeting model (planning and phasing) Start with a top‑down target by category and business unit, refine bottom‑up with forecast demand (projects, run‑rate, seasonality), and phase monthly or quarterly. Map contract commitments and blanket POs to budgets, and separate controllable OpEx vs. pass‑throughs. Maintain a controlled “contingency” slice for urgent/unplanned demand. Budget control at point of spend Enable budget checks at requisition, purchase order confirmation, and change order. Controls should evaluate the correct accounting dimensions, recognize pre‑encumbrance/encumbrance where used, and consider open commitments. Define tolerances (for price variances, freight, taxes) and what triggers a re‑approval vs. warning. For centrally negotiated contracts, reserve capacity to reduce approval churn. Signing limits and approvals Publish a single signing‑limit matrix that considers amount, risk (e.g., non‑standard terms), and category. Drive approvals from category and monetary thresholds, not individual preferences. Require dual approval for high‑risk items (e.g., prepayments, new vendor, non‑PO spend). Enforce Segregation of Duties so requesters cannot approve their own spend or vendor master/bank changes. Budget transfers and in‑year adjustments Allow controlled transfers between cost centers/categories with: Clear reasons (demand shift, price change, project acceleration). Caps (e.g., ≤10% of original budget without CFO OK). Traceable journal entries, effective dates, and audit trails. A quarterly rebasing cadence to avoid constant micro‑moves. Emergency top‑ups should be routed via a short, documented approval path with post‑facto review. Change‑order and variance governance Define which changes (quantity, price, schedule) require re‑approval and which can be auto‑accepted within tolerances. Log root causes (scope change, supplier lead time, FX) to continuously improve planning and supplier performance. Data model and analytics Standardize dimensions for budget, commitment, and actuals (entity, BU, cost center, category, supplier). Provide spend dashboards for: budget vs. actuals vs. commitments, forecast‑to‑complete, contract utilization, early‑pay savings, and approval lead times. Track exceptions (over‑budget, rejections, waivers) and drill to transaction. High - level process Define strategy and targets: Set fiscal targets by category/BU, phasing, reserve and contingency rules, and exception policy. Allocate and publish budgets: Distribute to owners and load approved amounts with dimensions and phasing. Configure controls and limits: Turn on budget control points, tolerances, signing limits, and workflows. Execute with control: Run requisitions/POs against budgets; apply sourcing thresholds; use contracts/agreements to preserve rates and capacity. Monitor performance: Review budget burn, commitments, and variances; surface at‑risk lines and approval bottlenecks. Manage changes: Process budget transfers and amendments; enforce change‑order re‑approvals; document rationale. Optimize for value: Capture early‑pay discounts, rebalance categories, and shift spend to preferred/diverse suppliers within policy. Review and improve: Quarterly retrospective on policy hits, cycle time, and savings; adjust limits, tolerances, and targets. Roles and responsibilities Chief Procurement Officer: Owns policy, targets, and exception governance; approves large transfers and high‑risk waivers. Category Manager: Builds category budgets, monitors burn and savings, drives rebalancing and supplier mix. Finance Controller/FP&A: Sets fiscal guardrails, approves budget journals/transfers, ensures accounting integrity and audit trails. Procurement Operations: Configures controls, runs approval workflows, and maintains signing‑limit matrices. Budget Owners (BU/Cost Center): Plan bottom‑up needs, approve local spend within limits, request in‑year transfers. Treasury/AP: Aligns payment timing and cash discount policies with working‑capital goals. Dynamics 365 configuration pointers Budgeting and Budget Control: Define budget models, codes, cycles, and budget control rules at the correct dimension set; enable checks at requisition/PO. Procurement policies: Enforce catalog/category access, RFQ thresholds, and re‑approval rules on PO changes. Signing limits and workflows: Implement monetary thresholds and conditional logic (category, risk, prepayment) for requisitions, agreements, POs, and change orders. Budget transfers: Use budget register entries and transfer journals with workflow, attachments, and effective dates. Analytics: Publish Power BI reports for budget vs. actuals vs. commitments, approval SLA, and exception management. Operational controls and KPIs Controls: Hard/soft budget checks at PR/PO, dual approval for high‑risk, SoD on vendor/bank updates, documented budget‑transfer journals, quarterly policy review. KPIs: Budget adherence %, commitment coverage %, approval cycle time, waiver rate, % spend under contract, early‑pay savings realized, rework due to change‑order rejections, exception rate (over‑budget attempts), share to preferred/diverse suppliers within target. Deliverables Spend Strategy Playbook (targets, phasing, sourcing thresholds). Signing‑Limit Matrix and Approval Routes. Budget Control and Tolerance Settings (by category/entity). Budget Transfer Policy and Journal Templates. Quarterly Spend Review Pack (variance bridges, actions, owners, due dates).

processes.title: Define signing limits with Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: The "Define signing limits" scenario in Dynamics 365 Finance allows organizations to establish approval hierarchies and monetary thresholds for procurement transactions. Signing limits are configured based on roles, departments, or individual users, ensuring that purchase requisitions, purchase orders, and budget transfers are routed to the appropriate approvers according to company policy. The system enforces these limits automatically, preventing unauthorized commitments and supporting audit requirements. Approval workflows can be tailored to reflect complex organizational structures, with escalation paths for exceptions and comprehensive logging of approval actions for compliance and reporting.

processes.title: Configure budget control for procurement in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: The "Configure budget control for procurement" scenario in Dynamics 365 Finance provides organizations with tools to enforce budgetary discipline throughout the procurement lifecycle. Budget control parameters can be set at various levels—company, department, project, or cost center—and integrated with purchase requisitions, purchase orders, and invoices. The system automatically checks available budgets before allowing commitments, issues warnings or blocks transactions that exceed limits, and supports flexible rules for exceptions. processes.title: Analyze sourcing market
processes.description: Analyze sourcing market builds a repeatable market‑intelligence cadence to understand category dynamics, supplier landscape, and cost/risk drivers so you can choose the right sourcing strategy, timing, and partners. It connects internal demand and spend signals with external market data to inform RFx approach, negotiation levers, contract terms, and risk posture. Scope and objectives Establish a disciplined view of the external market for each category, quantify price/capacity trends and competitive intensity, identify qualified and diverse suppliers, and translate insights into sourcing waves, award strategies, and guardrails for negotiations. Outcomes include better timing to market, improved price/term performance, risk‑adjusted supplier portfolios, and increased award share to diverse and sustainable suppliers. What to analyze Market structure and capacity: supplier count/size, regional footprint, utilization, consolidation/M&A, entry barriers, alternate materials or make‑vs‑buy options. Cost drivers and indices: commodities, labor, energy, logistics, FX, tariffs/duties; build should‑cost and index‑linked pricing constructs. Competitive benchmarks: price corridors, service SLAs, lead times, warranty/after‑sales norms, rebate practices. Risk signals: financial health, concentration, geo‑political exposure, ESG and regulatory compliance, cyber posture, supply chain resilience. Diversity and sustainability: certified diverse suppliers, local/regional options, emissions and packaging standards, ethical sourcing. Internal demand/spend: specification rationalization, aggregation opportunities, incumbent performance, quality/NCR history, total cost‑to‑serve. High‑level process Baseline demand and spend: consolidate 12–24 months of demand forecasts, specs, and contract expirations; segment by category, region, and criticality. Map supplier landscape: identify incumbents, challengers, and new entrants; capture diversity and sustainability credentials; assess capacity and geographic coverage. Quantify cost drivers: align categories to external indices and FX; produce should‑cost models with scenario bands (base/optimistic/pessimistic). Assess risk and compliance: screen sanctions/SSPA/privacy, financial health, ESG attestations; rate suppliers and regions; define red‑flag thresholds. Build the sourcing thesis: decide RFx vs. direct award, single vs. multi‑source, global vs. regional splits; set wave plan and award heuristics (price/quality/risk/ESG weights). Define negotiation levers: index‑linked clauses, volume tiers, service credits, rebates, VMI/consignment, lead‑time commitments, dual‑sourcing safeguards. Prepare the market: supplier briefings and data rooms via the collaboration portal; finalize RFx questionnaires and scoring; publish calendar and rules. Execute RFx and analyze: run sealed bids/rounds; normalize price and non‑price terms against should‑cost; run sensitivity and multi‑objective scoring; produce award recommendation. Close loop and monitor: codify index/FX adjustment rules, service KPIs, and business‑event alerts in contracts; schedule quarterly market refresh and supplier QBRs. Roles and responsibilities Category Manager: owns thesis, wave plan, RFx content, and award recommendations. Sourcing Analyst: builds spend cuts, market models, should‑costs, and KPI dashboards. Risk/Compliance: runs sanctions/SSPA/privacy/ESG checks; approves exceptions. Finance/FP&A: validates index/FX mechanics and TCO; aligns to budgets and cash targets. Sustainability & Diversity: curates certified suppliers and tracks award/spend attainment. Legal/Contracts: authors indexation, SLA, and risk‑transfer clauses; ensures auditability. Dynamics 365 and Microsoft support Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management: procurement categories, RFQ management, trade agreements, vendor performance, rebate management, vendor consigned inventory, change management and approvals. Supplier collaboration portal: supplier onboarding, profile updates, certifications, document exchange, bid responses. Finance: AP terms alignment (cash discounts, payment methods), positive pay, centralized payments, rebate settlement. Microsoft Fabric/Power BI: category spend cubes, price/index trackers, supplier scorecards, QBR packs, and variance bridges. Copilot/Agents: narrative market summaries, anomaly detection on bid responses, next‑best negotiation levers, auto‑drafted RFx/Q&A and award memos. Operational controls Policy alignment: competitive bidding thresholds, AVL enforcement, RFx fairness rules, confidentiality, and SoD (RFx author vs. approver vs. awarder). Data governance: versioned RFx, sealed bids, audit trails, index sources and update cadence, evidence for diversity certifications. Risk gates: mandatory checks for sanctions/ESG/privacy; escalation paths for high‑risk awards; dual‑sourcing for critical items. Contractization: index‑linked pricing clauses, service credits, exit/transition terms, step‑in rights, and business‑event alerts (late ASN, OTIF breaches). KPIs and signals to track Savings vs. should‑cost and vs. prior period; index‑adjusted price variance. Award share to diverse and sustainable suppliers; number of certified diverse suppliers invited/responding/awarded. Supplier risk score trend; dual‑source coverage for critical SKUs; regional exposure. RFx cycle time; supplier participation and compliance rates; bid normalization deltas. Contract leakage: off‑contract spend, price/term deviations, change‑order incidence. Service KPIs: OTIF, lead‑time adherence, quality/NCR rate, corrective action closure. Deliverables Category market brief and should‑cost workbook with index mapping and scenarios. Wave plan and negotiation playbook per category. RFx package (questionnaire, scoring model, data room contents). Award recommendation, TCO analysis, and risk register with mitigations. Contract clause library for indexation, SLAs, rebates, and sustainability. Quarterly market update pack and supplier QBR deck. Implementation tips Start with top 5 spend categories and near‑term expirations. Normalize specs to expand competition. Tie payment terms and early‑pay discounts to treasury targets. Use index bands rather than fixed prices for volatile inputs. Blend global and regional awards to hedge geopolitics and logistics. Bake supplier‑led innovation and sustainability metrics into SLAs—and pay for performance.

processes.title: Analyze supplier performance in the Supply risk assessment with Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
processes.description: The "Analyze supplier performance in the Supply risk assessment" scenario within Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management empowers organizations to proactively monitor and assess supplier reliability, delivery performance, and risk exposure. The scenario utilizes real-time supply chain data, including delivery timelines, quality metrics, and incident reports, to generate comprehensive risk profiles for each supplier. Advanced analytics and dashboards provide visibility into potential supply disruptions, compliance issues, and strategic vulnerabilities. The system supports automated alerts for high-risk suppliers, facilitates collaborative risk mitigation planning, and enables procurement teams to adjust sourcing strategies based on dynamic risk assessments. This scenario is designed to enhance supply chain resilience and ensure continuity of operations through data-driven supplier management.

processes.title: Manage supplier relationships
processes.description: This article explains how to use the manage vendor relationships business process in Dynamics 365 Commerce, Finance, Project Operations, and Supply Chain Management. This process is part of the procure to pay end-to-end process. It helps you find, select, and evaluate vendors for your business needs. The manage vendor relationships business process area is an essential part of the procure to pay process in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Dynamics 365 includes a comprehensive set of capabilities to help you streamline vendor management. You can use it to: Search for potential vendors based on product type, location, price, and other criteria. Approve qualified vendors and create vendor records with all the relevant information. Update vendor records as needed, such as changing bank accounts or payment terms. Monitor vendor performance using various metrics, such as delivery time, quality, and compliance. Collaborate with vendors through a centralized platform that shows purchase orders, invoices, and consignment stock. The manage vendor relationships business process area helps you optimize your supply chain operations and achieve better business outcomes. You should implement it at the start of your Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management implementation. It's a foundational process for any organization.

processes.title: Discover suppliers
processes.description: Develop supplier segments organizes the vendor base into meaningful groups so procurement can target sourcing strategies, enforce policies, track supplier diversity, and optimize buying outcomes across categories, regions, and business units. This process supports both portal-driven segmentation (via supplier collaboration) and manual maintenance in the ERP, and it explicitly includes supplier diversity attributes and purchasing demographics. Scope and outcomes The process defines the segmentation framework, enriches suppliers with the attributes that place them into segments, and keeps those segments current as suppliers onboard, update certifications, or performance shifts. Outcomes include clear segment definitions (e.g., strategic vs. transactional), validated diversity classifications, visibility into purchasing demographics (who buys from whom, where, and for what), and segment-specific playbooks for sourcing, risk, and performance management. Segmentation model (what to capture) Business identity: legal entity, parent/child relationships, tax IDs, NAICS/industry, geography. Commercial markers: category fit, price lists/trade agreements, contract status, capacity/lead times, delivery lanes. Risk and compliance: sanctions/KYC status, insurance, sustainability/ESG attestations, cybersecurity posture. Performance: on‑time delivery, quality metrics, responsiveness, dispute rate, claim history. Diversity: minority‑owned, women‑owned, veteran‑owned, disability‑owned, LGBTQ+‑owned, small/disadvantaged business, indigenous, local/regional designations; certification bodies; effective/expiry dates. Purchasing demographics: spend by business unit/region/cost center, category mix, order frequency, average PO value, tail vs. strategic spend share. Data sources (how it gets populated) Supplier collaboration portal self‑service forms for profile, certifications, banking, sustainability and diversity disclosures, with evidence uploads and dates. Manual entry in system for vendor groups, classifications, category assignments, and policy flags when portal is not in scope. Controlled imports (CSV/cXML/API) from supplier registries (e.g., diversity certifiers), CLM systems, and performance data from receiving/quality modules. Operating model Portal‑driven segmentation: suppliers submit/maintain profile and certifications; workflows validate and place suppliers into segments automatically based on rules. Manual in‑system segmentation: procurement analysts assign vendor groups, risk scores, diversity flags, and category memberships directly in ERP when collaboration is unavailable or during transition. Hybrid: start manual to establish baseline, then transition segments to portal upkeep; keep critical attributes under workflow (e.g., bank changes, diversity certification). High‑level process Define segment taxonomy and rules Set the canonical list of segments (e.g., strategic, preferred, qualified, tail), diversity attributes, and risk tiers; publish the decision rules and data dictionary. Configure master data and security Create vendor groups/classes, category associations, mandatory attributes, and approval workflows. Set role‑based access for who can view/change sensitive fields. Enable the supplier collaboration portal Publish onboarding questionnaires, required documents, and self‑service profile pages for diversity, sustainability, and banking; map each field to ERP attributes. Collect and validate data Intake portal submissions and imports; validate certifications (issuer, number, effective/expiry), run basic KYC/sanctions checks, and flag missing or expired evidence. Apply segmentation rules Assign segment, risk tier, and diversity status based on rules (e.g., spend thresholds, category fit, performance, certifications). Record effective dates and rationale. Enrich with purchasing demographics Link historic and rolling spend by BU/region/category to the supplier record; compute purchase frequency, order size, and tail‑spend indicators to refine segment placement. Approve and publish segments Route changes through workflow for procurement/category manager approval; publish segments to sourcing, requisitioning policies, and supplier performance dashboards. Govern usage in downstream processes Bind segments to policies (e.g., RFQ routing to “preferred,” auto‑blocks for “not qualified,” diversity‑spend targets in analytics, guided buying recommendations). Monitor and refresh Schedule reviews for expiring certifications, material performance shifts, M&A events; automatically notify suppliers via portal to update expiring documents. Improve the model Review segment drift vs. outcomes (savings, risk incidents, diversity‑spend attainment); refine rules and thresholds; retire unused attributes. Roles and responsibilities Procurement/category manager: owns taxonomy, thresholds, and approvals; resolves exceptions. Supplier onboarding/operations: validates submissions, runs checks, and manages workflows. Diversity & inclusion lead (or ESG): defines accepted certification bodies and target reporting. Risk/compliance: maintains KYC/sanctions rules, approves sensitive changes. Finance/AP: verifies banking and tax data; ensures SoD and auditability. Business stakeholders: supply purchasing demographics and feedback on supplier fit. Dynamics 365 support Vendor information management and vendor groups/classifications for segments, risk, and policies. Supplier collaboration portal for self‑service profile maintenance, confirmations, and document upload. Purchasing policies that reference vendor groups/segments to allow/deny categories or enforce RFQs. Trade agreements and approved vendor list to bind segments to price/contract usage. Analytics via Power BI/Microsoft Fabric to report diversity spend, segment performance, tail spend, and purchasing demographics. Supplier diversity and purchasing demographics (practical guidance) Diversity capture: model diversity as structured fields with certification authority, certificate ID, effective/expiry, and attach artifacts; differentiate self‑attested vs. certified. Targets and tracking: define percentage goals (e.g., percent of addressable spend to certified diverse suppliers) by category and region; monitor progress monthly. Purchasing demographics: publish a quarterly heatmap showing who buys from which segments by business unit and location; use it to rebalance work to diverse/preferred suppliers without increasing risk. Guardrails: enforce evidence-on-file rules for diversity claims and auto‑expire designations upon certificate expiry; route reinstatement through validation workflow. Operational controls and KPIs Controls: maker‑checker for profile changes; workflow approvals for risk/diversity flags; automated reminders for expiring certifications; audit trails for attribute changes. KPIs: percent of spend through preferred/strategic segments; diverse‑supplier spend attainment; number of active diverse suppliers by category/region; average time to validate new supplier; share of tail spend; policy violations avoided; data completeness score for vendor profiles. Deliverables Segmentation taxonomy and data dictionary. Configured vendor groups/classifications and workflows. Onboarding questionnaires and document lists (portal). Diversity certification playbook and accepted issuers list. Dashboards: diversity spend, purchasing demographics, segment performance.

processes.description: Register as vendor in the Vendor portal. Setup a vendor record to use vendor portal. To complete a vendor request, a vendor contact person must complete the prospective vendor registration wizard. In the Vendor request configurations form, you can create profiles that specify required fields and visible fields in the prospective vendor registration wizard. The vendor registration wizard will start out by asking the prospective vendor user which country/region the vendor is doing business in. This information determines the applicable configuration. If no specific configuration is defined for a country/region, a default configuration will be used. Prospective vendor registration request list page – Based on the information that is provided in the prospective vendor registration request, a procurement professional decides whether the vendor should be onboarded. The procurement professional views the incoming request on the Prospective vendor registration requests list page.

processes.title: Onboard new suppliers
processes.description: This process governs the onboarding of new suppliers following successful application approval. It ensures vendors are properly qualified, set up in the system, and ready for transactional engagement. It includes account creation, contact and banking details setup, vendor demographic enrichment, legal entity replication, and qualification workflows. Scope and Outcomes Converts approved applications into vendor accounts Captures and validates supplier contact and banking details Copies vendor profiles across legal entities Maintains and updates vendor demographics Qualifies suppliers for sourcing and purchasing Outcomes include active vendor records, validated banking and tax data, enriched demographics, and qualified sourcing-ready suppliers Onboarding Model Business Identity Legal name, registration details, tax IDs, NAICS codes, geography, parent/child relationships Contact Information Primary contacts, email, phone, address, role-based access Banking Details Bank name, account number, routing code, currency, country, verification status Demographics Industry, category fit, delivery lanes, capacity, lead times Compliance Insurance, ESG attestations, cybersecurity posture, sanctions/KYC status Certifications Diversity, quality, environmental credentials, effective/expiry dates Performance History If applicable, includes legacy data on delivery, quality, responsiveness Legal Entity Replication Copy vendor records to other legal entities with mapped attributes and controls Data Sources Supplier collaboration portal: onboarding forms, document uploads, certifications Manual entry: ERP-based vendor setup for non-portal suppliers Controlled imports: CSV, cXML, API from registries, certifiers, CLM systems Performance data: receiving, quality, and finance modules Operating Model Portal-driven onboarding: suppliers submit profiles, documents, certifications Manual onboarding: procurement teams create vendor records directly in ERP Hybrid: initial manual setup followed by portal-based updates and maintenance High-Level Process Approve Application Validate supplier application and convert to vendor record Create Vendor Account Generate vendor ID, assign vendor group, set up legal entity associations Capture Contact and Banking Details Enter and verify contact info, banking data, tax details Enrich Vendor Profile Add demographics, certifications, compliance attributes Replicate Across Legal Entities Copy vendor data to relevant entities with mapped fields and controls Qualify Vendor Assign category memberships, risk scores, diversity flags Publish Vendor Record Make vendor available for sourcing, RFQs, purchasing Monitor and Maintain Schedule reviews for expiring certifications, update profiles, notify suppliers Roles and Responsibilities Procurement/category manager: owns onboarding criteria, approvals, vendor group assignments Supplier onboarding operations: validates submissions, manages workflows Risk/compliance: maintains KYC/sanctions rules, approves sensitive changes Diversity & inclusion lead: defines certification bodies, reporting targets Finance/AP: verifies banking and tax data, ensures SoD and auditability Business stakeholders: provide feedback on supplier fit and purchasing needs Dynamics 365 Support Vendor information management: vendor groups, classifications, segments Supplier collaboration portal: self-service onboarding, document uploads Workflow automation: approvals, validations, notifications Purchasing policies: enforce sourcing rules, RFQ eligibility Analytics: dashboards for onboarding throughput, diversity attainment, vendor performance Deliverables Configured vendor groups, classifications, workflows Onboarding questionnaires, document lists Diversity certification playbook, accepted issuers list Dashboards: onboarding metrics, diversity spend, vendor performance

processes.title: Copy a vendor to another legal entity in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
processes.description: Copy a vendor to another legal entity where applicable across companies. If a vendor is registered for only one legal entity in your organization, and other legal entities must register the same vendor, you can use the Add vendor to another legal entity page to configure the vendor to do business with another legal entity. You must select a vendor group, currency, and hold status for the vendor in the selected legal entity. If multiple legal entities in your organization do business with the same vendor, and each legal entity maintains a separate vendor account for that vendor, you can merge the party IDs for the vendor accounts. In this way, information such as the address and the number of employees can be shared, so that you must update it in only one place.

processes.title: Maintain vendors in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
processes.description: Manually create a vendor record. When you create a vendor account, you enter information about the vendor. This information is used to automatically enter data in documents and to track activity that involves the vendor. For example, you can configure the following information for a vendor: Assign a vendor group. Every vendor must be assigned to a vendor group. The vendors in a vendor group have parameters that they share. For example, they might have the same terms of payment. Configure the vendor for catalog import. Vendors can provide a file that contains the catalog of their items and services. This file can be uploaded so that your workers can order from the vendor. Assign the vendor to procurement categories. Allow an existing vendor to do business with another legal entity in your organization. Put a vendor on hold for specific types of transactions. Set up banking information for the vendor, so that you can send payments electronically. Set up tax, delivery, invoice, and payment information for the vendor. By default, these settings are copied to new documents that you create for the vendor. Set up default financial dimensions that are used to automatically post transactions with the vendor to financial accounts. To speed up the process of creating vendor accounts, you can create templates. To create a template, on the Vendor page, on the Action Pane, select Options > Record info. Then select Company accounts template. Company account templates are shared with other users. You can also create a user template for your own use. You can't delete a vendor that is associated with other records, such as contacts or products

Covers quality, delivery, pricing, compliance, and service metrics. Supports continuous improvement, risk mitigation, and sourcing decisions. Scope & Outcomes Monitors supplier effectiveness post-onboarding through structured reviews and analytics. Identifies trends, anomalies, and non-conformances. Outcomes include performance dashboards, supplier scorecards, risk flags, and improvement plans. Performance Evaluation Model Delivery Metrics % In Full, On Time (IFOT) Delivery lead time variance Missed delivery windows Quality Metrics Failed quality inspections Non-conformance reports Warranty claims / service issues Pricing & Commercial Trends Price variance analysis Unexpected cost increases Contract compliance Forecast vs Actuals Order forecast accuracy Volume adherence Stakeholder Feedback Internal surveys (procurement, operations) External surveys (supplier self-assessment) Risk & Compliance Recall incidents Sanctions / KYC status changes Insurance / ESG / cybersecurity posture Service & Support Responsiveness Dispute resolution rate Claim history Data Sources ERP receiving and quality modules Supplier collaboration portal (self-assessments, service logs) CLM systems (contract compliance) Manual entry (non-conformance reports, survey results) Controlled imports (CSV, cXML, API from performance systems) Operating Model Portal-driven performance updates and surveys ERP-based transactional data capture Hybrid model for manual and automated inputs High-Level Process Define KPIs & Thresholds Set performance metrics by category, region, business unit Configure Data Capture Enable ERP modules, portal forms, survey templates Collect Performance Data Intake from transactions, surveys, supplier inputs Analyze & Score Compute KPIs, identify anomalies, flag risks Review & Validate Procurement reviews scorecards, confirms issues Publish Dashboards Share performance insights with sourcing teams Trigger Actions Initiate improvement plans, pause sourcing, escalate issues Monitor & Refresh Schedule reviews, notify suppliers, update metrics Roles & Responsibilities Procurement manager: owns KPI definitions, reviews performance, triggers actions Supplier onboarding / operations: manages portal inputs, validates data Risk / compliance: monitors sanctions, KYC, ESG, cybersecurity Diversity & inclusion: tracks diversity performance metrics Finance / AP: validates pricing, payment terms, cost anomalies Business stakeholders: provide feedback on supplier fit and service Dynamics 365 Support Vendor information management: stores performance attributes Supplier collaboration portal: collects surveys, service logs Workflow automation: routes reviews, flags issues Purchasing policies: enforce sourcing restrictions based on performance Analytics (Power BI / Microsoft Fabric): visualize KPIs, trends, risk indicators Deliverables Supplier scorecards Performance dashboards Non-conformance logs Survey results Recall reports Improvement plans Risk flags and escalation records

processes.title: Manage contracts in Microsoft Syntex
processes.description: Manages the lifecycle of supplier contracts from creation to renewal and termination. Supports contract authoring, review, approval, storage, and compliance tracking. Integrates Microsoft Syntex for intelligent document processing and Dynamics 365 SCM for purchase agreement workflows. Scope & Outcomes Covers contract initiation, negotiation, execution, amendment, and renewal. Outcomes include: * Digitally stored, searchable contracts * Validated purchase agreements * Automated compliance checks * Visibility into contract terms, obligations, and expiration timelines Contract Management Model Contract Types * Master Service Agreements (MSA) * Statements of Work (SOW) * Purchase Agreements * Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDA) Contract Attributes * Supplier name, legal entity, tax ID * Contract value, term, renewal clauses * Category alignment, delivery terms * Risk clauses, indemnity, liability limits * Diversity and ESG commitments Microsoft Syntex Capabilities * AI-powered document classification and metadata extraction * Content understanding and compliance tagging * Integration with SharePoint and Teams for collaboration * Pay-as-you-go licensing with Azure Cost Management Dynamics 365 SCM Capabilities * Purchase agreement workflows for supplier contracts * Integration with third-party CLM systems like Icertis * Support for contract intelligence, clause libraries, and approval routing * Contract status tracking and supplier performance linkage Data Sources * Supplier collaboration portal: contract uploads, metadata entry * ERP: contract records, purchase agreement linkage * Syntex: document processing, classification, compliance tagging * CLM systems: contract lifecycle workflows, amendments * Manual entry: ad hoc contracts, legacy agreements Operating Model * Portal-driven: suppliers submit contracts, metadata, amendments * Syntex automation: extract terms, classify documents, tag compliance * ERP integration: bind contracts to supplier records, enforce purchasing policies * Hybrid: manual review and automated processing for amendments and renewals High-Level Process 1. Initiate Contract Define contract type, scope, and required clauses 2. Author & Review Draft using templates, route for procurement and legal review 3. Approve & Sign Use SAFE limits and authorized signatories per Microsoft policy 4. Store & Tag Upload to SharePoint via Syntex, apply metadata and compliance tags 5. Link to ERP Bind contract to supplier record and purchase agreement in Dynamics 365 SCM 6. Monitor & Renew Track expiration, renewal dates, compliance status 7. Amend & Extend Submit PO amendment requests via MyOrder portal 8. Audit & Report Generate dashboards for contract status, supplier performance, compliance Roles & Responsibilities * Procurement: owns contract templates, reviews, approvals * Legal (CELA): reviews legal terms, amendments * Supplier Onboarding: validates submissions, manages workflows * Finance: verifies payment terms, auditability * Compliance: monitors risk clauses, ESG, diversity commitments Dynamics 365 Support * Vendor Information Management: stores contract metadata * Purchase Agreements: enforce sourcing rules, pricing terms * CLM Integration: supports Icertis and other providers * Syntex: automates document processing, tagging, compliance Deliverables * Contract templates and clause libraries * Configured workflows for review, approval, storage * Syntex classification models and metadata schema * Purchase agreement records in Dynamics 365 SCM * Dashboards for contract status, compliance, supplier performance

processes.title: Create a purchase agreement in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
processes.description: Create a purchase agreement in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management. Sometimes referred to "blanket agreements", purchase agreements can apply to a specific quantity of a product, a specific currency amount of a product, or a specific currency amount of the products in a procurement category. The prices and discounts of the purchase agreement override the prices and discounts that are specified in any trade agreements that exist.

processes.title: Define default purchase prices in Dynamics 365 Business Central
processes.description: Define default purchase prices in Dynamics 365. Dynamics 365 "default purchase prices" refer to the pre-set price that automatically populates on a purchase order when creating a new line for an item. This is typically defined on the item master record within the "Released product" page allowing you to specify a base purchase price that will be used as the default unless overridden by a purchase trade agreement or manually on the purchase order itself.

processes.title: Manage accounts payable
processes.description: A vendor invoice is generated upon receiving products or services as per a purchase order. It consists of a header and item or service lines, marking the last step in the purchase process. Some invoices may not correspond to purchase orders, like ongoing service bills. There are various methods to enter vendor invoices, including, vendor invoice approval journal, vendor invoice journal for non-purchase order invoices, and using the vendor invoice pool for expense accrual. Additionally, you can create vendor invoices based on confirmed purchase orders using the Open vendor invoices and Pending vendor invoices pages. The vendor invoices business process area should be defined and incorporated into the overall implementation. This phase typically occurs at the beginning of a project's lifecycle and involves establishing project goals, defining project scope, and developing a detailed project plan. The setup and configuration of your products and base pricing along with the general procurement process should be in place before the vendor invoice process.

processes.title: Correct a payment in Dynamics 365 Finance
processes.description: The “Correct a payment” scenario in Dynamics 365 Finance enables organizations to efficiently manage and rectify supplier payment errors within the procure-to-pay lifecycle. This process typically involves identifying payment discrepancies—such as duplicate payments, incorrect amounts, or misapplied invoices—and executing corrective actions. These actions may include reversing payments, reissuing payments, updating payment records, and ensuring accurate reconciliation in both supplier accounts and the general ledger. The scenario leverages Dynamics 365 finance and operations apps’s robust audit trails, approval workflows, and compliance controls to maintain financial integrity and transparency. Corrections are tracked systematically, ensuring that all adjustments are visible to stakeholders and compliant with internal and external audit requirements. The process supports various payment methods (ACH, check, wire, etc.) and integrates with bank reconciliation and vendor management modules to ensure end-to-end accuracy.

processes.title: Process vendor rebates with Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
processes.description: Processing vendor rebates in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management enables organizations to systematically manage, track, and realize supplier incentives and rebate agreements. The solution allows procurement teams to define rebate agreements with vendors, specifying qualifying products, purchase thresholds, and rebate terms. As purchases are made, the system automatically accrues rebate amounts based on transactional data, providing visibility into expected rebate income and facilitating reconciliation with vendor statements. The process includes automated calculation of rebates, integration with accounts payable for settlement, and reporting capabilities to monitor rebate performance. This functionality supports compliance, auditability, and maximizes the value of supplier relationships by ensuring all eligible rebates are claimed and processed efficiently.

processes.title: Procure goods and services
processes.description: This process governs the operational execution of purchasing goods and services, including creation and management of purchase requisitions, purchase orders, blanket orders, planned purchases, and returns. It ensures that procurement activities align with approved budgets, sourcing strategies, and supplier contracts. The process supports consolidation of requisitions, automated PO generation, and integration with financial and inventory systems. Scope & Outcomes Initiates procurement through requisitions and planned purchases Converts approved requisitions into purchase orders or blanket orders Manages vendor-specific pricing, delivery terms, and order confirmations Supports returns and adjustments for non-conforming goods Consolidates requisitions across departments or cost centers Ensures compliance with budget limits and approval workflows Outcomes include accurate PO records, timely deliveries, validated returns, and optimized procurement cycles Key Components Purchase Requisitions : Internal requests for goods/services, routed through approval workflows. Can be consolidated across business units or cost centers. Purchase Orders (POs) : Formal orders issued to suppliers, generated manually or automatically from approved requisitions or planned purchases. Blanket Orders : Long-term agreements with suppliers for recurring purchases, supporting release schedules and quantity tracking. Planned Purchases : Forecast-driven procurement based on demand planning, linked to production or project schedules. Returns : Managed through return orders or credit memos for defective, excess, or incorrect goods. Requisition Consolidation : Combines multiple requests into a single PO to optimize supplier engagement and reduce administrative overhead. Technology Support Dynamics 365 SCM Purchase requisition and PO workflows Blanket order management Planned purchase integration with MRP and demand forecasting Return order processing and inventory adjustments Budget control and approval routing Dynamics 365 Business Central Simplified PO creation and vendor management Purchase invoice matching and payment processing Return handling and credit memo generation Integration with financial dimensions and cost centers Roles & Responsibilities Requesters : Initiate requisitions, provide specifications, confirm receipt Procurement Managers : Review requisitions, issue POs, manage supplier communication Finance/AP : Validate budget availability, process payments, manage returns Warehouse/Receiving : Confirm delivery, inspect goods, initiate returns Category Managers : Oversee blanket orders, planned purchases, and supplier performance Deliverables Approved purchase requisitions Issued purchase orders and blanket agreements Consolidated requisition reports Return order documentation Spend and delivery performance dashboards

processes.title: Raise purchase requisitions
processes.description: Initiates the procurement cycle by capturing internal demand for goods or services. Purchase requisitions (PRs) can be created manually, through punch-out catalogs, or integrated from external systems. Supports both item-based and category-based requisition lines, enabling flexible sourcing aligned with business needs. Scope & Outcomes Covers creation, submission, and approval of purchase requisitions. Supports manual entry, catalog-based selection, and automated integrations. Outcomes include approved requisitions ready for conversion to purchase orders, visibility into demand, and alignment with budget and sourcing policies. Requisition Types Item-based lines : Specific SKUs or inventory items with quantity, unit price, and delivery details. Category-based lines : Non-catalog goods or services grouped by procurement category, often used for indirect spend. Punch-out requisitions : Real-time integration with supplier catalogs for dynamic item selection and pricing. Integrated requisitions : Automatically generated from external systems (e.g., project management, maintenance, or planning tools). Entry Methods Manual creation via procurement workspace or employee self-service. Punch-out catalog selection with automatic line population. Import from external systems using APIs or batch uploads. Key Attributes Captured Requester details, cost center, business unit Item/category, quantity, unit price, delivery date Supplier (optional), justification, attachments Budget check, approval routing, policy flags Operating Model Portal-driven requisition entry for employees and procurement teams Workflow automation for approvals based on thresholds, roles, and policies Integration with budget control and financial dimensions Requisition consolidation for bulk purchasing or blanket orders Technology Support Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management : Requisition creation, approval workflows, budget validation, and PO conversion Dynamics 365 Business Central : Simplified requisition entry, approval routing, and vendor linkage Punch-out integration : Connects to supplier-hosted catalogs for real-time item selection Workflow automation : Routes requisitions for approval based on spend limits and category rules Roles & Responsibilities Requesters : Initiate requisitions, provide specifications, confirm receipt Procurement Managers : Review requisitions, validate sourcing strategy, approve or redirect Finance/AP : Validate budget availability, ensure auditability Category Managers : Oversee category-based requisitions, enforce preferred supplier usage Deliverables Approved purchase requisitions Consolidated requisition reports Budget compliance logs Requisition-to-PO conversion records

processes.title: Use the buyers push to create transfer orders from purchases in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management

processes.title: Create intercompany purchases in Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management
processes.description: Create purchase order from Intercompany trade You can create an intercompany purchase order for an intercompany vendor. This automatically creates an intercompany sales order at the intercompany vendor. When you create an intercompany sales order, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management creates a corresponding purchase order automatically. Similarly, creating an intercompany purchase order prompts the automatic creation of a corresponding intercompany sales order. This is true for two-legged orders (transactions between two related companies) and for most three-legged companies (when an intercompany transaction originates with a sales order for an external customer).

processes.title: Manage open purchases
processes.description: Manages post-issuance lifecycle of purchase orders (POs), including updates, cancellations, delivery adjustments, and follow-ups. Supports change management workflows for quantity, pricing, delivery dates, and cross-docking. Ensures procurement agility, supplier coordination, and compliance with approval policies. Scope & Outcomes Covers all modifications to open POs across procurement scenarios. Outcomes include: Accurate, up-to-date PO records Controlled change approvals Timely supplier communication Visibility into PO status and fulfillment Change Management Scenarios Quantity Adjustments : Increase or decrease ordered quantities based on demand or supplier constraints Pricing Updates : Reflect negotiated changes, discounts, or corrections Delivery Information : Modify delivery dates, locations, or methods (e.g., cross-docking) Partial or Full Cancellation : Cancel entire PO or specific lines due to budget changes, supplier issues, or sourcing shifts Follow-ups : Track PO status, confirm delivery, escalate delays Supported PO Types Standard POs Intercompany POs Drop shipment / direct delivery Project-based POs Blanket order releases Operating Model Portal-driven : Procurement teams and requesters initiate changes via workspace Workflow-enabled : Approval routing for sensitive changes (e.g., pricing, quantity) System-integrated : Updates reflected across linked systems (inventory, finance, project management) Supplier collaboration : Notifications and confirmations for PO changes Technology Support Dynamics 365 Supply Chain Management PO change tracking Delivery schedule updates Cross-docking configuration Workflow approvals Dynamics 365 Business Central PO editing Cancellation handling Invoice matching Field Service / Asset Management PO updates for service-linked parts and maintenance Workflow Automation Escalation routing, notifications, audit trails Roles & Responsibilities Procurement Managers : Initiate and approve PO changes, coordinate with suppliers Requesters : Request updates, confirm delivery Finance / AP : Validate pricing changes, ensure auditability Warehouse / Receiving : Confirm delivery, initiate returns or adjustments Project Managers / Field Technicians : Trigger updates for project or service-linked POs Deliverables Updated PO records with change history Cancellation logs and audit trails Delivery schedule reports Supplier communication records PO performance dashboard

processes.title: Issue blanket purchase orders
processes.description: Establishes long-term purchasing arrangements with suppliers for recurring goods or services. Blanket orders define pricing, quantities, and delivery schedules over a specified period, streamlining procurement and reducing administrative overhead. In F&O, these are managed as purchase agreements and can be linked to requisitions, purchase orders, and trade agreements. Scope & Outcomes Supports strategic sourcing by locking in terms with preferred suppliers. Enables automated PO creation against agreed terms, improves spend forecasting, and enforces compliance with negotiated pricing and delivery conditions. Outcomes include: Validated purchase agreements with supplier commitments Automated PO generation based on releases Spend tracking against agreement thresholds Reduced manual entry and improved procurement efficiency Types of Purchase Agreements Value Commitment : Specifies a total monetary value to be purchased over time. Quantity Commitment : Defines specific quantities of items to be procured. Product Category Commitment : Applies to a category of items rather than specific SKUs. Blanket Orders with Release Schedules : Used for recurring deliveries with predefined intervals or triggers. Operating Model Procurement teams create purchase agreements in F&O, linking them to vendor records and trade agreements. Agreements can be referenced in requisitions and POs, enabling automated enforcement of pricing and terms. Release orders are generated manually or automatically based on demand, forecasts, or consumption. Technology Support Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations : Manages purchase agreements, release orders, and trade agreement enforcement. Supplier Collaboration Portal : Enables suppliers to view agreement terms, confirm releases, and submit updates. Workflow Automation : Routes agreements for approval, monitors thresholds, and triggers alerts. Power BI : Provides dashboards for agreement utilization, supplier performance, and spend tracking. Roles & Responsibilities Procurement Managers : Define agreement terms, negotiate with suppliers, and monitor usage. Finance/AP : Validate pricing, ensure auditability, and manage payment terms. Category Managers : Oversee category-level agreements and supplier compliance. Requesters : Reference agreements in requisitions and confirm deliveries. Deliverables Executed purchase agreements with supplier terms Release order records linked to agreements Spend utilization reports and compliance dashboards Audit logs of agreement changes and approvals
